models.name: shopping_mall_order_sellers
models.description:
Seller-specific portion of a multi-seller order.

When a buyer's order contains items from multiple sellers, the order is split into sub-orders for each seller.
Each sub-order is represented by one record in this table, containing seller-specific information and totals.

Each seller processes and fulfills their portion of the order independently with their own shipping and tracking.
The parent order maintains the buyer's unified view while this table enables seller-specific fulfillment workflows.

This table is managed through the parent order and does not require independent buyer operations.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order this seller portion belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller fulfilling this portion of the order. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: sub_order_number
plainFields.description: Unique sub-order number for this seller portion. Format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN-S#.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status for this seller's portion. Same status values as parent order but tracked independently.

plainFields.name: subtotal
plainFields.description: Sum of all item line totals for this seller's items before shipping and taxes.

plainFields.name: shipping_cost
plainFields.description: Shipping cost for this seller's items based on selected shipping method.

plainFields.name: shipping_method
plainFields.description: Shipping method selected for this seller's items. Values: standard, express, next_day, economy, international.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Carrier tracking number provided by seller when order is shipped.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Shipping carrier name (UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL, etc.) for tracking and delivery.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller marked this sub-order as shipped and provided tracking.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when carrier confirmed delivery for this seller's shipment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller sub-order was created from the parent order.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this seller sub-order was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this seller sub-order.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_items
models.description:
Individual line items within an order representing purchased products.

Each record represents one product SKU variant purchased with specific quantity and pricing.
Order items capture product information as it existed at the time of purchase for historical accuracy.

Items reference the specific sale SKU variant purchased, preserving color, size, and option selections.
Pricing is captured at order time to maintain accurate records even if product prices change later.

This table is managed through the parent order and supports order fulfillment, invoicing, and buyer order history.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Parent order this item belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller sub-order this item is part of for multi-seller order management. {@link shopping_mall_order_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sale_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Product SKU variant that was purchased. {@link shopping_mall_sale_skus.id}.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Product name captured at time of purchase for historical accuracy.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: SKU code captured at time of purchase for reference.

plainFields.name: variant_attributes
plainFields.description: JSON string capturing selected variant attributes (color, size, options) at time of purchase.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Price per unit at the time of purchase, preserving historical pricing.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased for this line item.

plainFields.name: line_total
plainFields.description: Total price for this line item calculated as unit_price × quantity.

plainFields.name: discount_amount
plainFields.description: Discount amount applied to this specific line item from promotions or coupons.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item was created as part of order placement.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this order item record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this order item.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_status_histories
models.description:
Historical record of all order status transitions for complete audit trail.

Captures every status change throughout the order lifecycle including timestamps and the actor who triggered the change.
Provides transparency into order progression from placement through completion, cancellation, or refund.

Each record represents a single status transition with the previous status, new status, and optional change reason.
The actor type and actor ID identify whether the change was triggered by buyer, seller, admin, or system automation.

This snapshot table enables audit trail review, dispute resolution, and performance analytics on order processing speed.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order whose status changed. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller sub-order whose status changed, for tracking seller-specific fulfillment progress. {@link shopping_mall_order_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: Order status before this transition occurred.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: Order status after this transition occurred.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who triggered the status change. Values: buyer, seller, admin, system.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the actor who triggered the status change (buyer_id, seller_id, admin_id, or system identifier).

plainFields.name: change_reason
plainFields.description: Optional explanation or reason for the status change provided by the actor.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the actor when the status change occurred for security audit.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this status change occurred.

models.name: shopping_mall_order_cancellations
models.description:
Order cancellation requests and approvals tracking the cancellation workflow.

Records all cancellation attempts including buyer-initiated, seller-initiated, and admin-initiated cancellations.
Captures the cancellation reason, approval status, and resolution timeline for accountability.

Buyers can request cancellation before shipment, which may require seller or admin approval based on order status.
Sellers can cancel orders they cannot fulfill due to inventory or other issues.
Admins can cancel orders for fraud, policy violations, or dispute resolution.

This table supports independent cancellation workflow management with search and filtering capabilities for all actors.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order being cancelled. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller sub-order being cancelled for multi-seller order partial cancellations. {@link shopping_mall_order_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: requested_by_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who requested the cancellation if buyer-initiated. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

foreignFields.name: requested_by_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who requested the cancellation if seller-initiated. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: requested_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who requested the cancellation if admin-initiated. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: approved_by_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who approved the cancellation request if seller approval was required. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: approved_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who approved the cancellation request if admin approval was required. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: cancellation_reason
plainFields.description: Reason code for cancellation. Values: buyer_changed_mind, buyer_ordered_by_mistake, seller_out_of_stock, seller_cannot_deliver, seller_product_discontinued, seller_pricing_error, admin_fraud_detected, admin_policy_violation, payment_failed, other.

plainFields.name: cancellation_explanation
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation or notes about the cancellation reason provided by the requestor.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Current approval status of the cancellation request. Values: pending, auto_approved, seller_approved, admin_approved, denied, expired.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Amount refunded to buyer as a result of this cancellation.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation was requested.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation was approved.

plainFields.name: denied_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation request was denied.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the cancellation was fully processed and refund completed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this cancellation record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for this cancellation record.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Buyer refund requests for delivered orders requiring admin review and approval.

Records all refund requests submitted by buyers after receiving orders, capturing the reason, evidence, and resolution.
Each request initiates an admin review workflow where admins evaluate the claim and decide on full, partial, or no refund.

Refund requests can be submitted within the refund window (typically 7-30 days after delivery) for various reasons including defective products, incorrect items, or buyer remorse.
The system tracks the complete refund workflow from initial request through admin decision and payment processing.

Buyers need to independently search and track their refund requests, making this a primary entity with dedicated management UI.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order for which refund is requested. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller sub-order for which refund is requested, supporting partial refunds in multi-seller orders. {@link shopping_mall_order_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who submitted the refund request. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

foreignFields.name: reviewed_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who reviewed and decided on the refund request. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: refund_request_number
plainFields.description: Unique refund request number for tracking and reference. Format: REF-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN.

plainFields.name: refund_reason
plainFields.description: Reason category for the refund request. Values: defective_product, not_as_described, wrong_item, damaged_in_shipping, never_arrived, buyer_changed_mind, other.

plainFields.name: refund_explanation
plainFields.description: Detailed explanation provided by buyer describing the issue and reason for refund request.

plainFields.name: requested_amount
plainFields.description: Amount buyer is requesting to be refunded (may be full order amount or partial).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request. Values: requested, under_review, information_requested, approved, processing, completed, denied, cancelled.

plainFields.name: admin_decision
plainFields.description: Admin decision on the refund request. Values: approve_full, approve_partial, deny, escalate, pending.

plainFields.name: admin_decision_notes
plainFields.description: Admin notes explaining the decision rationale for transparency and record-keeping.

plainFields.name: approved_refund_amount
plainFields.description: Actual refund amount approved by admin, which may differ from requested amount for partial refunds.

plainFields.name: return_required
plainFields.description: Whether buyer must return the product to receive the refund.

plainFields.name: return_tracking_number
plainFields.description: Tracking number provided by buyer when returning the product.

plainFields.name: return_received_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller confirmed receipt of returned product.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the buyer submitted the refund request.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when admin reviewed the refund request.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund was approved.

plainFields.name: denied_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was denied.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund processing was completed and funds returned to buyer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund request record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_methods
models.description:
Buyer saved payment methods for checkout convenience.

Stores tokenized payment method information including credit cards, debit cards, and digital wallets that buyers save for future purchases.
Each payment method is securely tokenized through the payment provider to avoid storing sensitive card details directly.

Buyers can save multiple payment methods and designate one as their default for streamlined checkout.
Payment methods support soft deletion to maintain audit trails while allowing buyers to remove unused methods.

The system never stores full card numbers or CVV codes, only payment provider tokens and last four digits for identification.
Payment methods must be validated through the payment provider before being marked as verified and usable for transactions.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who owns this payment method. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

plainFields.name: payment_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method. Values: credit_card, debit_card, paypal, apple_pay, google_pay, bank_transfer.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: Payment provider name. Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree.

plainFields.name: provider_token
plainFields.description: Tokenized payment method identifier from payment provider. Secure token reference instead of storing sensitive card data.

plainFields.name: last_four_digits
plainFields.description: Last four digits of card number or account identifier for buyer recognition. Used for display purposes only.

plainFields.name: card_brand
plainFields.description: Card brand if payment type is card. Values: visa, mastercard, amex, discover. Null for non-card payment methods.

plainFields.name: expiry_month
plainFields.description: Card expiration month (1-12) if payment type is card. Used to warn buyers of expiring cards.

plainFields.name: expiry_year
plainFields.description: Card expiration year (four digits) if payment type is card. Used to validate card is not expired.

plainFields.name: billing_name
plainFields.description: Name on the payment method as provided by payment provider. Used for verification and display.

plainFields.name: billing_postal_code
plainFields.description: Billing postal code for address verification. Used for fraud prevention and payment authorization.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Whether this payment method is the buyer's default for checkout. Only one method can be default per buyer.

plainFields.name: is_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the payment method has been verified through the payment provider. Unverified methods cannot be used for transactions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment method was added to buyer's account.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment method information was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment method was soft-deleted by the buyer. Null for active payment methods.

models.name: shopping_mall_payment_transactions
models.description:
Payment transaction records for order purchases.

Records all payment processing attempts and outcomes for orders placed on the platform.
Each order payment goes through authorization, capture, and confirmation stages tracked through transaction status.

Payment transactions are immutable audit records maintaining complete financial history including amount, payment method, provider transaction ID, and processing timestamps.
Transactions support multiple states throughout the payment lifecycle from pending authorization through successful capture or failure.

The platform uses payment provider tokens to process payments securely without storing sensitive card data.
All transactions record the payment provider's response for reconciliation and dispute resolution.

Refund transactions are tracked separately in shopping_mall_refund_transactions table, not as modifications to original payment transactions.
This ensures clean audit trails and supports partial refunds without corrupting original payment records.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order this payment transaction is for. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who initiated the payment. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Payment method used for this transaction. {@link shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.

plainFields.name: transaction_type
plainFields.description: Type of transaction. Values: authorization, capture, void, refund. Authorization holds funds, capture completes payment.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Transaction amount in the order currency. Stored as decimal value for precise financial calculations.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for the transaction amount. Three-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD, EUR, GBP.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current transaction status. Values: pending, authorized, captured, failed, voided, refunded. Tracks payment lifecycle.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: Payment provider that processed this transaction. Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree.

plainFields.name: provider_transaction_id
plainFields.description: Unique transaction identifier from the payment provider. Used for reconciliation and dispute resolution with provider.

plainFields.name: provider_response
plainFields.description: Raw JSON response from payment provider. Stored for debugging, reconciliation, and compliance. Contains provider-specific transaction details.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for transaction failure if status is failed. Examples: insufficient_funds, card_declined, invalid_card, fraud_detected. Null for successful transactions.

plainFields.name: failure_code
plainFields.description: Provider-specific error code for failed transactions. Used for detailed error analysis and retry logic.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the payment was initiated. Used for fraud detection and security auditing.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser user agent string for the payment request. Used for fraud analysis and device fingerprinting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment transaction was initiated. Immutable audit timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_refund_transactions
models.description:
Refund payment processing records for approved refund requests.

Records actual refund payment processing that occurs after refund requests are approved by admins or sellers.
This table is distinct from shopping_mall_refund_requests which tracks buyer refund requests and approval workflow.

Each refund transaction represents a financial operation returning funds to the buyer through the payment provider.
Refund transactions reference both the original payment transaction being refunded and the refund request that authorized the refund.

Refunds can be full (entire order amount) or partial (percentage or specific amount based on refund reason).
The system tracks refund status through the payment provider lifecycle from initiation through completion or failure.

Refund transactions are immutable audit records that cannot be modified after creation.
All refund processing details including provider responses and timestamps are permanently logged for financial reconciliation and compliance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Refund request that authorized this refund transaction. {@link shopping_mall_refund_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Original payment transaction being refunded. {@link shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this refund. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer receiving the refund. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Amount being refunded to the buyer. May be partial or full order amount depending on refund approval decision.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for the refund amount. Three-letter ISO 4217 code matching original payment currency.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Refund processing status. Values: processing, completed, failed. Tracks refund lifecycle through payment provider.

plainFields.name: provider
plainFields.description: Payment provider processing the refund. Must match the original payment provider.

plainFields.name: provider_refund_id
plainFields.description: Unique refund transaction identifier from payment provider. Used for reconciliation and tracking refund status.

plainFields.name: provider_response
plainFields.description: Raw JSON response from payment provider for refund processing. Stored for debugging and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for refund failure if status is failed. Examples: insufficient_balance, account_closed, provider_error. Null for successful refunds.

plainFields.name: initiated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund transaction was initiated with the payment provider.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund was successfully completed and funds returned to buyer. Null if refund is still processing or failed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this refund transaction record was created. Immutable audit timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_seller_payouts
models.description:
Seller payout records for earnings settlement.

Tracks platform payouts to sellers for their completed sales after commission deduction.
Payouts aggregate earnings from multiple orders and are processed according to seller-configured payout schedules (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly).

Each payout record represents a single bank transfer or payment to the seller's verified account.
Payouts are held for 7 days after order delivery confirmation to protect against fraudulent transactions and allow time for buyer disputes.

The system calculates net payout amounts by summing order totals minus platform commissions for the payout period.
Payout status tracks the transfer lifecycle from pending through processing to completed or failed.

Sellers can view detailed payout history including which orders contributed to each payout and the commission breakdown.
All payout transactions are immutable audit records maintaining complete financial history for tax reporting and reconciliation.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller receiving this payout. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: payout_period_start
plainFields.description: Start date of the period covered by this payout. Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement.

plainFields.name: payout_period_end
plainFields.description: End date of the period covered by this payout. Inclusive boundary for orders included in settlement.

plainFields.name: gross_amount
plainFields.description: Total gross sales amount before commission deduction. Sum of all order totals in the payout period.

plainFields.name: commission_amount
plainFields.description: Total platform commission deducted from gross amount. Sum of all commission charges for included orders.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Total refund amount deducted from payout. Refunds processed during the period reduce seller payout.

plainFields.name: adjustment_amount
plainFields.description: Manual adjustments to payout amount. Can be positive (credits) or negative (charges). Examples: dispute resolutions, fee corrections.

plainFields.name: net_payout_amount
plainFields.description: Final payout amount transferred to seller. Calculated as gross_amount minus commission_amount minus refund_amount plus adjustment_amount.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for all amounts in this payout. Three-letter ISO 4217 code.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Payout processing status. Values: pending, processing, completed, failed. Tracks bank transfer lifecycle.

plainFields.name: bank_account_last_four
plainFields.description: Last four digits of seller's bank account receiving the payout. Used for seller verification and record-keeping.

plainFields.name: bank_name
plainFields.description: Name of the bank receiving the payout transfer. Captured for seller reference and audit purposes.

plainFields.name: transfer_reference
plainFields.description: Bank transfer reference number or transaction ID. Used to track the transfer in banking systems.

plainFields.name: failure_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for payout failure if status is failed. Examples: invalid_account, insufficient_funds, bank_rejected. Null for successful payouts.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Admin notes or explanations for adjustments and special circumstances. Used for documenting manual interventions.

plainFields.name: initiated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payout transfer was initiated with the banking system.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payout was successfully completed and funds transferred to seller. Null if still processing or failed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this payout record was created. Immutable audit timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_platform_commissions
models.description:
Platform commission tracking for revenue accounting.

Records platform commission earned on each order transaction for financial reporting and revenue tracking.
Commissions are calculated as a percentage of order subtotal before shipping and taxes based on configured commission rates.

Each commission record links to the payment transaction that generated the revenue and tracks the commission amount, rate applied, and calculation details.
Commission rates may vary by product category, seller tier, or promotional periods.

Commissions are recorded when orders are completed and funds are released to sellers.
If an order is refunded, commission adjustments are tracked separately to maintain accurate revenue accounting.

This table serves as the authoritative source for platform revenue reporting, financial reconciliation, and seller settlement calculations.
All commission records are immutable audit entries ensuring financial data integrity and compliance with accounting standards.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Payment transaction that generated this commission. {@link shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order associated with this commission. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller from whose sale this commission was earned. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: order_subtotal
plainFields.description: Order subtotal amount before shipping and taxes. Commission base calculation amount.

plainFields.name: commission_rate
plainFields.description: Commission rate percentage applied to this transaction. Stored as decimal (0.15 for 15%). May vary by category or seller tier.

plainFields.name: commission_amount
plainFields.description: Commission amount earned by the platform. Calculated as order_subtotal multiplied by commission_rate.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for amounts. Three-letter ISO 4217 code matching the order currency.

plainFields.name: commission_type
plainFields.description: Type of commission calculation. Values: standard, category_specific, seller_tier, promotional. Indicates which rate structure was applied.

plainFields.name: is_refunded
plainFields.description: Whether this commission has been reversed due to order refund. True when refund adjusts commission revenue.

plainFields.name: refunded_amount
plainFields.description: Commission amount refunded if partial or full order refund occurred. Zero if no refund. Used for net revenue calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the commission record was created. Immutable audit timestamp.

models.name: shopping_mall_reviews
models.description:
Product reviews submitted by verified buyers after purchase.

Captures buyer feedback including star ratings, written content, and optional product images.
Each review is associated with a specific product SKU variant and verified against the buyer's purchase history through order records.

Reviews require verified purchase validation to ensure authenticity and build platform trust.
Buyers can submit one review per product purchase transaction, and can edit or delete their reviews at any time.

The review system supports moderation workflows with pending, approved, and rejected statuses.
Reviews contribute to aggregate product ratings and influence product discovery through search ranking algorithms.
Seller responses are stored separately as distinct entities with their own lifecycle management.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who submitted the review. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sale_id
foreignFields.description: Product being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_sales.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_sale_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Specific product variant (SKU) being reviewed. {@link shopping_mall_sale_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order that verifies the purchase for verified purchase validation. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Review moderation status. Valid values: pending_moderation, approved, rejected. Determines public visibility.

plainFields.name: star_rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1 to 5 stars. Required field representing buyer satisfaction level.

plainFields.name: review_title
plainFields.description: Optional review title or summary. Maximum 100 characters. Provides quick overview of review content.

plainFields.name: review_body
plainFields.description: Detailed review text content. Minimum 10 characters when provided, maximum 5000 characters. Contains substantive buyer feedback about product quality, features, and experience.

plainFields.name: is_verified_purchase
plainFields.description: Whether this review is from a verified purchase. True when buyer purchased the product through the platform and order was delivered successfully.

plainFields.name: is_anonymous
plainFields.description: Whether buyer chose to submit review anonymously. When true, reviewer name displays as Anonymous Buyer instead of actual name.

plainFields.name: helpfulness_vote_count
plainFields.description: Total count of helpful votes from other buyers. Used for Most Helpful sorting algorithm. Incremented when buyers vote review as helpful.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Review submission timestamp. Recorded when buyer initially submits the review.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp. Updated when buyer edits review content or admin moderates the review.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Set when buyer or admin deletes the review. Deleted reviews excluded from public display and rating calculations.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_images
models.description:
Product images uploaded by buyers as part of their reviews.

Buyers can upload up to 5 images per review to provide visual evidence of product quality, appearance, and condition.
Images are processed and stored in multiple sizes for optimal display performance across different contexts.

Review images help other buyers make informed purchase decisions by showing real-world product appearance beyond seller-provided marketing images.
Images are displayed in review galleries with thumbnail, lightbox, and full-size viewing capabilities.

All images undergo automatic validation for format, size, and quality requirements before acceptance.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review that this image belongs to. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL path to the uploaded review image. Points to the original high-resolution image stored in the platform's media storage.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_url
plainFields.description: URL path to the generated thumbnail version. Size 200x200 pixels for efficient display in review lists.

plainFields.name: medium_url
plainFields.description: URL path to the medium-sized version. Size 800x800 pixels for lightbox preview displays.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display position order within the review's image gallery. Lower numbers appear first. Allows buyer to control image sequence.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Image upload timestamp. Recorded when buyer uploads the image during review submission or editing.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_seller_responses
models.description:
Seller responses to buyer reviews on their products.

Sellers can submit one response per review to address buyer feedback, provide explanations, or offer resolutions.
Responses demonstrate seller customer service quality and engagement with buyer feedback.

Each response is a distinct entity with its own creation timestamp and ownership separate from the buyer review.
Responses undergo the same moderation checks as buyer reviews to ensure professional tone and policy compliance.

When buyers edit their original reviews, associated seller responses are automatically removed to maintain contextual accuracy.
Sellers must submit fresh responses to edited review content.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review being responded to. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who submitted the response. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: response_body
plainFields.description: Seller response text content. Minimum 10 characters, maximum 2000 characters. Contains seller's reply to buyer feedback including explanations, apologies, or solutions offered.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Response moderation status. Valid values: pending_moderation, approved, rejected. Controls public visibility.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Response submission timestamp. Recorded when seller initially submits the response.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last modification timestamp. Updated when seller edits response or admin moderates it.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Set when seller deletes their response or system auto-removes due to review edit. Deleted responses excluded from public display.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_helpfulness_votes
models.description:
Buyer votes indicating whether reviews were helpful.

Authenticated buyers can vote on reviews to surface the most valuable feedback for other customers.
Each buyer can submit one vote per review choosing either helpful or not helpful.

Helpfulness votes determine review ranking in Most Helpful sort order and influence review visibility.
Votes are used to calculate helpfulness scores that prioritize useful reviews over less informative ones.

The system prevents duplicate voting, self-voting, and seller voting on their own product reviews to maintain vote integrity.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review being voted on. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who submitted the vote. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

plainFields.name: is_helpful
plainFields.description: Whether the buyer found the review helpful. True for helpful vote, false for not helpful vote. Only helpful votes increment the review's helpfulness count.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Vote submission timestamp. Recorded when buyer votes on review helpfulness.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_reports
models.description:
User-submitted reports flagging reviews for policy violations.

Buyers and sellers can report reviews they believe violate platform policies including spam, offensive content, fake reviews, or irrelevant feedback.
Each report requires a reason selection and optional detailed explanation to help admins investigate.

Reports are routed to the admin moderation queue for manual review.
Multiple reports on the same review escalate priority and may trigger automatic temporary hiding pending admin investigation.

The system tracks report patterns to identify users who abuse the reporting system and legitimate reviews that are frequently falsely reported.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review being reported. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: reporter_buyer_id
foreignFields.description: Buyer who submitted the report. {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id}.

foreignFields.name: reporter_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who submitted the report. {@link shopping_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: report_reason
plainFields.description: Reason category for the report. Valid values: spam, offensive_language, fake_review, not_about_product, personal_information, other. Helps admins prioritize and categorize violations.

plainFields.name: report_details
plainFields.description: Optional detailed explanation from reporter. Maximum 1000 characters. Provides context for admin investigation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Report resolution status. Valid values: pending, reviewed_valid, reviewed_invalid, dismissed. Tracks admin moderation outcome.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Report submission timestamp. Recorded when user flags the review.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Admin review completion timestamp. Set when admin completes investigation and makes moderation decision.

models.name: shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs
models.description:
Audit trail of review moderation actions and status changes.

Captures complete history of review lifecycle including submission, moderation decisions, status transitions, and admin actions.
Each log entry records who performed the action, what changed, and why the action was taken.

Moderation logs enable accountability, dispute resolution, and quality assurance for moderation consistency.
Admins can review moderation history to understand decision patterns and identify training opportunities.

Logs are append-only and immutable to maintain audit trail integrity for compliance and investigation purposes.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review being moderated. {@link shopping_mall_reviews.id}.

foreignFields.name: shopping_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who performed the moderation action. {@link shopping_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of moderation action performed. Valid values: auto_approved, auto_flagged, manual_approved, manual_rejected, edited_by_admin, deleted_by_admin, deleted_by_buyer, restored. Describes what happened to the review.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: Review status before this action. Valid values: pending_moderation, approved, rejected. Captures state transition.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: Review status after this action. Valid values: pending_moderation, approved, rejected. Records resulting state.

plainFields.name: moderation_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the moderation decision. Includes policy violation details, rejection reasons, or approval notes. Maximum 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: system_flags
plainFields.description: Automatic system flags that triggered moderation. JSON array of flag types detected by automated content analysis including profanity, spam patterns, or personal information.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Action timestamp. Recorded when the moderation action was performed.

Update the attributes of an existing product category identified by its unique category slug. This operation allows administrators to modify category information including name, description, parent category relationships, and display order within the hierarchy.

The category hierarchy can be restructured by changing parent relationships, enabling flexible taxonomy management. However, operations must validate that hierarchy changes don't create circular references or orphan categories.

Security: This operation is restricted to platform administrators only, as category structure directly impacts the entire marketplace product organization. Only users with the admin actor role can modify categories. The operation logs all changes for audit purposes.

Validation rules enforce data integrity including unique slug constraints, valid parent references, and proper hierarchy depth limits. The operation rejects updates that would violate these constraints or create inconsistent category structures.

Related operations: Create category (POST /categories), Delete category (DELETE /categories/{categorySlug}), List categories (PATCH /categories). Changes to categories may affect product listings and search indexes that reference the updated category.

It permanently removes the category record identified by the categoryId path parameter from the database. This operation is used when a category needs to be completely eliminated from the system, rather than just deactivated or hidden. The operation must ensure that the category can be safely deleted without violating referential integrity constraints with child categories or associated products.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a product category from the marketplace catalog
operations.description:
Permanently remove a product category entity from the shopping mall catalog system. This operation performs a hard delete, completely removing the category record from the database rather than marking it as inactive or archived.

The deletion process validates that the target category exists and can be safely removed. Categories that have child categories or associated product sales cannot be deleted until those relationships are resolved. The operation protects referential integrity by preventing deletion of categories that are actively referenced by other entities in the system.

Security considerations include restricting this operation to admin users only, as category deletion is a destructive administrative action that affects the entire marketplace structure. The operation logs all deletion attempts for audit purposes and tracks which admin performed the deletion.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_categories table from the Prisma schema. Before deletion, the system checks for dependent entities including child categories in the hierarchical structure and any product sales assigned to this category. If dependencies exist, the deletion is rejected with an appropriate error message guiding admins to resolve the dependencies first.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for navigating the hierarchical category structure and finding specific subcategories based on various criteria including name patterns, status, creation date, and other category attributes.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and flexible sorting options. Admins and system users can sort child categories by name, creation date, display order, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order. This enables efficient management of large category trees with potentially hundreds of subcategories under a single parent.

Security considerations include appropriate access control to ensure only authorized users can view and search the category hierarchy. The operation applies rate limiting for search queries to prevent abuse. Category visibility rules may filter results based on the requesting user's authorization level, though categories are generally publicly viewable data in an e-commerce context.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_categories table as defined in the Prisma schema, specifically querying records where the parent_id matches the categoryId path parameter. The response returns category summary information optimized for hierarchical display and navigation, including essential fields needed for rendering category trees and management interfaces. The operation efficiently handles deep category hierarchies through proper indexing on the parent_id foreign key relationship.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of product sales
operations.description:
Retrieve a comprehensive, filtered, and paginated list of product sales listings from the shopping mall marketplace. This operation provides advanced search and filtering capabilities essential for product discovery, inventory management, and marketplace analytics.

The search supports multiple filter criteria including partial product name matching, seller filtering, category hierarchy navigation, price range constraints, sale status filtering (active, paused, sold_out), and stock availability checks. Buyers can discover products across the marketplace, sellers can manage their inventory listings, and admins can monitor all marketplace activity.

Pagination is fully configurable with adjustable page sizes and supports multiple sorting options including creation date, price (ascending/descending), popularity metrics, and alphabetical ordering. The response returns summarized sale information optimized for list displays, including essential product details, pricing, primary images, seller information, and current stock status.

Security and authorization are role-based: public access allows basic product browsing for unauthenticated users, authenticated buyers receive personalized features like wishlist status, sellers can filter to view only their own listings, and admins have unrestricted access to all marketplace data with additional moderation fields.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_sales table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating relationships to sellers, categories, SKUs, and images. operations.summary: Create a new product sale listing
operations.description:
Create a new product sale listing in the shopping mall marketplace, enabling sellers to offer products to buyers. This operation is restricted to authenticated sellers and represents the first step in the complete product listing workflow.

Sellers provide comprehensive product information including product name, detailed description, category assignment for proper marketplace organization, base pricing structure, and initial sale configuration. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token, ensuring proper ownership assignment and preventing unauthorized listing creation.

The operation validates that the assigned category exists and is a valid leaf-level category in the hierarchy, preventing assignment to parent categories. Product names and descriptions must meet content guidelines, and pricing must be within acceptable ranges. The initial sale status is typically set to draft or pending, allowing sellers to complete variant setup, SKU configuration, and image uploads before activating the listing.

Upon successful creation, the operation returns the complete sale entity including the generated sale ID, which is required for subsequent operations such as adding variant attributes, creating SKUs, uploading images, and setting inventory levels. The created sale is associated with the authenticated seller and inherits default marketplace settings.

Security considerations include authentication enforcement (only sellers can create sales), rate limiting to prevent spam listings, content validation to ensure marketplace quality standards, and category validation to maintain proper taxonomy structure. This operation is foundational to the seller product management workflow.

Related operations: Update sale details (PUT /sales/{saleId}), Add sale variants (POST /sales/{saleId}/variants), Upload sale images (POST /sales/{saleId}/images), Manage inventory (POST /inventory-stocks).

Authorization is enforced through JWT token validation, and the system verifies that the authenticated seller's ID matches the sale's owner. Administrative users may have elevated permissions to moderate or update any listing.

Business rules enforced during updates include category existence validation, ensuring the sale code remains unique if modified, and maintaining referential integrity with related entities like SKUs and images. The deletion cascades to all related entities including sale snapshots, variant attributes, variant values, SKUs, product images, customer questions, and seller answers. Security considerations: This operation requires elevated administrative permissions as it permanently destroys business data. Only platform administrators should have access to this endpoint. The operation should be used cautiously as the deletion is irreversible and may affect historical order data, reviews, and inventory records that reference this sale.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for finding variant attributes based on various criteria including attribute name, display order, and attribute status.

Variant attributes represent the configurable dimensions of a product (such as Color, Size, Material, Style) that allow customers to select specific product variants. Each attribute contains multiple variant values that represent the specific options available (e.g., Color attribute has values like Red, Blue, Green). This operation returns the attribute definitions for a given sale, which can be used to display product configuration options to buyers.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Results can be sorted by display order, attribute name, creation date, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order. Advanced filtering allows searching by attribute name patterns or filtering by specific attribute characteristics.

Security considerations: This is a read-only operation that retrieves product configuration metadata. It can be accessed by authenticated users who need to view product variant options. The sale is identified by its unique business code, which must exist in the shopping_mall_sales table. The operation integrates with the shopping_mall_sale_variant_attributes table as defined in the Prisma schema, incorporating all available attribute fields and their relationships to variant values.

Security considerations include seller authentication and ownership verification. Only the seller who owns the sale can define its variant attributes. The operation integrates with the shopping_mall_sale_variant_attributes table as defined in the Prisma schema, creating the attribute structure that will later be populated with specific variant values through separate operations.

Each SKU represents a unique combination of variant attributes (such as color, size, material, etc.) with its own pricing, inventory quantity, and availability status. The SKU inherits the base product information from the parent sale but maintains independent stock levels and pricing.

The created SKU becomes immediately available for purchase if marked as active and has sufficient stock quantity. Inventory tracking begins automatically upon SKU creation. operations.summary: Delete a specific SKU variant from a product sale listing
operations.description:
Permanently remove a specific SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variant from a product sale listing. This operation allows sellers to delete SKU variants that are no longer available or offered, completely removing the record from the database.

The operation targets a specific SKU using composite unique identifiers. The saleCode identifies the parent product sale listing (with global uniqueness), while the skuCode identifies the specific SKU variant within that sale (scoped to the sale). This ensures precise targeting of the exact SKU to be deleted.

Security and business rule enforcement: Only the seller who owns the parent sale listing can delete its SKUs. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and validated against the sale's ownership. The operation enforces critical business rules to prevent data integrity violations. Specifically, SKUs that have existing inventory stock records, are referenced in active shopping carts, are part of pending or completed orders, or have inventory reservations cannot be deleted. These validations prevent orphaned data and ensure transactional consistency.

The deletion is permanent and irreversible. Once a SKU is deleted, all variant-specific information including pricing history, variant attribute mappings, and SKU-specific images are removed. The operation will fail with appropriate error messages if the SKU has any active dependencies. Sellers should ensure that the SKU has no active inventory, orders, or cart references before attempting deletion.

Common use cases include removing discontinued product variants, cleaning up test SKUs created during product setup, or eliminating variants that were created in error. Before deletion, sellers should consider whether archiving or marking the SKU as unavailable would be more appropriate for maintaining historical records.

Related operations: Update SKU (PUT /sales/{saleCode}/skus/{skuCode}), Create SKU (POST /sales/{saleCode}/skus), List all SKUs for a sale (GET /sales/{saleCode}/skus).

operations.description:
Create a new product image record associated with a specific sale listing in the shopping marketplace. This operation allows authenticated sellers to add visual assets to their product listings, which are essential for attracting buyers and showcasing product details effectively.

The operation accepts comprehensive image metadata including the image URL (which should reference a pre-uploaded file in the storage system), display order for gallery sequencing, alt text for accessibility, and optional dimension information. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token to ensure proper ownership association.

Security considerations include strict validation that the requesting seller owns the target sale listing. Only the seller who created the sale can add images to it, while admins have override capabilities for moderation purposes. The operation validates that the referenced sale exists and is in a state that allows image uploads (not finalized or archived).

Business rules enforced by this operation include maximum image count limits per sale (typically 10-20 images), file size restrictions, acceptable image formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP), and minimum resolution requirements for quality assurance. The display_order field is used to control the sequence of images in the product gallery, with the first image (order 0) serving as the primary thumbnail.

The created image becomes immediately visible in the seller's product management interface and, if the sale is published, in the buyer-facing product detail pages. Related operations include PATCH /sales/{saleCode}/images for retrieving the image list, PUT /sales/{saleCode}/images/{imageId} for updating image metadata, and DELETE /sales/{saleCode}/images/{imageId} for removing images.

operations.summary: Upload a new product image for a specific SKU variant of a sale listing
operations.description:
Upload and attach a new product image to a specific SKU variant within a sale listing. This operation enables sellers to add visual content to their product variants, enhancing the buyer's ability to evaluate the product before purchase.

The operation validates that the sale exists, the SKU belongs to the specified sale, and the seller has permission to modify the sale. Images are uploaded as URI references rather than binary data, following the API's content-type convention of application/json. The system may enforce limits on the number of images per SKU and validate image format requirements.

Security: Only the seller who owns the sale listing can upload images to their SKUs. The seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and validated against the sale's ownership. The operation includes validation to prevent unauthorized image uploads and ensures the SKU code is valid within the context of the specified sale.

The uploaded image becomes immediately visible in product displays and search results. Images should represent the actual product variant accurately to maintain marketplace trust and reduce return rates. Related operations include retrieving SKU images (GET /sales/{saleCode}/skus/{skuCode}/images/{imageId}) and managing the parent sale listing.

operations.summary: Retrieve paginated historical snapshots of a product sale
operations.description:
Fetch a filtered and paginated list of historical point-in-time snapshots for a specific product sale listing.

This operation provides access to the complete audit trail of a product sale's historical states. Each snapshot represents a frozen record of the sale's information at a specific moment in time, capturing changes to pricing, product descriptions, images, variants, and other sale attributes. This functionality is essential for transparency, dispute resolution, regulatory compliance, and understanding the evolution of product listings over time.

The operation supports advanced filtering and pagination to efficiently navigate through potentially large snapshot histories. Users can search snapshots by creation date ranges, sort chronologically to see the progression of changes, and paginate through results to manage large datasets. This is particularly valuable for sales that have undergone numerous modifications, allowing stakeholders to trace exactly when and how product information changed.

Security and access control: Snapshot visibility depends on user authorization. Sellers can view snapshots of their own products to review their listing history. Admins have broader access for marketplace oversight, fraud detection, and dispute resolution. Buyers may have limited access to snapshots related to their purchases for verification purposes. The operation enforces these access controls based on the authenticated user's role and relationship to the sale.

Business applications include: tracking price changes for competitive analysis, verifying product descriptions at the time of purchase for customer service, investigating seller behavior patterns for fraud detection, providing evidence in dispute resolution, and maintaining regulatory compliance for marketplace operations. The snapshot system ensures that historical product information is immutable and trustworthy.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_sale_snapshots table as defined in the Prisma schema, which has a snapshot stance indicating it contains historical audit trail data. Related operations include retrieving individual snapshot details (GET) and the main sale listing operations that trigger snapshot creation.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the current inventory stock information for a specific product SKU variant. It operates on the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table, which maintains real-time available quantities for each product variant. The operation requires the SKU ID to locate the corresponding inventory record and returns current stock levels including total quantity, reserved quantity, available quantity, and low stock threshold settings. This endpoint supports inventory monitoring, stock validation during checkout, and seller inventory management workflows.
operations.summary: Retrieve current inventory stock levels for a product SKU variant
operations.description:
Retrieve the current inventory stock information for a specific product SKU variant from the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table. This operation provides real-time visibility into stock levels, availability status, and inventory thresholds for a single product variant.

The inventory stock record represents the single source of truth for how many units of a specific SKU are currently available for purchase. The response includes total quantity (complete stock level), reserved quantity (units temporarily held during checkout), and available quantity (calculated as total minus reserved, representing units buyers can immediately purchase).

This endpoint is critical for several workflows: buyers checking product availability before purchase, sellers monitoring inventory levels across their catalog, and the checkout system validating stock availability during order placement. The low stock threshold field indicates the seller-configured level that triggers restock alerts.

Stock quantities are maintained through inventory transactions including sales, returns, restocks, and manual adjustments. Reserved quantities represent units in pending checkouts that are temporarily allocated but not yet confirmed as sold. When available quantity reaches zero, the SKU becomes unavailable for purchase until restocked.

The operation supports both seller self-service inventory monitoring (sellers viewing their own SKU stock levels) and administrative oversight (admins monitoring platform-wide inventory). Accurate real-time inventory data prevents overselling and ensures buyers see correct availability information.

Related operations: PATCH /inventoryStocks searches across multiple SKUs for bulk inventory monitoring, while this endpoint provides detailed stock information for a single SKU variant.

responseBody.description: Current inventory stock levels and threshold configuration for the SKU

Inventory reservations are critical for maintaining inventory accuracy during the purchase flow. When a buyer proceeds to checkout, inventory is temporarily reserved to ensure availability while payment is being processed. This operation allows tracking and verification of these temporary holds.

The reservation record includes the reserved SKU identifier, quantity held, creation timestamp, expiration timestamp, and associated order information. Reservations automatically expire after a configured time period if the order is not completed, releasing the inventory back to available stock.

Security considerations: Only authenticated users with appropriate permissions can access reservation details. Buyers can view their own reservations, while sellers can view reservations for their products, and admins have full access to all reservation records.

Update the details of an existing inventory reservation in the system. This operation allows modification of reservation parameters including reserved quantity, expiration timestamp, and reservation status.

Inventory reservations can be updated for several business scenarios: extending the reservation period when a buyer needs more time to complete checkout, adjusting the reserved quantity if the buyer modifies their cart before completing purchase, or releasing a reservation early if the buyer abandons the checkout process.

The update operation validates that the new reservation parameters are valid, such as ensuring the requested quantity doesn't exceed available inventory when increasing a reservation, or that expiration times are set to future timestamps. The system prevents updates that would violate inventory constraints or business rules.

Security and authorization: Only authorized actors can update reservations. Typically, the system automatically manages reservation updates during the checkout flow, but admins may have manual override capabilities for special cases or issue resolution. Buyers cannot directly modify reservations - updates occur through cart and checkout operations.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table as defined in the Prisma schema, ensuring all updates maintain referential integrity with related SKU and order records.

This operation is used to release a reservation when it's no longer needed, such as when a checkout is abandoned, a cart item is removed, or an order is successfully completed and the reservation should be converted to actual inventory deduction.
operations.summary: Delete an inventory reservation to release temporarily held stock
operations.description:
Delete an inventory reservation record to release the temporarily held stock quantity back to available inventory. This operation is used when a reservation is no longer needed and should be cancelled.

Inventory reservations are created during the checkout process to temporarily hold product quantities and prevent overselling while a buyer completes their purchase. Each reservation has an expiration time, after which it becomes invalid. This operation allows for manual cancellation of reservations before their natural expiration.

Common use cases include: (1) When a buyer removes items from their cart before checkout completion, (2) When a checkout session is abandoned and needs cleanup, (3) When an order is successfully placed and the reservation should be released as inventory is deducted through the order fulfillment process, (4) When system cleanup processes remove expired or orphaned reservations.

Security considerations: The operation validates that the reservation exists and is in a valid state for deletion. The system ensures that releasing the reservation properly updates the corresponding inventory stock levels. After deletion, the reserved quantity becomes available again for other buyers to purchase.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table from the Prisma schema. The deletion is permanent and cannot be undone. If the reservation has already been consumed by order placement, the operation may fail or have no effect depending on business rules.

Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of shopping cart items for the currently authenticated buyer. This operation provides the buyer's personal cart contents with support for complex queries including product filtering, sorting, and pagination.

The shopping cart is a buyer-specific collection of products they intend to purchase. Each cart item references a specific product SKU (variant) with a desired quantity. The cart persists across sessions, allowing buyers to save items for later purchase. This operation returns the current state of the buyer's cart with full product details for each item.

The operation supports comprehensive filtering and search capabilities including: filtering by product category, price range filtering, availability status filtering (in-stock vs out-of-stock items), sorting by date added, price, or product name, and pagination for large carts. The response includes detailed information about each cart item including the product details, selected SKU variant, current price, availability status, and quantity.

Security considerations: This operation is restricted to authenticated buyers and only returns cart items belonging to the current user based on their JWT token. Buyers cannot access other users' carts. The operation performs real-time validation of item availability and pricing, alerting buyers to any changes since items were added.

Business rules: Cart items may reference products that are no longer available or have changed in price. The response indicates such discrepancies so the buyer can make informed decisions. Quantity limits per item may apply based on available inventory. Items in the cart do not create inventory reservations until the buyer begins checkout.

Inventory validation occurs in real-time to prevent overselling situations. If the requested quantity exceeds available stock, the operation returns an error with current stock availability information. The updated cart item is returned with current pricing and availability details.

If the cart item doesn't exist or belongs to a different buyer, the operation returns an appropriate error.

Security considerations include authentication requirement and ownership validation. Only the cart owner can delete their cart items, preventing unauthorized modifications to other users' shopping carts. The operation is idempotent - attempting to delete an already-deleted or non-existent cart item returns a success response.

When a cart item is removed, any associated inventory reservations are released, making the stock available for other buyers. The operation completes immediately and does not return the deleted cart item data.

Related operations include updating cart item quantity (PUT /buyers/me/cart/items/{cartItemId}), retrieving the full cart (PATCH /buyers/me/cart/items), and adding items to cart (POST /buyers/me/cart/items). operations.specification: This operation creates a new order in the shopping marketplace by processing items from the buyer's shopping cart and initiating the checkout workflow. It operates on the shopping_mall_orders table and creates associated records in shopping_mall_order_sellers, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_inventory_reservations, and shopping_mall_payment_transactions tables. This endpoint handles the critical business transaction of converting cart items into confirmed orders with payment processing, inventory reservation, and multi-seller order splitting when necessary.
operations.summary: Create a new order from shopping cart items with payment processing
operations.description:
Create a new order by processing selected items from the authenticated buyer's shopping cart, validating inventory availability, calculating totals, processing payment, and reserving inventory for fulfillment. This operation executes the complete checkout workflow that transforms cart items into a confirmed purchase order.

The operation validates that all cart items are available and in stock, calculates order totals including product prices, quantities, taxes, shipping costs, and platform fees. It processes payment through the specified payment method, creates inventory reservations to prevent overselling, and splits the order into seller-specific portions when items come from multiple sellers. Each seller receives their portion of the order for independent fulfillment.

Security considerations include authentication to identify the buyer, validation of payment method ownership, verification of shipping address ownership, and prevention of race conditions during inventory reservation. The operation enforces business rules such as minimum order amounts, seller-specific shipping policies, and payment processing requirements.

This operation integrates with multiple Prisma schema tables including shopping_mall_orders (parent order), shopping_mall_order_sellers (seller-specific portions), shopping_mall_order_items (line items), shopping_mall_inventory_reservations (stock holds), shopping_mall_payment_transactions (payment records), and shopping_mall_cart_items (source items that are cleared after successful order creation). The response includes the complete created order with all nested relationships, payment confirmation, and order tracking information.

Related operations: Buyers must first add items to cart (POST /cart-items), manage shipping addresses (POST /buyer-addresses), and configure payment methods (POST /payment-methods) before creating orders. After order creation, buyers track orders (GET /orders/{orderId}) and sellers fulfill orders (PUT /order-sellers/{orderSellerId}).

requestBody.description: Order creation details including cart item selection, shipping address, payment method, and delivery preferences

responseBody.description: Complete created order information including order ID, payment confirmation, and initial order status

operations.summary: Update an existing order's information

Update an existing order in the shopping mall platform with modified information. This operation allows buyers to update certain aspects of their orders, typically before the order has been processed or shipped by sellers.

The operation supports updating mutable order properties such as delivery address changes, special delivery instructions, or contact information updates. Not all order fields are editable - certain fields like order totals, purchased items, and payment information are immutable once the order is placed.

Security considerations include ownership verification to ensure only the order owner can modify the order, and business rule validation to prevent updates to orders that are already in shipping or delivered status. The operation validates that the order exists, belongs to the authenticated buyer, and is in a state that allows modifications.

operations.specification: This operation performs soft deletion of an order record from the shopping_mall_orders table in the Prisma schema. It marks the order as deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp while retaining the record for historical, audit, and compliance purposes. This operation should only be available under specific business conditions, such as orders in draft or pending payment states, or for administrative cleanup purposes.
operations.summary: Soft delete an order from the system
operations.description:
Mark an order record as deleted in the shopping mall platform by setting the deleted_at timestamp. This operation uses soft deletion to preserve the order record for historical, legal, and compliance purposes while hiding it from active buyer views.

The deletion operation is restricted to specific order states and user roles. Typically, only orders that have not been confirmed or paid can be deleted by buyers. Orders that are in processing, shipped, or delivered states generally cannot be deleted and should use the cancellation workflow instead through the dedicated cancellation operations.

Security validation ensures that only authorized users can delete orders - buyers can only delete their own orders in eligible states. The operation validates order ownership, current status eligibility, and performs the soft deletion by setting the deleted_at field in the shopping_mall_orders table.

This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_orders table as defined in the Prisma schema. The soft deletion preserves all order data including items, status history, and payment information for audit trails. Deleted orders are filtered from normal queries but remain accessible for administrative review and compliance reporting. For orders that need to be reversed after processing, use the cancellation or refund request workflows instead. Related operations include order cancellation (POST /orders/{orderId}/cancel) and refund requests (POST /orders/{orderId}/refund-requests).

Administrative users have elevated permissions to delete orders across all states for system maintenance, dispute resolution, fraud prevention, and regulatory compliance purposes. Unlike buyer deletion which is restricted to specific order states, administrators can mark orders as deleted regardless of their current status when business requirements justify such action.

Security validation ensures proper administrative authorization before allowing deletion. The operation performs the soft deletion by setting the deleted_at field in the shopping_mall_orders table while preserving all order data, associated items, status history, and payment records for audit trails and legal compliance.

operations.summary: Create a new refund request for a delivered order
