Pagination metadata for navigating through review report results.

Provides essential information for client-side pagination controls including current page number, total number of pages, records per page limit, and total record count. Enables users to navigate forward and backward through the complete set of review reports matching the search criteria.

This metadata is critical for administrative moderation interfaces where large volumes of reports need to be processed efficiently without overwhelming the UI or network with excessive data transfer.

data.description:
Array of review report summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual review report data matching the search filters and pagination parameters. Each element is a lightweight summary representation optimized for list views in moderation queues and administrative dashboards.

The array length will not exceed the limit specified in the pagination metadata, and may be shorter on the final page of results. Empty array indicates no reports match the current filter criteria or the requested page is beyond the available data range.

IPageIShoppingMallReviewReport.ISummary.description:
Paginated response wrapper for review report summaries.

Encapsulates a page of review report records along with pagination metadata, enabling efficient navigation through large collections of user-submitted reports flagging reviews for policy violations. This structure follows the standard IPage pattern used throughout the API for consistent pagination behavior.

Used as the response type for search and filter operations on review reports, particularly in administrative moderation workflows where moderators need to process multiple reports efficiently. The pagination wrapper allows clients to request specific page ranges and provides all necessary information to build pagination controls.

This wrapper type combines the IPage.IPagination metadata (current page, total pages, record counts) with an array of IShoppingMallReviewReport.ISummary entities representing the actual report data for the current page. The separation of pagination metadata from content data enables flexible client-side rendering and progressive loading strategies.

pagination.description:
Pagination metadata for navigating through moderation log audit trail.

Provides essential information for client-side pagination controls including current page number, total number of pages, records per page limit, and total record count. Enables administrators to navigate through the complete audit history of moderation actions taken on a specific review.

This metadata is critical for administrative audit interfaces where comprehensive review of moderation history is required for compliance, quality assurance, and investigation purposes without overwhelming the interface with excessive historical data.

data.description:
Array of moderation log summary records for the current page.

Contains the actual moderation action history matching the search filters and pagination parameters. Each element is a lightweight summary representation optimized for audit trail displays and administrative dashboards showing who performed which actions when.

The array length will not exceed the limit specified in the pagination metadata, and may be shorter on the final page of results. Empty array indicates no moderation actions match the current filter criteria or the requested page is beyond the available audit history range.

IPageIShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.IS.description:
Paginated response wrapper for review moderation log summaries.

Encapsulates a page of moderation log records along with pagination metadata, enabling efficient navigation through comprehensive audit trails of administrative actions taken on product reviews. This structure follows the standard IPage pattern used throughout the API for consistent pagination behavior.

Used as the response type for moderation history queries, particularly in administrative compliance and quality assurance workflows where complete visibility into moderation decisions is required. The pagination wrapper allows administrators to navigate through potentially extensive audit histories while maintaining reasonable response sizes and performance.

This wrapper type combines the IPage.IPagination metadata (current page, total pages, record counts) with an array of IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.ISummary entities representing the actual moderation action history for the current page. The separation of pagination metadata from audit content enables flexible rendering of moderation timelines and progressive loading of historical records.

email.description:
Buyer email address used for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all buyer accounts in the shopping_mall_buyers table. Serves as the primary identifier for login and account recovery.

The system validates this against RFC 5322 email format standards and enforces uniqueness constraints at the database level. This email will be used for order confirmations, shipping updates, and other transactional communications.

password.description:
Buyer's plain text password for authentication.

This is the plain text password provided during registration, which will be securely hashed by the backend using bcrypt with minimum work factor of 12 rounds before storage in the password_hash column. The password must meet minimum security requirements including length constraints.

Buyers should never send pre-hashed passwords - the hashing is exclusively the backend's responsibility. The plain text password is never stored or logged by the system.

full_name.description:
Buyer full name for personalization and order fulfillment.

Displayed in order confirmations and shipping labels. Used throughout the platform for personalized experiences. Minimum 2 characters, maximum 100 characters as enforced by the shopping_mall_buyers table schema.

This should be the buyer's real name for accurate order fulfillment and delivery purposes.

phone_number.description:
Buyer contact phone number with country code for delivery coordination.

Stored with country code following E.164 international format. Used for order delivery coordination and customer support communications.

The phone number may be used for SMS notifications about order status changes and delivery updates according to buyer preferences. This field is optional during registration (nullable in the shopping_mall_buyers table) to allow for flexibility in account creation flows where buyers may not have or wish to provide a phone number immediately.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.

This field is OPTIONAL - the server can extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers. However, clients may provide it explicitly for server-side rendering scenarios or when the actual client IP differs from the request IP.

The IP address is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for security monitoring, fraud detection, and audit trail purposes. Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the current page where registration occurred.

This MANDATORY field captures the exact URL of the registration page for session context tracking and analytics. It helps identify registration sources and user journey patterns.

The href is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table as part of the session metadata, enabling analysis of registration conversion funnels and user acquisition channels.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL representing the previous page before registration.

This MANDATORY field captures where the user came from before reaching the registration page. It can be an empty string for direct access but must be provided.

The referrer is essential for tracking marketing campaign effectiveness, understanding user acquisition sources, and analyzing the customer journey. It is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for analytics and attribution purposes.

IShoppingMallBuyer.ICreate.description:
Request body for buyer registration (join) operation.

This schema defines the data required to create a new buyer account in the shopping mall platform. It includes essential buyer information from the shopping_mall_buyers table: email, password_hash (submitted as plain password), full_name, and optionally phone_number, along with session context fields for audit trails.

The registration process creates a new buyer record in the shopping_mall_buyers table and simultaneously establishes an initial authentication session in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table. This atomic operation ensures buyers can immediately access the platform after registration without requiring a separate login step.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because this is a self-signup operation where the buyer themselves are creating their account. The session is created immediately upon registration, so connection metadata must be captured at this point.

Security measures include password strength validation, email uniqueness verification, and secure credential storage. The plain text password is hashed by the backend before storage, following industry-standard security practices.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying the buyer account.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key (id) in the shopping_mall_buyers table, uniquely identifying the buyer across the entire platform. The ID is included in the authentication response to enable immediate buyer identification without requiring additional API calls.

Clients should store this ID for session management and use it to associate subsequent API requests with the authenticated buyer. The ID remains constant throughout the buyer's lifetime on the platform and serves as the authoritative buyer identifier in all system operations.

email.description:
Buyer email address used for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all buyer accounts. Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards. Used as the primary login credential and for order notifications, shipping updates, and promotional communications.

This field corresponds to the email column in the shopping_mall_buyers table and serves as the unique identifier for authentication.

full_name.description:
Buyer full name for personalization and order fulfillment.

Displayed in order confirmations and shipping labels. Used throughout the platform for personalized shopping experiences. Minimum 2 characters, maximum 100 characters as enforced by the shopping_mall_buyers table schema.

This field corresponds to the full_name column in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

phone_number.description:
Buyer contact phone number with country code.

Optional during registration but recommended for order delivery coordination and customer support. Stored with country code in E.164 international format (e.g., +821012345678).

Used for SMS notifications about order status and delivery updates. This field corresponds to the nullable phone_number column in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status indicating whether the buyer has confirmed ownership of the email address.

Unverified accounts have restricted capabilities including inability to place orders. This flag is set to false upon registration and updated to true after the buyer confirms their email through the verification link.

This field corresponds to the email_verified column in the shopping_mall_buyers table and is used for account capability enforcement.

created_at.description:
Account creation timestamp recording when the buyer registered on the platform.

Automatically set by the system upon successful registration. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format. Used for user analytics and account age tracking.

This field corresponds to the created_at column in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

updated_at.description:
Last modification timestamp recording when buyer profile information was last updated.

Automatically updated by the system on any profile changes. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format. Used for tracking account activity and security monitoring.

This field corresponds to the updated_at column in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for account deactivation.

When set, the account is considered deactivated and login is prevented. Accounts can be reactivated within 90 days by clearing this field. This implements soft-delete functionality for buyer accounts.

This field corresponds to the nullable deleted_at column in the shopping_mall_buyers table and is null for active accounts.

IShoppingMallBuyer.IAuthorized.description:
Successful authentication response containing buyer identity and authorization tokens.

This response is returned upon successful buyer login, registration, or token refresh operations, providing all necessary information for the client to establish and maintain an authenticated session. The structure includes complete buyer profile data from the shopping_mall_buyers table along with JWT authentication credentials.

The response enables immediate buyer identification and includes both short-lived access tokens for API authorization and long-lived refresh tokens for session persistence. All fields correspond directly to columns in the shopping_mall_buyers table except for the token object which contains JWT credentials.

Upon receiving this response, clients should securely store both the buyer ID and tokens (preferably in secure HTTP-only cookies for web applications or secure storage mechanisms for mobile applications). The access token should be included in all subsequent API requests, while the refresh token should be securely stored for token renewal when the access token expires.

The successful authentication also creates a corresponding session record in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table, linking the tokens to the buyer's authentication history and enabling session management, security monitoring, and audit capabilities.

email.description:
Buyer's registered email address used as the unique login identifier.

This email must match an existing buyer account in the shopping_mall_buyers table. The system performs case-insensitive email matching during authentication to ensure consistent login experience regardless of input casing.

Email validation follows RFC 5322 standards, ensuring proper email format before authentication attempts. Failed authentication with valid email format may indicate incorrect password or non-existent account.

password.description:
Buyer's plain text password for credential verification.

The password is transmitted securely over HTTPS and is immediately hashed using the platform's password hashing algorithm (typically bcrypt or Argon2) for comparison against the stored hashed password in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

The plain text password is never stored or logged by the system. Password verification occurs through secure one-way hashing comparison, ensuring password confidentiality throughout the authentication process.

Minimum password requirements are enforced during account creation but not validated again during login, as stored passwords already meet security standards.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security audit purposes.

This field is optional as the server can typically extract the IP address from the HTTP request headers. However, clients may provide it explicitly for scenarios such as server-side rendering (SSR) where the actual client IP differs from the proxy IP.

The IP address is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table as part of the session record, enabling security monitoring, fraud detection, and geographical access analysis. Both IPv4 and IPv6 formats are supported.

When not provided by the client, the backend automatically extracts the IP from request headers (X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, or direct socket connection).

href.description:
Current page URL where the login action was initiated.

This mandatory field captures the complete URL of the page from which the buyer attempted to log in, providing context for the authentication event. The href is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for audit trail purposes and user experience analysis.

Typical values include the login page URL, checkout page (for login during purchase), or any page with embedded login functionality. This information helps understand user behavior patterns and can be used for post-login redirection to improve user experience.

The URL should be a complete, valid URI including protocol (https://), domain, path, and any query parameters that provide session context.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the previous page before the login page.

This mandatory field captures the URL of the page the buyer visited immediately before accessing the login functionality. The referrer is stored in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for marketing attribution, user journey analysis, and session flow tracking.

For direct navigation to the login page (e.g., typing URL directly or bookmark access), this field should be an empty string. For organic navigation through the site, it contains the full URL of the previous page, helping understand how buyers arrive at the login process.

This information is valuable for conversion funnel analysis, identifying which pages or features drive login actions, and understanding user navigation patterns throughout the shopping experience.

IShoppingMallBuyer.ILogin.description:
Buyer login credentials and session context for authentication.

This request body contains all information necessary to authenticate a buyer account and establish a new authenticated session. The structure combines credential validation fields (email and password) with session context metadata (IP, href, referrer) to enable both secure authentication and comprehensive session tracking.

The email and password fields are used for credential verification against the shopping_mall_buyers table, while the session context fields populate the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for audit trail and security monitoring purposes.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) provide valuable insights into login patterns, user behavior, and potential security threats. They enable the platform to detect suspicious login activities, analyze user journey patterns, and maintain detailed audit logs for compliance and customer support purposes.

All fields except IP address are mandatory, ensuring complete session context capture for every login attempt. The IP address is optional because the server can extract it from HTTP headers, though clients may provide it explicitly for special cases like server-side rendering scenarios.

refresh.description:
Valid refresh token from a previous authentication response.

This JWT refresh token was originally issued during buyer login and is now being submitted to obtain a new access token. The refresh token must be valid, not expired, and associated with an active buyer session in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table.

The system validates the refresh token by verifying its cryptographic signature, checking its expiration time, and confirming that the associated session has not been revoked or invalidated. If validation succeeds, a new access token (and potentially a new refresh token, depending on token rotation policy) is issued.

Refresh tokens are long-lived credentials (typically 7-30 days) that enable buyers to maintain authenticated sessions without repeatedly entering their login credentials. They should be stored securely by clients and transmitted only to this refresh endpoint.

If the refresh token is expired, invalid, or associated with a revoked session, the request will fail, requiring the buyer to log in again with their email and password credentials.

IShoppingMallBuyer.IRefresh.description:
Request body for refreshing authentication tokens.

This simple structure contains only the refresh token necessary to obtain new access tokens without requiring the buyer to re-enter their login credentials. The refresh operation is a critical component of modern token-based authentication systems, enabling seamless session continuation while maintaining security through short-lived access tokens.

The refresh token submitted in this request was originally issued during the buyer's login (via the IShoppingMallBuyer.ILogin operation) or during a previous token refresh operation (if token rotation is implemented). The token serves as proof of the buyer's authenticated session and is validated against the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table.

Upon successful validation, the system issues a new access token with a fresh expiration time, allowing the buyer to continue accessing authenticated endpoints. Depending on the platform's security policy, the system may also issue a new refresh token and invalidate the old one (token rotation), enhancing security by limiting the lifetime of any single refresh token.

This operation is typically performed automatically by client applications when they detect that the current access token is expired or about to expire, providing a seamless authentication experience without user intervention.

IShoppingMallSeller.ICreate.description:
Request body for seller account registration in the e-commerce marketplace.

This schema defines the data required to create a new seller account. It captures essential seller information including authentication credentials, contact details, and complete business information. The registration process validates this data before creating a new record in the shopping_mall_sellers database table.

Security considerations include password validation (the plain text password will be hashed server-side before storage), email uniqueness verification, and input sanitization to prevent injection attacks.

The seller account is created with initial status and requires email verification. Upon successful registration, the seller receives JWT tokens for immediate authenticated access to seller dashboard features.

email.description:
Seller email address used for authentication and business communication.

This email serves as the unique identifier for the seller account and is used for login credentials. Must be unique across all seller accounts in the system to prevent duplicate registrations.

The system validates email format according to RFC 5322 standards and checks for duplicate registrations. This corresponds to the 'email' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

password.description:
Seller's password for account authentication (plain text).

The password is provided in plain text during registration and will be securely hashed using bcrypt with minimum work factor of 12 rounds before being stored in the database as password_hash.

Password strength requirements include minimum 8 characters. The server handles all hashing operations to ensure consistent security practices. Never send or store passwords in hashed form from the client.

full_name.description:
Seller contact person full name for business correspondence.

This is the full name of the seller representative or business owner used for official business correspondence and account verification. May represent the business owner or authorized representative depending on the business structure.

The name should be between 1 and 255 characters. This corresponds to the 'full_name' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

phone_number.description:
Business contact phone number with country code.

The phone number is required for seller accounts to enable direct communication for order fulfillment and customer service. Should be provided in international format (E.164 standard) starting with a country code.

Example formats: +821012345678 (South Korea), +14155551234 (USA), +447911123456 (UK). This corresponds to the 'phone_number' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

business_name.description:
Legal business name or DBA (Doing Business As) name.

This is the official legal business name used for official documentation, tax purposes, and business verification. It represents the registered business entity operating on the marketplace.

Minimum 2 characters, maximum 200 characters. Used for compliance and business validation processes. This corresponds to the 'business_name' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

business_description.description:
Business overview describing the seller store, product focus, and brand identity.

This description is displayed on the seller store page to help buyers understand the business offerings, brand story, and product specialization. It should provide a compelling overview of what makes the business unique.

Maximum 2000 characters. Used for seller store pages and buyer discovery. This corresponds to the 'business_description' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

store_name.description:
Public-facing store brand name displayed to buyers throughout the platform.

This is the customer-facing brand name that appears in product listings, search results, and seller pages. Must be unique across all sellers to ensure distinct brand identities.

Maximum 100 characters. Used prominently throughout the buyer experience. This corresponds to the 'store_name' field in the shopping_mall_sellers Prisma schema.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing (OPTIONAL - server can extract).

The IP address from which the seller is registering. This is optional as the server can extract it from the request headers automatically. However, clients may provide it explicitly in server-side rendering scenarios or when using proxy servers.

Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats. Used for security monitoring, fraud detection, and maintaining session audit trails in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) where the registration is occurring (MANDATORY).

This is the full URL of the page from which the seller initiated the registration process. It provides context for session tracking and helps understand user registration flow patterns.

This value is stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table along with the session record created upon successful registration. Required for complete session tracking.

Example: https://marketplace.example.com/seller/register

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that led to the registration page (MANDATORY).

This is the URL of the page the seller visited immediately before arriving at the registration page. It helps track marketing effectiveness, user journey analysis, and referral sources.

Can be an empty string if the seller navigated directly to the registration page (direct access with no previous page). Required for analytics and user flow tracking.

Example: https://marketplace.example.com/seller/info or empty string for direct navigation.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated seller account.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key (id field) in the shopping_mall_sellers table and uniquely identifies the seller throughout the system. It is used for authorization checks, data association, and audit trails.

The seller ID is embedded in JWT tokens to enable stateless authentication and is referenced across all seller-related operations including product management, order processing, and analytics.

email.description:
Email address of the authenticated seller account.

This is the verified email address from the shopping_mall_sellers table (email field) that serves as the seller's primary identifier and contact method. It is used for account communications, notifications, and as the username for login.

The email is included in the authorization response to enable the client to display account information and verify the authenticated identity.

full_name.description:
Seller contact person full name for business correspondence and account verification.

This is the full name from the shopping_mall_sellers table (full_name field) representing the seller representative or business owner. May represent the business owner or authorized representative depending on the business structure.

Used for official business correspondence, account verification, and display in seller dashboard and profile pages.

phone_number.description:
Business contact phone number with country code for direct communication.

This is the phone number from the shopping_mall_sellers table (phone_number field) required for seller accounts to enable direct communication for order fulfillment and customer service.

Used for important notifications, order updates, and customer communication. Displayed in international format.

business_name.description:
Legal business name or DBA (Doing Business As) name for official documentation.

This is the official legal business name from the shopping_mall_sellers table (business_name field) used for official documentation, tax purposes, and business verification.

Represents the registered business entity operating on the marketplace. Used for compliance and business validation processes.

business_description.description:
Business overview describing the seller store, product focus, and brand identity.

This description from the shopping_mall_sellers table (business_description field) is displayed on the seller store page to help buyers understand the business offerings, brand story, and product specialization.

Provides a compelling overview of what makes the business unique. Used for seller store pages and buyer discovery.

store_name.description:
Public-facing store brand name displayed to buyers throughout the platform.

This is the customer-facing brand name from the shopping_mall_sellers table (store_name field) that appears in product listings, search results, and seller pages. Unique across all sellers to ensure distinct brand identities.

Used prominently throughout the buyer experience to identify the seller's store and products.

status.description:
Seller account approval and operational status determining platform capabilities.

This status from the shopping_mall_sellers table (status field) indicates the current state of the seller account. Valid values include: pending (awaiting admin approval), approved (active seller with full access), rejected (application denied), suspended (temporarily restricted).

Determines seller capabilities and product visibility. Only approved sellers can create listings and receive orders.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status indicating confirmed email ownership.

This boolean from the shopping_mall_sellers table (email_verified field) indicates whether the seller has confirmed ownership of the business email address through the verification process.

Unverified accounts cannot access seller dashboard or create listings. Email verification is required for account activation and security.

created_at.description:
Account creation timestamp recording when the seller registered on the platform.

This timestamp from the shopping_mall_sellers table (created_at field) records the exact date and time when the seller registered on the marketplace platform.

Used for seller onboarding analytics, account age tracking, and historical analysis of seller acquisition.

updated_at.description:
Last modification timestamp recording when seller profile was last updated.

This timestamp from the shopping_mall_sellers table (updated_at field) tracks the most recent modification to any seller account field. Automatically updated on any changes.

Used for change tracking, audit trails, and data synchronization across the system.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for account deactivation and preservation.

This nullable timestamp from the shopping_mall_sellers table (deleted_at field) implements the soft delete pattern by recording when the account was deactivated rather than physically deleting the record.

When set, the seller account is deactivated, all product listings are hidden, and login is prevented. Accounts can be reactivated within 90 days. Null for active accounts.

IShoppingMallSeller.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated seller account information with JWT tokens for authorized access.

This schema represents the successful authentication response for seller accounts, containing the seller's complete profile information from the shopping_mall_sellers table along with JWT tokens for subsequent authenticated requests.

The response includes both access tokens (for API requests) and refresh tokens (for token renewal) following JWT best practices. The seller's profile information enables the client to display account details and personalize the user interface.

This DTO is returned from both login and token refresh operations, providing a consistent authentication response structure. All sensitive data like passwords are excluded for security.

email.description:
Seller's registered email address used for authentication.

This email must match an existing verified email in the shopping_mall_sellers table. Email validation follows RFC 5322 standards and is case-insensitive for comparison purposes.

The email serves as the unique identifier for seller accounts during the login process.

password.description:
Seller's account password in plain text for authentication verification.

The password is transmitted securely and compared against the hashed password stored in the shopping_mall_sellers table using cryptographic hashing algorithms. The plain text password is never stored and is only used for verification during the authentication process.

Password strength requirements are enforced during account registration to ensure security.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring (OPTIONAL - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR).

This field captures the network address from which the login request originates. The IP address is stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for audit trails and security analysis.

IP tracking enables detection of suspicious login patterns, geographic anomalies, and potential account compromise. While the server can typically extract this from the request headers, clients may provide it explicitly in server-side rendering scenarios.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the current page URL where the login is being performed (MANDATORY).

This field records the exact page location where the authentication request originated. It is stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table as part of the session metadata.

The href provides context for understanding user behavior, enables proper redirect flows after authentication, and supports security monitoring by tracking login page variations. This value must be provided by the client as the server cannot reliably infer the client-side page context.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL representing the previous page URL before the login page (MANDATORY).

This field captures the page that directed the user to the login flow. It is stored in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table for analytics and user flow analysis.

The referrer helps understand how sellers navigate to the login page, supports marketing attribution, and aids in detecting unusual authentication patterns. An empty string is acceptable for direct navigation to the login page. This value must be provided by the client as it reflects client-side navigation history.

IShoppingMallSeller.ILogin.description:
Seller login request credentials for authentication.

This schema represents the data required to authenticate a seller account in the shopping mall platform. It collects the seller's email and password for credential verification, along with session context information (IP address, current page URL, and referrer URL) for security monitoring and audit trails.

The login process validates these credentials against the shopping_mall_sellers table and creates a new session record in shopping_mall_seller_sessions upon successful authentication. Session context fields enable comprehensive security monitoring and user behavior analysis.

This DTO is used exclusively for seller authentication endpoints and must include both authentication credentials and connection metadata for complete session tracking.

refresh_token.description:
Valid refresh token used to obtain new access tokens without re-authentication.

This token is a long-lived JWT that was issued during the initial login or previous refresh operation. It is validated against the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table to ensure it belongs to an active, non-revoked session.

The refresh token enables seamless token renewal without requiring the seller to re-enter credentials. It has a longer lifespan than access tokens (typically days to weeks) but is securely stored and transmitted to maintain security.

Refresh tokens are rotated with each refresh operation to prevent token reuse attacks, and any refresh token can be revoked when the seller logs out or when suspicious activity is detected.

IShoppingMallSeller.IRefresh.description:
Seller token refresh request for obtaining new access tokens.

This schema represents the data required to refresh expired or near-expiration access tokens for seller accounts. It contains the refresh token that was issued during login or a previous refresh operation.

The refresh mechanism allows sellers to maintain authenticated sessions without repeatedly entering credentials, balancing security with user experience. The refresh token is validated against active sessions in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table.

Token refresh operations implement security best practices including refresh token rotation, reuse detection, and automatic revocation on suspicious activity. This DTO is used exclusively for seller token refresh endpoints.

Must be unique across all admin accounts. Serves as the primary identifier for secure admin access and system communications.

password_hash.description:

Never stores plain text passwords. This hash is generated from the admin's password during registration or password updates using bcrypt with a minimum of 12 rounds as specified in the Prisma schema.

Generated through secure system-level processes. Used for admin tenure tracking, audit purposes, and access history analysis.

updated_at.description:
Last modification timestamp for admin account information.

Automatically updated on any changes including profile updates, privilege level adjustments, or security setting modifications. Tracks account maintenance history.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for admin account deactivation.

When set, the admin account is deactivated and all administrative access is revoked. Used for former administrators, compromised accounts, or security incidents. Null for active accounts.

IShoppingMallAdmin.description:
Complete platform administrator account with elevated marketplace governance permissions.

Admins are trusted platform operators responsible for maintaining marketplace integrity, moderating content, resolving disputes, and managing platform-wide configurations. Admin accounts are created through secure system-level processes rather than public registration.

Each admin has an assigned privilege level (super_admin, moderator, or support) determining their access scope. This hierarchical permission model enables appropriate delegation while maintaining security. The system enforces mandatory two-factor authentication for all admin accounts.

Admins have all capabilities of buyers and sellers for testing and support purposes, plus exclusive administrative functions. All admin actions are comprehensively logged for accountability and compliance. Account lifecycle includes active and soft-deleted states with strict access controls.

IShoppingMallAdmin.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new platform administrator account during registration.

This DTO contains the essential information required to establish a new admin account in the system, including authentication credentials, profile details, privilege level assignment, and contact information. The password is provided in plain text and will be securely hashed by the backend before storage.

All core admin fields (email, full_name, phone_number, admin_level, email_verified) are required during registration to ensure complete account setup. The admin_level must be specified at creation to establish the appropriate permission scope from the start.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included because this is a self-registration operation where the administrator is creating their own account and establishing their initial session immediately upon successful registration.

email.description:
Administrator email address for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all admin accounts. This email will serve as the login credential and must follow RFC 5322 email format standards. Used for authentication, platform notifications, and administrative communications.

password.description:
Administrator password for authentication (plain text).

The backend will hash this password using secure algorithms before storing it in the password_hash column of the shopping_mall_admins table. The password should meet platform security requirements for strength and complexity.

This plain text password will never be stored directly - it is immediately hashed upon receipt using bcrypt with minimum 12 rounds.

full_name.description:
Full name of the administrator for identification and audit logging.

Used in admin action records, accountability tracking, and internal communications. This name will be displayed in the admin dashboard and associated with all administrative operations.

Provides clear identification of which administrator performed specific actions throughout the system. Required for complete account setup and audit trail accuracy.

phone_number.description:
Admin contact phone number for two-factor authentication and emergency contact.

Required for all admin accounts to enable SMS-based 2FA verification. This phone number is mandatory as it serves as a critical security component ensuring authorized access to administrative functions.

The phone number should be in a valid format capable of receiving SMS messages for authentication codes. Used for account security and emergency administrator contact purposes.

oneOf.description:
Super administrator privilege level with full platform access.

Grants complete access to all platform functions including system configuration, admin management, seller approval, content moderation, and all operational capabilities.

This is the highest privilege level and should be assigned carefully only to trusted platform operators.

Moderator privilege level for content oversight and seller management.

Provides access to content moderation functions, seller approval workflows, and dispute resolution capabilities. Cannot modify system-level configurations or manage other administrator accounts.

Suitable for team members focused on marketplace integrity and content quality.

Support privilege level for customer service operations.

Limited to customer service functions and basic operational support tasks. Cannot access system configuration, admin management, or content moderation features.

Appropriate for customer support staff who need administrative access for assisting users.

admin_level.description:
Admin privilege level determining access scope and permissions.

Must be specified at account creation to establish the appropriate permission scope from the start. This level controls which administrative functions the account can access.

Valid values:
- super_admin: Full access to all platform functions including system configuration and admin management
- moderator: Content moderation, seller approval, and dispute resolution capabilities
- support: Customer service functions and basic operational support

The privilege level cannot be changed through regular update operations and requires special administrative approval for modifications.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status to set during admin account creation.

Indicates whether the administrator's email address has been verified at the time of registration. This field allows the system to create admin accounts with pre-verified email addresses (true) for trusted onboarding processes, or unverified status (false) requiring subsequent email verification.

Since email_verified is a non-nullable field in the Prisma schema without a default value, it must be explicitly specified during account creation to ensure proper initialization of the admin account's verification state.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking (optional - server can extract, but client may provide for SSR).

Recorded in the admin session for security auditing and tracking the origin of administrative access. Can be IPv4 or IPv6 format.

While optional in the request (server can extract from connection), providing this field is useful in server-side rendering scenarios where the true client IP needs to be forwarded.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) where the registration is occurring.

Mandatory field that captures the exact URL from which the admin account creation was initiated, used for session tracking and security audit trails.

This URL is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to maintain a complete record of where administrative sessions originated for security monitoring and compliance purposes.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) that led to the registration page.

Mandatory field that tracks the navigation path leading to account creation. Can be an empty string for direct access to the registration page.

Provides context about how the administrator reached the registration form, useful for security analysis and tracking registration source patterns.

email.description:
Administrator's email address used for authentication.

Must be a valid email format and match an existing administrator account in the shopping_mall_admins table. This email serves as the unique identifier for admin authentication.

The system performs case-insensitive email matching during authentication to ensure consistent login experience.

password.description:
Administrator's password for authentication verification.

Provided as plain text in the request and verified against the hashed password stored in the shopping_mall_admins table using secure password hashing algorithms.

The backend handles password hashing and comparison. Client applications should transmit this over HTTPS to ensure security during transit.

Failed authentication attempts are tracked for security monitoring and brute-force attack prevention.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking and security audit trails.

This optional field captures the IP address from which the admin is logging in. While the server can extract this from the request headers, clients may provide it explicitly for cases like server-side rendering or proxy scenarios.

The IP address is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table as part of the session record for security monitoring, geographic analysis, and suspicious activity detection.

Accepts both IPv4 and IPv6 address formats. When not provided, the server will extract it from request headers.

href.description:
Current page URL where the login is being performed.

This required field captures the complete URL of the page from which the administrator initiated the login request. It is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table for session context tracking and audit purposes.

Useful for understanding admin login patterns, detecting anomalies, and providing context for security investigations. The URL should include protocol, domain, path, and query parameters.

Example: https://admin.example.com/login or https://admin.example.com/dashboard

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the page from which the admin navigated to the login page.

This required field captures the URL of the previous page before reaching the login page. It is stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table for session tracking and navigation flow analysis.

Helps understand how administrators access the login page (direct access, from marketing pages, from password reset flows, etc.). Can be an empty string for direct navigation to the login page.

Example: https://admin.example.com/home or empty string for direct access

IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin.description:
Administrator login credentials including email, password, and session context information.

This request body contains all information needed to authenticate an existing administrator account. The email and password are verified against stored credentials in the shopping_mall_admins table.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are captured for security audit trails and are stored in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table. These fields enable tracking of login attempts, detection of suspicious activity, and investigation of security incidents.

The href and referrer fields are required to maintain complete session audit trails, while the ip field is optional as the server can extract it from request headers when not provided.

refresh_token.description:
Valid JWT refresh token issued during previous authentication.

This token was provided in the IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized response from a successful login or join operation. It is a signed JWT containing the administrator's session identifier and identity claims.

The refresh token has a longer lifespan than access tokens (typically hours or days vs minutes) and is used to obtain new access tokens without requiring credential re-entry. The system validates this token against the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table to ensure the session is still active and not revoked.

Refresh tokens are single-use in token rotation scenarios, where presenting a refresh token issues both a new access token and a new refresh token, invalidating the old refresh token for enhanced security.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for obtaining new JWT access tokens.

This request body contains the refresh token that was previously issued during authentication. The token is validated against active admin sessions to ensure it remains valid and has not been revoked.

The refresh operation enables continuous authenticated sessions without requiring administrators to re-enter their credentials, balancing security (short-lived access tokens) with user experience (long-lived refresh tokens).

Successful refresh operations may implement token rotation, issuing both new access and refresh tokens while invalidating the presented refresh token.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the authenticated administrator.

This UUID corresponds to the primary key in the shopping_mall_admins table and uniquely identifies the admin account across the entire platform.

Clients should store this identifier to associate subsequent actions with the authenticated admin. It is included in JWT token claims and used for authorization checks and audit logging.

email.description:
Admin email address used for authentication and platform notifications.

Must be unique across all admin accounts. Serves as the primary identifier for secure admin access and system communications.

full_name.description:
Admin user full name for identification and audit logging.

Used in admin action records, accountability tracking, and internal communications. Provides clear identification of which administrator performed specific actions.

phone_number.description:
Admin contact phone number for two-factor authentication and emergency contact.

Required for all admin accounts to enable SMS-based 2FA verification. Critical security component ensuring authorized access to administrative functions.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Authenticated administrator account information with issued JWT tokens.

This response is returned after successful authentication (login) or token refresh operations. It provides the administrator's unique identifier and the JWT tokens needed to access protected platform resources.

The response enables the client application to:
1. Identify the authenticated administrator (via id)
2. Authorize subsequent API requests (via access token in Authorization header)
3. Maintain session continuity (via refresh token for obtaining new access tokens)

Clients should securely store these tokens (preferably in HTTP-only cookies or secure storage) and implement token refresh logic before access token expiration.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the system configuration record.

Automatically generated UUID that serves as the primary key for this configuration entry.
This ID is immutable and used for direct record lookups and relationships.

config_key.description:
Unique configuration key identifier used to reference specific platform settings.

This key follows a naming convention and must be unique across all system configurations.
Examples include 'platform_name', 'default_commission_rate', 'max_product_images', 'free_shipping_threshold'.

The key serves as the human-readable identifier for retrieving and updating configuration values throughout the platform.

config_value.description:
Configuration value stored as a string.

Values can represent different data types (numbers, booleans, JSON objects) serialized as strings.
The actual data type is indicated by the value_type field.

For boolean values, use 'true' or 'false' strings.
For numeric values, store as decimal strings (e.g., '15.5').
For complex objects, store as JSON-encoded strings.

value_type.description:
Data type indicator for the configuration value to assist with proper parsing and validation.

Valid values include: 'string', 'integer', 'decimal', 'boolean', 'json', 'url'.
Helps the application layer interpret the config_value correctly and apply appropriate type conversions.

This metadata ensures type safety when consuming configuration values throughout the platform.

description.description:
Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

Provides comprehensive context for administrators to understand what this configuration controls and the impact of changing its value.
Should include valid value examples, constraints, and any platform-wide effects of modifications.

This field is required to ensure all configurations are properly documented for maintainability.

category.description:
Configuration category for organizational grouping.

Examples: 'payment', 'shipping', 'email', 'platform', 'commission', 'features', 'security'.
Enables filtering and organizing configurations by functional area in admin interfaces.

Categorization helps administrators locate related settings and understand the scope of configuration changes.

status.description:
Current operational status of the configuration setting.

Valid values: 'active' (configuration is in use), 'inactive' (configuration is disabled but preserved).
Allows temporary disabling of configurations without permanent deletion, supporting testing and rollback scenarios.

Status changes are audit-logged through the updated_at timestamp.

is_sensitive.description:
Flag indicating whether this configuration contains sensitive data.

When true, the configuration value contains sensitive information such as API keys, passwords, or credentials.
Sensitive configurations should be encrypted at rest and masked in admin interfaces for security.

This flag triggers special handling in the application layer to protect confidential platform settings.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was first created.

Automatically set by the database upon record insertion.
Follows ISO 8601 date-time format for consistency.

Used for audit trails and tracking when settings were introduced to the platform.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

Automatically updated by the database whenever config_value, status, or other fields are changed.
Follows ISO 8601 date-time format for consistency.

Essential for tracking configuration change history, cache invalidation, and troubleshooting.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp indicating when the configuration was marked as deleted.

When not null, this configuration has been soft-deleted but is preserved for audit trails and potential recovery.
Deleted configurations are filtered from active configuration lookups but remain in the database.

Supports safe deletion with the ability to restore configurations if needed.

IShoppingMallSystemConfig.description:
Platform-wide system configuration entity representing key-value settings that control core platform behavior and features.

This entity stores foundational configuration parameters used throughout the e-commerce shopping mall platform including business settings, operational parameters, feature flags, and integration configurations.
Each configuration is identified by a unique key and stores its value as a string along with metadata describing the value type, purpose, category, and sensitivity level.

System configurations are managed exclusively by administrators through secure interfaces.
Changes to configurations are audit-logged with timestamps to track when settings were modified.
Configurations can be activated or deactivated using the status field without permanent deletion, allowing temporary feature disabling.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain configuration history and allow recovery of accidentally deleted settings.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the system configuration record.

Primary key used for direct lookups and references in list views.

config_key.description:
Unique configuration key identifier used to reference specific platform settings.

Provides the human-readable key for identifying configurations in summary lists and dropdowns.

config_value.description:
Configuration value stored as a string.

Displays the current value of the configuration setting in summary views.

value_type.description:
Data type indicator for the configuration value.

Helps administrators understand how to interpret the config_value in list displays.
Examples: 'string', 'integer', 'boolean', 'json'.

category.description:
Configuration category for organizational grouping.

Enables filtering and grouping of configurations by functional area in list views.
Examples: 'payment', 'shipping', 'email', 'platform'.

status.description:
Current operational status of the configuration setting.

Indicates whether the configuration is 'active' (in effect) or 'inactive' (disabled).
Important for administrators to see which settings are currently applied.

IShoppingMallSystemConfig.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary representation of system configuration for list views and embedded references.

Provides essential configuration information including key, value, type, category, and status without verbose descriptions or detailed metadata.
Optimized for display in configuration lists, admin dashboards, and quick reference scenarios.

Excludes detailed description field, sensitivity flag, and timestamps to reduce payload size in list operations while retaining all information needed for effective configuration management.

config_key.description:
Unique configuration key identifier used to reference this setting throughout the platform.

This key must be unique across all system configurations and follows a naming convention for consistency. Common examples include 'platform_name', 'default_commission_rate', 'max_product_images', 'free_shipping_threshold', 'email_smtp_host', 'payment_gateway_mode'.

The key serves as the primary reference for retrieving and managing this configuration value throughout the application. Choose descriptive, consistent naming that clearly indicates the setting's purpose.

config_value.description:
Configuration value stored as string representation.

This field stores the actual setting value in string format, regardless of the underlying data type. The value_type field indicates how this string should be interpreted and parsed.

For boolean values, use 'true' or 'false' strings. For numeric values, store as decimal strings (e.g., '15.5' for percentages, '100' for limits). For complex objects or arrays, store as JSON-encoded strings. For URLs, store the complete URL string. This flexible string-based storage allows any configuration type while maintaining consistent database schema.

value_type.description:
Data type indicator for the configuration value to assist with proper parsing and validation.

Specifies how the config_value string should be interpreted by the application layer. Valid values include: 'string' for text values, 'integer' for whole numbers, 'decimal' for floating-point numbers, 'boolean' for true/false flags, 'json' for complex objects or arrays, 'url' for web addresses.

This metadata ensures type safety and correct parsing when consuming configuration values throughout the platform. The application can use this field to apply appropriate type conversions and validations.

description.description:
Human-readable description explaining the purpose and usage of this configuration setting.

Provide a comprehensive explanation of what this configuration controls, its impact on platform behavior, valid value formats, acceptable ranges or options, and any important constraints or side effects.

This documentation is essential for future administrators to understand the configuration's purpose and safely modify values. Include examples of valid values and explain the consequences of different settings. This field is required to ensure all configurations are properly documented for long-term maintainability.

Assign this configuration to a functional category to enable filtering and logical organization in admin interfaces. Valid categories include: 'payment' for payment gateway and transaction settings, 'shipping' for delivery and logistics configurations, 'email' for email service and notification settings, 'platform' for general platform behavior, 'commission' for fee and commission rate settings, 'features' for feature flags and toggles, 'security' for authentication and authorization settings.

Proper categorization helps administrators locate related settings and understand the functional scope of configuration changes.

Active configurations are applied to platform behavior immediately. Inactive configurations are preserved in the database but not used by the application, allowing preparation of settings before deployment or temporary disabling without deletion.

Only administrators with appropriate security clearance should view or modify sensitive configurations. This flag triggers enhanced security measures throughout the configuration lifecycle.

IShoppingMallSystemConfig.ICreate.description:
Configuration creation request data for adding new platform system settings.

Used when administrators need to introduce new configuration parameters that control platform-wide behavior, features, or integrations. All fields are required to ensure complete and well-documented configuration entries.

Common creation scenarios include adding new payment gateway credentials, defining new commission rate structures, establishing email service configurations, creating feature flags for A/B testing, or setting up integration parameters for third-party services.

The config_key must be unique across all configurations and follow consistent naming conventions. The config_value stores the actual setting in string format with value_type indicating the data type. Comprehensive descriptions are mandatory to ensure future administrators understand each configuration's purpose and impact.

System-managed fields like id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are automatically generated and should not be included in creation requests. The status field allows configurations to be created in either active or inactive state, supporting staged deployment workflows.

config_value.description:

This metadata ensures type safety and correct parsing when consuming configuration values throughout the platform. The application can use this field to apply appropriate type conversions and validations. When updating config_value, ensure value_type is updated accordingly to maintain data integrity.

System-managed timestamp fields (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are automatically maintained by the database and should not be included in update requests. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set to the current time when any field is modified.

When updating config_value, ensure the value_type field is also updated if the data type changes to maintain consistency. Status changes between 'active' and 'inactive' allow temporary configuration disabling without deletion, supporting safe testing and rollback scenarios.

id.description:

Primary key for the shopping_mall_buyers table, automatically generated as a UUID upon account creation. This identifier remains immutable throughout the account lifecycle and is used to reference the buyer across all related entities including orders, reviews, cart items, and sessions.

email.description:
Buyer email address used for authentication and communication.

Must be unique across all buyer accounts in the marketplace. Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards to ensure deliverability. Serves as the primary login credential and is used for order notifications, shipping updates, promotional communications, and account recovery.

This field is indexed in the database for efficient lookup during authentication and search operations.

full_name.description:
Buyer full name for personalization and order fulfillment.

Displayed in order confirmations and shipping labels to ensure proper delivery. Used throughout the platform for personalized greetings and customer service interactions. This is a required field with a minimum of 2 characters and maximum of 100 characters as defined in the Prisma schema.

The full name should be the buyer's real name for delivery coordination and legal compliance purposes.

phone_number.description:
Buyer contact phone number with country code.

Optional during registration but recommended for order delivery coordination and customer support. When provided, should include the country code for international format compatibility. Used for SMS notifications about order status updates and delivery scheduling.

Can be null if the buyer chooses not to provide a phone number during registration or profile updates.

email_verified.description:
Email verification status indicating whether the buyer has confirmed ownership of the email address.

Unverified accounts have restricted capabilities including inability to place orders or access certain platform features. Buyers must verify their email through a confirmation link sent during registration to activate full account functionality.

This flag is automatically set to false upon account creation and updated to true when the buyer clicks the verification link. Critical for preventing fraudulent registrations and ensuring communication deliverability.

created_at.description:
Account creation timestamp recording when the buyer registered on the platform.

Automatically set by the system upon successful registration and never modified thereafter. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format for international compatibility. Used for user analytics, account age verification, and determining eligibility for time-based promotions or features.

This field enables lifecycle analysis such as customer retention metrics and cohort analysis.

updated_at.description:
Last modification timestamp recording when buyer profile information was last updated.

Automatically updated by the system on any profile changes including name updates, phone number modifications, or email changes. Follows ISO 8601 date-time format. Used for tracking account activity, security monitoring, and determining data freshness for cache invalidation.

This timestamp helps identify stale accounts and supports audit trail requirements.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for account deactivation.

When set, the account is considered deactivated and login is prevented while preserving historical data for order history, reviews, and analytics. Implements soft-delete pattern to maintain referential integrity across the system.

Accounts can be reactivated within 90 days by clearing this field through administrative action. After 90 days, accounts may be permanently deleted according to data retention policies and privacy regulations.

IShoppingMallBuyer.description:
Authenticated customer account entity representing buyers in the marketplace.

Buyer accounts are the primary demand-side actors who browse products, make purchases, and interact with sellers through reviews and questions. Each buyer account requires email verification to access full platform features including shopping cart, order placement, and product reviews.

Buyers maintain independent relationships with their orders, cart items, wishlist items, saved addresses, payment methods, and reviews. Account lifecycle includes active and soft-deleted states for proper user management and compliance with data protection regulations.

The system tracks buyer registration, authentication history through sessions, and maintains profile information for personalized shopping experiences. All authentication-related fields like password_hash are excluded from API responses for security.

Password changes must be performed through dedicated password reset endpoints with proper verification.

When set to true, returns only currently active sessions (not expired). When set to false, returns only expired sessions. When null or omitted, returns all sessions regardless of status. This filter is useful for session management and security monitoring.

IShoppingMallBuyerSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying buyer authentication sessions.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities for retrieving buyer session records. It enables administrators to conduct security audits, monitor active sessions, and investigate authentication patterns.

Pagination parameters (page, limit) control result set size and navigation through large session histories. Sort parameters (sort_by, order) determine the ordering of results based on temporal fields. Filter parameters enable targeted searches based on session characteristics such as creation time, IP address, connection context, and activity status.

Security considerations: This operation is restricted to administrator actors only, as session data contains sensitive security information. The IP address filter supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats. Date range filters support ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information for precise temporal filtering.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction from broad searches (all sessions) to highly specific investigations (sessions from a specific IP within a time window from a particular referrer).

IShoppingMallBuyerSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a buyer authentication session.

Provides essential session information for identifying and tracking buyer login sessions. Used in contexts where complete session details are not required, such as embedded references in other entities or list views.

Contains the necessary fields to identify a session, understand its origin and traffic source, and determine its current status without the overhead of full session data.

Unique identifier of the buyer session.

Primary key used to reference this specific authentication session across the system. Generated automatically upon session creation and remains immutable throughout the session lifecycle.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the authenticated buyer.

Links this session to the specific buyer account that established the authenticated connection. This association enables tracking all sessions belonging to a particular buyer for security monitoring and multi-session management.

ip.description:
IP address from which the buyer authenticated.

Captures the client's IP address at the time of session creation for security auditing, fraud detection, and geographic analysis. Can be either IPv4 or IPv6 format.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the platform entry point for this session.

Tracks which page or service the buyer accessed when establishing their authentication session. This information is valuable for understanding user navigation patterns, identifying popular entry points, and detecting potential security issues related to specific URLs.

The href field provides context about how buyers interact with the platform and can reveal insights into user behavior, marketing campaign effectiveness, and potential vulnerabilities in specific platform features.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the source that directed the buyer to the platform.

Captures the external URL from which the buyer arrived before creating their session. This data is essential for marketing attribution, tracking traffic sources, detecting suspicious referral patterns, and analyzing the effectiveness of external partnerships or advertising campaigns.

The referrer field helps administrators understand acquisition channels and identify potential phishing attempts or unauthorized traffic sources that may pose security risks.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created.

Records the exact moment the buyer successfully authenticated and the session was established. Used for session age calculations, activity tracking, and audit trail purposes. Follows ISO 8601 format.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp indicating when the buyer logged out or the session was terminated.

When null, indicates the session is still active. When populated with a timestamp, indicates the exact moment the session ended either through explicit logout, administrative termination, or automatic expiration. This field is critical for distinguishing active sessions from expired ones and for calculating session duration.

Administrators use this field to monitor session lifecycles, identify abnormally long sessions that may indicate security issues, and maintain accurate records of user activity periods for audit and compliance purposes.

IShoppingMallBuyerSession.description:
Complete buyer authentication session record representing an active or historical login session for a buyer account in the shopping mall marketplace.

This schema captures comprehensive session information including authentication timestamps, JWT token details, IP address, browser information, and session lifecycle metadata. Sessions are created upon successful buyer login and track the buyer's authenticated state throughout their interaction with the platform.

The session entity serves critical security functions including session validation, concurrent login management, forced logout capabilities, and security audit trails. Each session maintains its own JWT token with configurable expiration times and refresh capabilities.

Sessions reference their parent buyer account and maintain authentication context necessary for authorization decisions. The session tracks both creation time and last activity time to support idle timeout policies and activity monitoring.

This schema is used in session retrieval responses, session management interfaces, and security monitoring dashboards. It includes all session attributes necessary for session validation, renewal decisions, and comprehensive security audit trails.

Generated automatically upon session creation and used to reference this specific session throughout its lifecycle.

Links this session to the authenticated buyer account and is used for session ownership verification and access control checks.

ip.description:
IP address from which the buyer authenticated and established this session.

Captures the network origin of the authentication request for security monitoring, fraud detection, and geographic analysis. Can be IPv4 or IPv6 format.

href.description:
Connection URL representing the page or endpoint where the authentication occurred.

Records the specific platform URL accessed during session establishment, useful for understanding authentication flow paths and user behavior analysis.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the page or source that directed the buyer to the authentication endpoint.

Captures marketing attribution data and helps track authentication flow origins. May be empty for direct navigation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this authentication session was initially created and the buyer successfully logged in.

Records the exact moment of session establishment in ISO 8601 format. Used for session age calculation, expiration enforcement, and audit trail purposes.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp indicating when the buyer logged out or the session was terminated.

This field is null for active sessions that are currently valid and in use. When set, it records the exact moment the session ended, whether through explicit logout, forced termination by administrators, token expiration, or security-triggered invalidation.

The expired_at timestamp is critical for session lifecycle management, enabling the system to distinguish between active and terminated sessions. It supports security audit trails by providing complete session duration information and helps enforce session cleanup policies by identifying sessions that should be archived or purged from active session stores.
