IShoppingMallSeller.description:
Complete seller account entity representing a merchant in the shopping mall marketplace.

This entity contains all information about a seller's account including authentication credentials, business details, approval status, and account lifecycle timestamps. Sellers are authenticated users who can list products, manage inventory, fulfill orders, and operate their virtual storefront within the marketplace platform.

The seller entity supports the complete seller lifecycle from initial registration through approval workflow to active selling operations. Each seller account undergoes administrative review before being approved to sell on the platform, ensuring marketplace quality and compliance with business policies. The status field tracks the approval workflow with values: pending (awaiting review), approved (active seller), rejected (application denied), or suspended (temporarily restricted).

Security considerations include password hashing (password_hash field stored in database but never exposed in API responses), role-based access control, and session management. Sellers can only access and modify their own account information and products. Administrative operations such as status changes require admin-level permissions.

This entity maps directly to the shopping_mall_sellers table in the Prisma database schema and is central to all seller-related operations including product management, order fulfillment, and seller analytics. All field names and types correspond exactly to the Prisma schema definition to ensure data consistency and type safety.

email.description:
Updated email address for seller authentication and communication.

Changing the email address updates the primary login credential and communication channel for the seller account. The new email must be unique across all seller accounts and will be verified before the change takes effect.

password.description:
New password for seller account authentication.

Provides the plain text password that will be securely hashed before storage. Used when the seller wants to change their account password for security reasons. The password will be validated against security requirements before being accepted.

full_name.description:
Updated seller contact person full name.

Allows modification of the seller contact person full name used for business correspondence and account verification. This may represent the business owner or authorized representative and is used for official communications and account management.

phone_number.description:
Updated business contact phone number with country code.

Allows sellers to modify their business contact phone number used for direct communication regarding order fulfillment and customer service. The updated phone number should include the country code to ensure proper international contact capability.

business_name.description:
Updated legal business name or DBA (Doing Business As) name.

Allows modification of the legal business name used for official documentation, tax purposes, and business verification. Changes to the business name may trigger re-verification workflows to ensure compliance with marketplace policies. The business name must be between 2 and 200 characters.

business_description.description:
Updated business overview describing the seller store and brand identity.

Allows sellers to modify the business description that appears on their store page to help buyers understand their business, product focus, and brand identity. The updated description is displayed throughout the platform and should accurately represent the seller's marketplace presence. Maximum 2000 characters.

store_name.description:
Updated public display name of the seller's store.

Changing the store name updates how the seller's business appears to buyers throughout the marketplace. The new store name should be unique and recognizable, representing the seller's brand identity.

oneOf.description:
Updated seller account approval and operational status.

Allows modification of the seller account status within the approval workflow. Valid values include: pending (awaiting admin approval), approved (active seller with full access), rejected (application denied), suspended (temporarily restricted). Determines seller capabilities and product visibility throughout the marketplace.

Status changes are typically performed by administrators as part of the seller approval workflow or account management processes. Changing status to approved grants full marketplace access including product listing capabilities. Setting status to rejected or suspended restricts seller operations and may hide existing product listings.

IShoppingMallSeller.IUpdate.description:
Update request for seller account information and profile settings.

This DTO contains the fields that sellers can modify in their own account. All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to specific account attributes. Sellers can update their business information, contact details, and authentication credentials through this operation.

Security considerations ensure that sellers can only update their own accounts, verified through JWT authentication. The seller_id from the authentication token must match the seller_id in the URL path parameter. Certain critical fields such as email_verified and system timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are immutable and cannot be modified by sellers.

Password changes require the new password to meet security requirements including minimum length and complexity rules. The provided plain text password will be securely hashed using bcrypt before storage.

This DTO maps to update operations on the shopping_mall_sellers table in the Prisma database schema. The updated_at timestamp is automatically set by the system when any field is modified.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this seller authentication session.

Generated automatically upon session creation when a seller successfully authenticates to the platform.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller who created this authentication session.

Links this session record to the authenticated seller account. References shopping_mall_sellers.id.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller who owns this authentication session.

Provides essential seller identification context including seller name and basic profile information for session tracking and audit purposes.

ip.description:
IP address from which the seller authenticated to the platform.

Used for security monitoring, fraud detection, geographic access analysis, and identifying suspicious login patterns. Critical for forensic investigations and compliance requirements.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the platform entry point for this authentication session.

Tracks which page or service the seller accessed when logging in. Useful for understanding seller behavior and optimizing platform navigation.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the source that directed the seller to the platform.

Used for marketing attribution analysis, traffic source tracking, and understanding how sellers discover and access the marketplace.

created_at.description:
Session creation timestamp recording when the seller successfully authenticated.

Marks the exact moment the authentication session began. Used for session duration calculation, activity timeline analysis, and security monitoring.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp indicating when the seller logged out or the session was terminated.

Null for currently active sessions. When set, indicates the session has ended either through explicit logout, forced termination, or timeout expiration.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.description:
Complete seller authentication session record with full session details and seller context.

Represents a single authentication event when a seller logs into the platform. Contains comprehensive session metadata including connection context (IP address, access URL, referrer) for security monitoring, fraud detection, and business activity analysis.

Sessions track the complete lifecycle from authentication through expiration or logout. Multiple concurrent sessions are supported for multi-device access and team collaboration scenarios.

This entity provides critical audit trail data for detecting suspicious login patterns, monitoring unauthorized access attempts, analyzing seller activity, and supporting forensic investigations for security incidents and compliance requirements.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this seller authentication session.

This UUID serves as the unique identifier for each authentication session record in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table.

seller.description:

Provides essential seller identification for quick reference in session lists and audit logs. References the shopping_mall_sellers table through the shopping_mall_seller_id foreign key relationship.

ip.description:
IP address from which the seller authenticated.

Used for security monitoring and geographic access analysis. Key identifier for detecting suspicious login patterns and unauthorized access attempts from unusual locations.

href.description:

Tracks which page or service the seller accessed when authenticating. Essential for understanding user navigation patterns and platform entry points in session analysis.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the source that directed the seller to the platform.

Used for marketing attribution and traffic source analysis. Helps identify how sellers discover and access the platform, supporting marketing effectiveness measurement.

Indicates when this authentication session began. Primary sorting field for session history displays and temporal analysis of login patterns.

expired_at.description:

Null for active sessions, timestamp for terminated sessions. Quick indicator of session status enabling rapid identification of active versus historical sessions in security monitoring.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary.description:
Lightweight seller session representation for lists and session history displays.

Optimized summary view containing essential session identification and status information including connection context. Provides complete session metadata for security auditing and session management interfaces.

Used in session management dashboards, security monitoring interfaces, and multi-session views where sellers review their active and past authentication sessions.

IShoppingMallSellerSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying seller authentication sessions with pagination support.

This schema defines the request body for session search operations, providing comprehensive filtering capabilities to find sessions based on various criteria including creation date ranges, expiration date ranges, IP addresses, connection URLs, referrer sources, and seller identification. Supports pagination to handle large session histories efficiently.

Used in session list and search endpoints to enable sellers and administrators to locate specific sessions, audit authentication activity, monitor for security anomalies, and analyze traffic sources. The flexible filtering options support use cases ranging from finding recent logins to investigating historical access patterns and marketing attribution analysis.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to return. Defaults to 1 if not provided. Used in conjunction with limit to implement cursor-free pagination for session lists.

limit.description:
Number of sessions to return per page.

Controls page size for pagination. Maximum value enforced to prevent excessive payload sizes. Typical values range from 10 to 50 for session management interfaces.

sort.description:
Array of sort specifications in format 'field' or '-field' for descending order.

Allows sorting results by session fields such as 'created_at', '-created_at' (newest first), 'expired_at', 'ip'. Multiple sort criteria can be specified with priority given to earlier entries in the array.

search.description:
General search term for finding sessions across multiple fields.

Performs partial matching against IP addresses, href URLs, and referrer URLs. Useful for quick searches when users know part of the information they're looking for but not the specific field.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Filter sessions by specific seller account identifier.

Finds all sessions belonging to a particular seller. Primarily used by administrators for cross-seller security monitoring and seller-specific session auditing. Enables investigation of authentication patterns for individual merchant accounts.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by exact IP address match.

Finds all sessions originating from a specific IP address. Useful for security investigations when suspicious activity is detected from a particular IP or for verifying legitimate access from known locations.

href.description:
Filter sessions by connection URL platform entry point.

Finds sessions based on which page or service the seller accessed during authentication. Useful for analyzing navigation patterns, identifying common entry points, and tracking usage of different platform features.

referrer.description:
Filter sessions by referrer URL traffic source.

Finds sessions based on the source that directed sellers to the platform. Essential for marketing attribution analysis, traffic source tracking, and understanding how sellers discover the marketplace.

created_at_after.description:
Filter sessions created after this timestamp (inclusive).

ISO 8601 format timestamp for range-based filtering. Combine with created_at_before to search sessions within a specific time window. Useful for auditing login activity during specific time periods.

created_at_before.description:
Filter sessions created before this timestamp (inclusive).

ISO 8601 format timestamp for range-based filtering. Combine with created_at_after to search sessions within a specific time window. Useful for identifying stale sessions or analyzing historical authentication patterns.

expired_at_after.description:
Filter sessions that expired after this timestamp (inclusive).

ISO 8601 format timestamp for range-based filtering. Combine with expired_at_before to find sessions terminated within a specific time window. Useful for analyzing logout patterns and session lifecycle management.

expired_at_before.description:
Filter sessions that expired before this timestamp (inclusive).

ISO 8601 format timestamp for range-based filtering. Combine with expired_at_after to search terminated sessions within a specific period. Useful for identifying long-running sessions or analyzing session duration patterns.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Update request body for modifying existing administrator account information.

This DTO contains fields that can be modified after an admin account has been created. All fields are optional, following the partial update pattern where only specified fields are modified. Fields correspond directly to editable columns in the shopping_mall_admins Prisma schema table.

Security considerations: Password updates are excluded from this general update DTO and must be handled through dedicated password change endpoints with proper authentication and validation. Sensitive fields such as password_hash and internal security tokens are never accepted in update requests. The admin ID is excluded as it comes from the path parameter, preventing attempts to modify the account identifier. System-managed fields like created_at and updated_at are excluded as they are automatically maintained by the database.

Ownership and authorization: Only administrators with appropriate permissions can modify admin accounts. The operation validates that the authenticated admin has rights to perform the update. Changes to critical fields such as email or admin_level may trigger additional security verification steps and audit log entries.

page.description:
Page number for pagination.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated admin list. Page numbering starts at 1. Used in conjunction with limit to control result set size and navigation.

limit.description:
Maximum number of admin records per page.

Controls the page size in paginated results. Accepts values between 1 and 100 to balance performance and usability. Default limit is typically 20 if not specified.

search.description:
General search query for filtering administrators.

Searches across multiple admin fields including email, full_name, and phone_number using partial matching. Useful for quickly finding specific administrators without knowing exact field values.

Used to view admins with specific permission scopes.

IShoppingMallAdmin.IRequest.description:

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for retrieving paginated lists of platform administrators from the shopping_mall_admins Prisma schema. Supports multiple filter criteria that can be combined to narrow down results, including text search, admin_level filtering, status filtering, and date range filtering.

Pagination parameters (page and limit) control result set size and navigation. Sorting parameters (sort_by and order) allow customization of result ordering based on Prisma schema fields. All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction based on specific administrative needs.

Filter fields directly correspond to shopping_mall_admins table columns: email, admin_level (privilege level), created_at (account creation timestamp), and deleted_at (soft-delete status). The search parameter provides flexible text matching across multiple fields for rapid administrator lookup.

Used to navigate through multiple pages of session records.
Combined with limit to implement efficient pagination for large session histories.
Defaults to 1 if not specified, showing the first page of results.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination to manage response payload size.
Typically set between 10-50 for optimal performance and usability.
Maximum limit enforced at 100 to prevent excessive data transfer and performance issues.

search.description:

Supports partial matching to find sessions with specific characteristics.
Useful for quickly locating sessions from particular locations or with specific connection context.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by specific IP address or IP address pattern.

Critical for security investigations when suspicious access patterns are detected from certain IP ranges.

Filter for expired or terminated admin sessions.

Returns only sessions where expired_at is set in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions Prisma schema, indicating the session has ended through logout, timeout, or administrative termination. Used for historical session analysis and audit trails.

Active sessions have null expired_at (admin still logged in), while expired sessions have a timestamp indicating when the session ended. Essential for security monitoring to distinguish between current and historical sessions.

created_after.description:
Filter sessions created after this timestamp (inclusive).

ISO 8601 format date-time string for precise temporal filtering based on the created_at field in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions Prisma schema.
Used in combination with created_before to define date ranges for session queries.
Helpful for analyzing login activity during specific time periods or investigating security incidents within a timeframe.

created_before.description:

ISO 8601 format date-time string for precise temporal filtering based on the created_at field in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions Prisma schema.
Used in combination with created_after to define date ranges for session queries.
Enables administrators to focus on historical sessions or recent activity as needed.

sort_by.description:

Sorts sessions by their creation timestamp (created_at field from shopping_mall_admin_sessions Prisma schema) to show sessions in chronological order.
This is the only sortable timestamp field available in the session schema.
Defaults to descending order (newest first) when combined with sort_order parameter.

oneOf.description:

Controls whether results are ordered in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) sequence.
Descending order is most common for session monitoring to see recent activity first.
Ascending order useful for historical analysis starting from earliest sessions.

Ascending order useful for historical analysis starting from earliest sessions.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the selected sort field.

Controls whether results are ordered in ascending (oldest first) or descending (newest first) sequence.
Descending order is most common for session monitoring to see recent activity first.
Ascending order useful for historical analysis starting from earliest sessions.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating administrator session records.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for retrieving admin session data from the shopping_mall_admin_sessions Prisma schema, essential for security monitoring, audit compliance, and access pattern analysis.
Administrators can search and filter sessions by various criteria to identify suspicious activity, track concurrent logins, or generate audit reports.

Pagination controls: The page and limit parameters enable efficient navigation through potentially large session histories without overwhelming the client or server.
Default pagination behavior returns the most recent sessions first, with configurable page size to balance between data completeness and performance.

Temporal filtering: Date range filtering through created_after and created_before parameters allows administrators to focus on specific time periods based on the created_at timestamp field.
This is critical for security incident investigation where administrators need to examine login activity during suspicious timeframes.
Temporal filters support compliance requirements for session audit trail retention and reporting.

Search and filter capabilities: The search parameter provides quick filtering across multiple session attributes including IP addresses, connection URLs (href), and referrer information for rapid investigation.
IP address filtering enables identification of all sessions from specific locations or networks, crucial for detecting unauthorized access attempts or geographic anomalies.
Session status filtering (active vs expired) based on the expired_at field allows administrators to distinguish between current active sessions and historical terminated sessions.
Filter parameters can be combined to create precise queries such as "all active sessions from IP X created in the last 24 hours."

Sorting options: Sessions are sorted by their creation timestamp (created_at), the primary temporal field in the shopping_mall_admin_sessions schema.
Sorting direction (ascending or descending) can be controlled via the sort_order parameter to view sessions in different analytical contexts.

Security and audit context: This request DTO is designed to support comprehensive session monitoring and audit trail analysis based on actual Prisma schema fields (ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at).
The filtering capabilities enable administrators to quickly respond to security events by identifying affected sessions and login patterns.
All query parameters are optional, with sensible defaults to provide useful results even with minimal filtering criteria.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of admin authentication session for lightweight display in lists and references.

Represents an active or historical login session for an admin user, tracking authentication state and connection metadata. Used for session management, security auditing, and displaying admin login history.

This summary variant excludes connection URLs and focuses on essential session identification and status information for efficient list rendering and reference displays.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this admin session record.

Primary key that distinguishes this session from all other admin authentication sessions in the system.

admin.description:
Reference to the authenticated admin account that owns this session.

Provides context about which administrator this session belongs to, including their identity and basic profile information.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin authenticated.

Captured during login for security auditing and suspicious activity detection. Used to identify login locations and detect unauthorized access patterns.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this admin session was established.

Records the exact moment of successful authentication, used for session duration tracking and security audit trails.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp indicating when the admin logged out or the session was terminated.

Null for active sessions. When set, indicates the session has ended either through explicit logout or administrative termination.

IShoppingMallAdminSession.description:
Complete admin authentication session record from the shopping_mall_admin_sessions table.

Represents a single authentication session for an administrator account, tracking login timestamps, IP address, connection context, and session status. Each session record tracks a distinct login instance for an admin user, enabling session management, security auditing, and access control.

Sessions are created when administrators successfully authenticate and are terminated when they explicitly log out (expired_at is set). The session record contains all metadata necessary for tracking admin activity and maintaining audit trails.

Used in session retrieval operations (read), session termination operations (delete), and administrative security audit interfaces.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the admin session record.

Primary key for the session record, automatically generated by the system when a new session is created during admin authentication. This identifier is used to reference specific sessions in session management operations.

admin.description:
Reference to the authenticated admin account that owns this session.

Provides complete admin context including identity, privilege level, and basic profile information. This transformed foreign key reference (from shopping_mall_admin_id in the Prisma schema) enables clients to display full session details without additional API calls to fetch admin information.

Each session belongs to exactly one admin account, and admins can have multiple active sessions simultaneously across different devices or browsers.

ip.description:
IP address from which the admin authenticated.

Records the client IP address used during the login process for security auditing and suspicious activity detection. This field helps identify login locations and detect unauthorized access attempts from unusual IP addresses.

href.description:
Connection URL indicating the platform entry point for this admin session.

Tracks which admin interface or service was accessed during authentication. This metadata provides context about the authentication flow and is useful for security analysis and access pattern tracking.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL indicating the source that directed the admin to the platform.

Used for access pattern analysis and security auditing. Helps understand how administrators are navigating to the authentication interface and can identify unusual referrer patterns that may indicate security issues.

created_at.description:
Session creation timestamp recording when the admin successfully authenticated and the session began.

Critical for audit trails and compliance reporting. This timestamp marks the beginning of the session and is used to calculate session duration and analyze login patterns.

expired_at.description:
Session expiration timestamp indicating when the admin logged out or the session was terminated.

Null for active sessions that are still in use. When set, indicates the session has ended either through explicit logout or administrative termination. Used to track session duration and detect abandoned sessions.

IShoppingMallCategory.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving product categories.

Defines the complete set of query parameters for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating category lists in the shopping mall marketplace. This request type supports both simple category browsing and advanced hierarchical navigation through the category taxonomy.

The request structure enables flexible category discovery including name-based search, parent category filtering for hierarchical navigation, status filtering, and custom sorting options. Pagination parameters allow efficient retrieval of large category datasets.

Used in category list operations including top-level category browsing, subcategory navigation, and administrative category management interfaces. The parameters work together to provide comprehensive category querying capabilities for building navigation menus, product filters, and category management tools.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the complete category dataset. Page numbers are 1-indexed, where page 1 represents the first set of results. This parameter works in conjunction with limit to implement efficient pagination.

limit.description:
Number of categories to return per page.

Defines the page size for pagination, controlling how many category records are included in a single response. This parameter enables clients to balance between fewer requests with larger payloads and more requests with smaller payloads. The maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive data transfer in a single request.

search.description:
Search query string for filtering categories by name.

Enables text-based search across category names to help users find specific categories quickly. The search typically performs case-insensitive partial matching, allowing users to find categories using incomplete names or keywords. This parameter is essential for category discovery in large taxonomies.

parent_id.description:
Filter categories by parent category identifier for hierarchical navigation.

When provided as a UUID, retrieves only the child categories of the specified parent category, enabling navigation through the category hierarchy. When explicitly set to null, retrieves only root-level categories (categories with no parent). When omitted entirely, retrieves all categories regardless of hierarchical position.

This parameter is essential for building hierarchical category navigation interfaces and category tree structures in the marketplace.

oneOf.description:
Active category status value.

Indicates categories that are visible to buyers and available for product assignment in the marketplace. Active categories appear in navigation menus, product filtering interfaces, and category browsing experiences.

Inactive category status value.

Indicates categories that are hidden from public display but preserved for historical product references. Inactive categories prevent new product assignments while maintaining historical data integrity.

status.description:
Category visibility status filter.

Filters categories based on their visibility status in the marketplace. The 'active' status indicates categories that are visible to buyers and available for product assignment. The 'inactive' status indicates categories that are hidden from public display but preserved for historical product references.

This filter is essential for both public category browsing (showing only active categories) and administrative management (viewing all categories regardless of status). When omitted, the operation may return categories of all statuses depending on the endpoint's default behavior and user authorization level.

oneOf.description:
Sort by category name field.

Orders results alphabetically by category name, enabling name-based browsing and organization. Useful for presenting categories in a predictable alphabetical sequence.

Sort by category creation timestamp.

Orders results chronologically by when categories were created. Useful for finding recently added categories or viewing category creation history.

Sort by display order field.

Orders results by the custom display ordering value set by administrators. This reflects the intended presentation sequence for categories in navigation menus and browsing interfaces, as defined in the shopping_mall_categories.display_order field.

sort_by.description:
Field name to use for sorting the category results.

Determines which category attribute is used as the primary sorting criterion. Available options include 'name' for alphabetical sorting, 'created_at' for chronological sorting by creation date, and 'display_order' for custom display ordering defined by administrators. This parameter works in conjunction with sort_direction to control result ordering.

oneOf.description:
Ascending sort direction.

Orders results from lowest to highest, such as A-Z for names, earliest to latest for dates, or lowest to highest for numeric display order values.

Descending sort direction.

Orders results from highest to lowest, such as Z-A for names, latest to earliest for dates, or highest to lowest for numeric display order values.

sort_direction.description:
Direction for sorting results, either ascending or descending.

Controls whether results are sorted in ascending order (asc) from lowest to highest, or descending order (desc) from highest to lowest. This parameter applies to the field specified in sort_by, enabling flexible result ordering for different use cases.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the category.

Primary key UUID used to reference this category across the platform. Generated automatically when the category is created and remains immutable throughout the category lifecycle.

name.description:
Category name displayed to users.

Human-readable name of the category shown in navigation menus, product listings, and filtering interfaces. Used for product classification and buyer navigation. Should be clear and descriptive to help buyers find relevant products.

Must be between 2 and 100 characters in length. Examples include 'Electronics', 'Men's Clothing', 'Laptops', 'Gaming Laptops'.

slug.description:
URL-friendly unique identifier for the category.

Used for constructing SEO-optimized category URLs and programmatic category references. Must be globally unique across all categories for reliable identification and routing.

Typically follows lowercase-with-hyphens pattern like 'electronics', 'mens-clothing', 'home-garden'. Generated from the category name during creation and used in category browsing URLs.

description.description:
Detailed category description explaining the types of products included.

Provides comprehensive information about the category scope, helping buyers understand what types of products belong in this category and assisting sellers in correct product categorization. Maximum 1000 characters.

This field is optional and may be null for categories that don't require detailed explanations, particularly for self-explanatory category names or leaf-level categories in the hierarchy.

image_url.description:
Category banner or icon image URL for visual representation.

Used in category navigation menus, browsing interfaces, and category landing pages to provide visual context and improve user experience. The URL points to a pre-uploaded image in the storage service.

This field is optional for leaf categories but recommended for top-level categories to enhance visual navigation. When null, the category is displayed without a dedicated image.

parent_id.description:
Parent category identifier for hierarchical organization.

References the parent category in the category tree structure, enabling multi-level category hierarchies. When null, indicates this is a root-level category at the top of the taxonomy. When populated with a UUID, establishes the parent-child relationship within the category tree.

This field is essential for rendering hierarchical navigation interfaces, breadcrumb trails, and category tree structures. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_categories.parent_id foreign key field in the database schema.

status.description:
Category visibility status in the marketplace.

Indicates whether the category is currently active and visible to buyers or inactive and hidden from public display. Active categories appear in navigation menus and are available for product assignment. Inactive categories are preserved for historical product references but hidden from active use.

Possible values are 'active' for visible categories and 'inactive' for hidden categories. Inactive categories prevent new product assignments while maintaining historical data integrity. This field directly corresponds to the shopping_mall_categories.status column in the database schema.

display_order.description:
Numeric ordering value for category display sequence.

Controls the position of this category relative to its siblings when rendering category lists and navigation menus. Lower values appear first in the display sequence. Administrators set this value to customize category presentation order within each hierarchical level.

This field enables precise control over category positioning in navigation interfaces, ensuring important categories can be prominently displayed. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_categories.display_order field in the database schema.

product_count.description:
Cached count of active products directly assigned to this category.

Represents the number of active products that are currently categorized under this specific category. This count is updated when products are added, removed, or when product status changes affect visibility.

Used for displaying product counts in category browsing interfaces without expensive real-time queries. Helps buyers understand category size and product availability. Does not include products in child categories, only direct assignments to this category level.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the category was created.

Records the exact date and time when this category was initially created by an administrator in the system. Represented in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

This timestamp is immutable and provides an audit trail for category creation. Useful for tracking category history, sorting by creation date, and understanding taxonomy evolution over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the category information was last modified.

Records the most recent date and time when any field in this category was updated, including name changes, description modifications, parent reassignments, status changes, or display order adjustments. Represented in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

Automatically updated on any field change to maintain accurate modification tracking. Useful for identifying recently modified categories, cache invalidation strategies, and audit trail purposes.

IShoppingMallCategory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product category for lightweight references.

Provides essential category information for product classification, navigation breadcrumbs, and embedded references. Used when including category context in product listings, search results, and hierarchical navigation without loading complete category details.

Includes hierarchical context through the parent_id field, enabling proper category tree rendering and breadcrumb navigation. The status field allows filtering and display logic based on category visibility. The display_order field ensures categories are presented in the administrator-defined sequence.

Optimized for list performance by including only essential category identification and organizational fields. For complete category details including descriptions, images, product counts, and full metadata, use the main IShoppingMallCategory type.

id.description:
Primary key unique identifier for the category.

This UUID serves as the immutable reference for the category across all system operations and relationships. Generated automatically upon category creation and never changes throughout the category lifecycle.

parent_id.description:
Parent category identifier for hierarchical organization.

Foreign key reference to another category's ID in the shopping_mall_categories table. When null, indicates a root-level category at the top of the hierarchy. When set, establishes parent-child relationship enabling tree-structured taxonomy with unlimited nesting depth.

This UUID reference enables buyers to navigate category breadcrumbs and supports sophisticated product organization through hierarchical classification.

parent.description:
Parent category for hierarchical organization.

Enables tree-structured taxonomy with unlimited nesting depth. When null, indicates a root-level category at the top of the hierarchy. Parent relationships allow buyers to navigate category breadcrumbs and enable sophisticated product organization.

The parent reference uses summary type to prevent circular reference issues in the category tree structure.

name.description:
Category name displayed to buyers and sellers.

Human-readable label shown throughout the platform including navigation menus, product listings, and category browsing interfaces. Must be descriptive and clearly communicate the product types included in this category.

Examples: Electronics, Men's Clothing, Laptops, Gaming Laptops, Home & Garden.

slug.description:
URL-friendly identifier generated from category name.

Used for constructing SEO-optimized category URLs and deep linking. Must be unique globally across all categories to prevent routing conflicts. Typically derived from the category name with lowercase conversion and special character replacement.

Examples: electronics, mens-clothing, gaming-laptops.

description.description:
Detailed category description explaining the types of products included.

Provides buyers with context about category scope and helps sellers understand correct product categorization. Supports plain text formatting up to 1000 characters. Optional field that enhances category understanding and SEO value.

Useful for ambiguous categories or those requiring classification guidance.

image_url.description:
Category banner or icon image URL.

Visual representation displayed in category navigation, browsing interfaces, and landing pages. Enhances user experience by providing visual cues for category identification. Optional for leaf categories, recommended for top-level categories.

Should reference accessible image storage with appropriate dimensions for responsive display.

display_order.description:
Numeric ordering value controlling category display sequence within the same parent level.

Lower values appear first in navigation menus and category lists. Enables precise admin control over category positioning for merchandising and user experience optimization. Typical values range from 0 to 999.

Categories with equal display_order values fall back to alphabetical sorting by name.

oneOf.description:
Category visibility status controlling public display and product assignment.

Active categories are visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive categories are hidden from public display but preserve historical product references, preventing new product assignments while maintaining data integrity.

Status transitions are admin-controlled and immediately affect category visibility across the platform.

Category visibility status controlling public display and product assignment.

Active categories are visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive categories are hidden from public display but preserve historical product references, preventing new product assignments while maintaining data integrity.

Status transitions are admin-controlled and immediately affect category visibility across the platform.

status.description:
Category visibility status controlling public display and product assignment.

Active categories are visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive categories are hidden from public display but preserve historical product references, preventing new product assignments while maintaining data integrity.

Status transitions are admin-controlled and immediately affect category visibility across the platform.

product_count.description:
Cached count of active products directly assigned to this category.

Denormalized value updated when products are added, removed, or change status. Displays product counts in category browsing interfaces without expensive real-time aggregation queries. Excludes products in draft, archived, or deleted states.

Count reflects only direct category assignments, not recursive totals from child categories.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the category was created by an admin.

Records the initial creation moment in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Used for category lifecycle tracking, audit trails, and chronological sorting. Immutable value set once upon creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the category information was last modified.

Automatically updated on any field change including name, description, parent reassignment, status change, or display order adjustment. Tracks the most recent modification for cache invalidation and change detection.

Essential for identifying stale data in distributed systems and frontend caches.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for category archival.

When set, indicates the category is logically deleted and hidden from active use while preserving historical product categorization data. Null for active categories. Soft deletion maintains referential integrity for products, orders, and analytics that reference this category.

Deleted categories cannot be reassigned to products and are excluded from navigation and browsing interfaces.

IShoppingMallCategory.description:
Complete category entity representing hierarchical product taxonomy nodes.

Categories organize the marketplace product catalog into browsable classification trees. Each category can have a parent category, creating unlimited nesting depth for flexible taxonomy management that accommodates diverse product ranges.

Categories serve multiple platform roles: buyers navigate category hierarchies to discover products, sellers assign categories to organize listings, and admins manage the taxonomy structure to maintain marketplace organization. The category system supports both broad classifications and granular product grouping.

Category visibility is controlled through status management, enabling temporary hiding without data loss. Soft deletion preserves historical relationships while removing categories from active use. Display ordering provides merchandising control over category presentation.

parent_id.description:
UUID of the parent category in the hierarchy.

Foreign key reference to another category's ID for establishing parent-child relationships. Null or omitted for root-level categories at the top of the taxonomy tree. When specified, must reference an existing active category to create a subcategory.

Enables building multi-level category hierarchies with unlimited nesting depth for flexible product organization.

name.description:
Display name of the category that will be shown to users throughout the marketplace.

Human-readable label that clearly identifies the product classification. Must be between 2 and 100 characters. Should be descriptive and help buyers understand the category scope.

Examples: Electronics, Men's Clothing, Smart Home Devices, Gaming Laptops.

slug.description:
URL-friendly unique identifier for SEO-optimized category URLs.

Must be globally unique across all categories to prevent routing conflicts. Typically lowercase-with-hyphens format derived from the category name. Used for constructing clean, readable URLs.

Examples: electronics, mens-clothing, smart-home-devices, gaming-laptops.

description.description:
Detailed description explaining what types of products belong in this category.

Optional field providing buyers with context about category scope and helping sellers understand correct product categorization. Supports up to 1000 characters of plain text. Enhances SEO value and clarifies classification rules.

Useful for ambiguous categories or those requiring additional classification guidance.

image_url.description:
Category banner or icon image URL for visual representation.

Optional image displayed in category navigation and browsing interfaces. Should reference accessible image storage with appropriate responsive dimensions. Enhances user experience through visual category identification.

Recommended for top-level categories, optional for leaf categories.

display_order.description:
Numeric value controlling display sequence among sibling categories at the same hierarchy level.

Lower values appear first in navigation menus and category lists. Enables precise admin control over category positioning for merchandising optimization. Typical values range from 0 to 999.

Categories with equal display_order values fall back to alphabetical sorting by name.

oneOf.description:
Initial operational status of the category.

Active status makes the category immediately visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive status creates the category but hides it from public view while preserving it for future activation.

Initial operational status of the category.

Active status makes the category immediately visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive status creates the category but hides it from public view while preserving it for future activation.

status.description:
Initial operational status of the category.

Active status makes the category immediately visible to buyers and sellers, allowing product browsing and new product assignments. Inactive status creates the category but hides it from public view while preserving it for future activation.

IShoppingMallCategory.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new product category in the marketplace taxonomy.

Defines the essential information required to establish a new category within the hierarchical category structure. Administrators must provide unique identifiers (slug), display information (name and optional description), hierarchy position (parent_id), display sequence (display_order), and initial visibility (status).

The parent_id field enables building multi-level category hierarchies by referencing an existing category's UUID. When null or omitted, the new category is created as a root-level category at the top of the taxonomy tree. When specified, it must reference an existing active category to establish the parent-child relationship.

The slug must be globally unique across all categories and provides SEO-friendly URLs for category pages. This identifier is immutable after creation to maintain referential integrity and prevent broken links.

The display_order value determines where this category appears relative to its siblings (other categories at the same hierarchy level under the same parent). This enables precise control over category navigation structure and prominence for merchandising purposes.

Validation ensures all unique constraints are satisfied, parent references are valid, and hierarchy rules are maintained. The operation rejects requests that would create circular references or violate category structure constraints.

System-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, product_count) are automatically generated during creation and must not be included in the request. The creating admin's identity is captured from the authentication context, not from request body data.

parent_id.description:
Updated parent category ID for hierarchy restructuring.

Changing the parent reassigns the category to a different position in the taxonomy tree. Setting to null promotes the category to root level. The system validates that hierarchy changes don't create circular references or violate depth constraints.

This field references the parent category's UUID from the shopping_mall_categories table.

name.description:
Updated category name displayed to users.

Must be descriptive and clearly communicate the product classification. Name changes affect all navigation menus and product displays that reference this category.

Validated for length constraints and uniqueness within the same parent level.

slug.description:
Updated URL-friendly identifier for the category.

Must be globally unique across all categories to prevent routing conflicts. Changing the slug affects all category URLs and requires redirect management to preserve SEO value and prevent broken links.

Typically derived from the category name with lowercase conversion and special character replacement.

description.description:
Updated detailed category description.

Provides context about category scope and classification guidance. Supports plain text up to 1000 characters. Can be set to null to remove existing description.

Useful for clarifying ambiguous categories or updating categorization rules.

image_url.description:
Updated category banner or icon image URL.

Visual representation for navigation and browsing interfaces. Can be set to null to remove existing image. Should reference accessible image storage with appropriate responsive dimensions.

Changing images requires cache invalidation across the platform.

display_order.description:
Updated display sequence order within the parent level.

Controls category positioning in navigation menus for merchandising optimization. Lower values appear first. Changes immediately affect category presentation order.

Typical values range from 0 to 999.

oneOf.description:
Updated category visibility status.

Changing to inactive hides the category from public display and prevents new product assignments while preserving historical data. Changing to active restores category visibility and enables product assignments.

Status transitions immediately affect platform-wide category visibility.

Updated category visibility status.

Changing to inactive hides the category from public display and prevents new product assignments while preserving historical data. Changing to active restores category visibility and enables product assignments.

Status transitions immediately affect platform-wide category visibility.

status.description:
Updated category visibility status.

Changing to inactive hides the category from public display and prevents new product assignments while preserving historical data. Changing to active restores category visibility and enables product assignments.

Status transitions immediately affect platform-wide category visibility.

IShoppingMallCategory.IUpdate.description:
Update payload for modifying existing category attributes.

All fields are optional, allowing partial updates to specific category properties without affecting other attributes. Only provided fields are updated while omitted fields retain their existing values.

This request body is restricted to admin users who manage the marketplace taxonomy structure. Updates are validated to ensure data integrity, prevent circular hierarchy references, maintain unique constraints, and preserve referential integrity with existing products.

Changes to category structure affect product organization, navigation menus, and search indexes across the entire marketplace.

id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID) for the product sale record.

This is the primary key in the shopping_mall_sales table and is auto-generated by the system upon creation. Used for internal references and database relationships but not exposed in public URLs.

The UUID ensures globally unique identification across distributed systems and prevents ID collision in multi-tenant environments.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code for the product sale.

This human-readable code is used in API endpoints and URLs to reference the sale. The code must be globally unique across all sales in the marketplace.

Typically formatted as a short, memorable string that can be used in public-facing interfaces. Used for SEO-friendly URLs and external integrations where UUIDs are too verbose.

title.description:
Product sale title or name displayed to buyers in listings and search results.

This is the primary display name that helps buyers identify and understand the product being offered. Should be descriptive, accurate, and optimized for search discoverability.

Must be between 3 and 200 characters in length. The title appears in product cards, search results, category browsing, and product detail pages.

description.description:
Detailed product description providing comprehensive information about the sale item.

Contains full product details including features, specifications, materials, dimensions, usage instructions, and any other relevant information. Helps buyers make informed purchase decisions and reduces support inquiries.

Must be between 50 and 5000 characters. Supports plain text formatting. A thorough description improves conversion rates and reduces return rates by setting accurate expectations.

brand.description:
Brand name of the product.

Identifies the manufacturer or brand associated with this product. Optional field up to 100 characters.

Brand information helps buyers filter products and make purchase decisions based on brand preference and reputation. Popular brands may receive enhanced visibility in search results.

condition.description:
Product condition indicating the state of the item being sold.

Valid values: new, refurbished, used. This field ensures buyer transparency about the product state.

New products are unused and in original packaging. Refurbished products have been restored to working condition. Used products show signs of previous use. Accurate condition disclosure prevents disputes and returns.

status.description:
Current product lifecycle status controlling visibility and purchasing capability.

Valid values: draft, pending_approval, published, suspended, archived.

Draft products are being created by sellers. Pending_approval products await admin review. Published products are live and purchasable. Suspended products are temporarily hidden. Archived products are permanently delisted.

Status transitions are controlled through business workflows and admin moderation. Only published products are visible to buyers and available for purchase.

short_description.description:
Brief product summary for listing displays and search previews.

Optional field between 100-500 characters providing a concise product overview. Used in product cards, category listings, and search results where full descriptions are too lengthy.

Effective short descriptions highlight key features and benefits to encourage clicks to the full product detail page.

meta_keywords.description:
SEO keywords for search optimization and discoverability.

Optional comma-separated keyword list helping search engines and internal search algorithms understand product relevance. Improves product visibility in search results.

Keywords should reflect terms buyers use when searching for this type of product. Avoid keyword stuffing and focus on relevant, specific terms.

weight.description:
Product weight in kilograms.

Used for shipping cost calculations and logistics planning. Optional field supporting decimal values for precise weight measurement.

Accurate weight information ensures correct shipping quotes and prevents fulfillment issues. Essential for products where shipping costs significantly impact total price.

dimension_length.description:
Product length dimension in centimeters.

Optional field for shipping calculations and packaging requirements. Supports decimal values for precise measurements.

Dimension information helps carriers determine shipping costs and ensures products fit in standard packaging. Critical for oversized items with dimensional weight pricing.

dimension_width.description:
Product width dimension in centimeters.

Optional field for shipping calculations and packaging requirements. Supports decimal values for precise measurements.

Width measurement works with length and height to calculate total package volume for shipping cost determination.

dimension_height.description:
Product height dimension in centimeters.

Optional field for shipping calculations and packaging requirements. Supports decimal values for precise measurements.

Height completes the three-dimensional measurement set needed for accurate shipping cost calculations and carrier selection.

manufacturer.description:
Manufacturer name identifying the company that produced the product.

Optional field up to 100 characters. Manufacturer information provides buyers with production source transparency.

Useful for warranty claims, product recalls, and buyer confidence. Some buyers prefer products from specific manufacturers based on quality reputation.

return_policy_days.description:
Number of days buyers can request returns after delivery.

Valid values: 7, 14, 30, 60, or 0 for no returns. Defines the return window during which buyers can initiate return requests.

Longer return periods increase buyer confidence but create inventory uncertainty for sellers. Marketplace may enforce minimum return periods for buyer protection.

warranty_info.description:
Warranty details and duration provided by seller or manufacturer.

Optional field up to 1000 characters describing warranty coverage, duration, and claim procedures. Includes information about what is covered, warranty period, and how buyers can make warranty claims.

Clear warranty information reduces buyer uncertainty and support inquiries. Comprehensive warranties can be a competitive advantage.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product sale record was first created by the seller.

Automatically set by the system upon initial creation in ISO 8601 format with timezone. Used for sorting, filtering, and displaying product listing age to buyers and sellers.

Creation timestamp enables chronological sorting, analytics on listing velocity, and identification of stale inventory.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the product sale information was last modified.

Automatically updated by the system on any product information change including title, description, pricing, category reassignment, or status updates. Tracks the most recent modification for cache invalidation and change detection.

Essential for identifying stale data in distributed systems, frontend caching strategies, and displaying freshness indicators to buyers and sellers.

seller.description:
Summary information about the seller who owns this product listing.

Provides essential seller context including store name, email, and account status. Buyers use this information to evaluate seller reputation before making purchase decisions.

Seller summary enables buyers to view seller profiles, check ratings, and assess trustworthiness. Links to complete seller information for detailed reputation metrics.

category.description:
Summary information about the category this product belongs to.

Provides category context including category name and hierarchy position. Used for displaying breadcrumb navigation and helping buyers understand product classification.

Category reference enables proper product organization, filtering, and navigation. Essential for marketplace taxonomy and search functionality.

IShoppingMallSale.description:
Complete product sale listing entity with all details and relationships.

Represents a product offered for sale by a merchant in the shopping marketplace. This is the main entity that buyers browse, search, and purchase from.

Each sale is owned by a specific seller and belongs to a category for organization and discoverability. The sale entity contains core product information including title, description, condition, status, dimensions, and warranty details.

Complex products with multiple configuration options use variant attributes and SKUs to represent different product combinations. The sale entity provides the base product information while SKUs handle variant-specific pricing and inventory.

This DTO is returned from single-item retrieval operations and provides complete information needed to display a product detail page. Related entities like SKUs, variant attributes, images, and reviews are accessed through separate API operations to maintain efficient response sizes.

IShoppingMallSale.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product sale listing for lightweight references.

Provides essential product information for display in lists, cards, search results, and embedded contexts. Optimized for performance by excluding large text fields and composition arrays while maintaining sufficient detail for buyer decision-making.

Used in product lists, category pages, search results, shopping cart displays, and order item references. For complete product details including full description and all SKU variants, use the main IShoppingMallSale type.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product sale listing.

Primary key used to reference this product across the platform. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.id field in the Prisma schema.

Generated automatically when the product is listed and remains immutable throughout the product lifecycle.

code.description:
Unique business identifier for the product.

Used for seller's internal SKU tracking and product references. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.code field in the Prisma schema.

Provides a human-readable identifier that sellers can use for their own inventory management and product identification systems.

title.description:
Product name displayed to buyers.

Must be between 3 and 200 characters in length. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.title field in the Prisma schema.

Used in search results, product cards, and order summaries. Should be clear and informative to help buyers identify the product quickly.

Brand name of the product.

Optional field up to 100 characters. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.brand field in the Prisma schema.

short_description.description:
Brief product summary for listing displays.

Optional field between 100-500 characters. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.short_description field in the Prisma schema.

Provides a concise overview of the product for display in summary views without loading the full description. May be null if not provided by the seller.

price.description:
Minimum price across all SKU variants for this product.

This is a computed field derived from the product's SKU variants, not a direct field from the Prisma schema. Represents the lowest-priced variant to help buyers quickly assess affordability.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD). Individual SKU variants may have different prices. Supports up to 2 decimal places for cents.

thumbnail_url.description:
URL of the product's primary thumbnail image.

This is a computed field derived from the product's image relationships, not a direct field from the Prisma schema. Typically represents the first image or a designated primary image.

Should be optimized for fast loading in list views. Format should be web-friendly (JPEG, PNG, WebP). May be null if no images have been uploaded for this product.

return_policy_days.description:
Number of days buyers can request returns after delivery.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.return_policy_days field in the Prisma schema. Valid values are 7, 14, 30, 60, or 0 for no returns allowed.

This field informs buyers of the return window and affects purchase confidence. Different sellers may offer different return policies based on product type and business practices. A value of 0 indicates that the product cannot be returned after purchase.

warranty_info.description:
Warranty details and duration provided by seller.

Optional field up to 1000 characters. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.warranty_info field in the Prisma schema.

Describes warranty coverage, duration, and claim procedures. Provides buyer assurance and product quality information. May be null if no warranty is offered for the product.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the product was first created by the seller.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.created_at field in the Prisma schema. Automatically set when the product listing is initially created.

Used for sorting by newest listings and tracking product age in the marketplace.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the product was last modified.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.updated_at field in the Prisma schema. Updated automatically on any product information change including title, description, price, status, or other field modifications.

Helps buyers identify recently updated products and enables tracking of product information freshness. Used in admin interfaces for monitoring seller activity and product maintenance.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for product archival.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.deleted_at field in the Prisma schema. When set, indicates the product has been logically deleted while preserving order history and data integrity.

Soft-deleted products are excluded from public searches but maintain referential integrity for historical orders and analytics. Null for active products. Enables potential product restoration within a retention period.

seller.description:
Reference to the seller who listed this product.

Provides essential seller information including store name, email, and status. Links this product to its merchant for trust and filtering purposes.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.shopping_mall_seller_id foreign key relationship in the Prisma schema. Contains lightweight seller information without full business details.

category.description:
Reference to the product's primary category.

Provides category classification for navigation and filtering. Helps buyers find products through category browsing.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sales.shopping_mall_category_id foreign key relationship in the Prisma schema. Contains essential category information without hierarchical details.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Determines which page of results to return based on the limit size. For example, with limit=20, page=1 returns items 1-20, page=2 returns items 21-40.

Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of items per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100 to balance user experience with server performance. Larger limits reduce API calls but increase response size.

Defaults to 20 if not specified.

search.description:
Search query for partial product name matching.

Performs case-insensitive substring search against product titles. Supports multi-word queries with implicit AND semantics. Minimum 2 characters required to prevent overly broad searches.

Examples: 'laptop', 'blue shirt', 'gaming mouse wireless'.

seller_id.description:
Filter products by specific seller.

Restricts results to products owned by the specified seller. Useful for viewing a seller's complete catalog or seller-specific inventory management. References the shopping_mall_sellers.id field.

When used by authenticated sellers, typically set to their own ID for inventory management.

category_id.description:
Filter products by category assignment.

Restricts results to products assigned to the specified category. Does not include products from child categories (non-recursive filtering). References the shopping_mall_categories.id field.

Enables category-based product browsing and navigation.

min_price.description:
Minimum price threshold for filtering.

Returns only products where the minimum SKU price is greater than or equal to this value. Works in conjunction with max_price for range filtering. Useful for budget-based product discovery.

Price comparisons use the lowest available price across all product SKUs.

max_price.description:
Maximum price threshold for filtering.

Returns only products where the minimum SKU price is less than or equal to this value. Works with min_price for range filtering. Enables buyers to stay within budget constraints.

Price comparisons use the lowest available price across all product SKUs.
