has_stock.description:
Filter by stock availability.

When true, returns only products with at least one SKU having available inventory. When false or omitted, returns all products regardless of stock status.

Useful for filtering out-of-stock products in buyer-facing searches.

IShoppingMallSale.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for product sale discovery.

Provides comprehensive filtering, searching, and sorting capabilities for querying the product marketplace. Supports multiple use cases including buyer product discovery, seller inventory management, and admin marketplace oversight.

All filter parameters are optional and combine with AND semantics when multiple filters are specified. The search query performs partial matching while exact filters like category_id and seller_id require precise matches.

Pagination is controlled through page and limit parameters, with sensible defaults ensuring usable results even when pagination is omitted. Sorting options enable buyers to organize results according to their priorities.

Authorization context affects default filtering: public users see only published products, authenticated sellers can view their own products in any status, and admins have unrestricted access to all products.

IShoppingMallSaleSku.description:
Complete detailed representation of a SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variant within a product sale listing.

This schema represents individual product variants defined by specific attribute combinations (e.g., size, color, style). Each SKU is a unique purchasable item with its own pricing structure and availability status. SKUs enable sellers to offer product variations while maintaining consolidated product listings.

The SKU entity is central to pricing management, variant configuration, and cart operations. When buyers select product options, the system resolves to a specific SKU for pricing and availability validation. Inventory tracking is handled separately through the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table, allowing independent stock management per SKU.

Pricing supports base price (regular selling price), compare-at price (original MSRP for discount display), and sale price (temporary promotional pricing). Sale prices have defined start and end timestamps for automated promotion activation and deactivation.

Security and ownership: SKUs inherit access control from their parent sale listing. Only the owning seller can manage SKU details, while buyers have read access to available SKUs during shopping.

id.description:
System-generated unique identifier for the SKU record.

UUID that uniquely identifies this SKU across the entire platform. Used for internal references, cart items, order items, and inventory transactions. Generated automatically when the SKU variant is created and remains immutable.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent product sale listing.

Links this SKU to its parent sale. Multiple SKUs can belong to the same sale, representing different product variants. This relationship is immutable after SKU creation and establishes the ownership and access control context for the SKU.

sku_code.description:
Unique business identifier code for this SKU within the parent sale.

Human-readable code that must be unique within the scope of the sale (composite unique constraint with shopping_mall_sale_id). Typically represents variant configuration (e.g., 'RED-L', 'SIZE-42'). Format: BASE-SKU-ATTR1-ATTR2. Used for seller's internal SKU tracking and catalog management.

variant_combination.description:
JSON object containing selected variant attribute values.

Defines this SKU's specific configuration as a JSON structure mapping attribute names to selected values. Example: {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}. This combination must be unique within the sale to ensure each SKU represents a distinct product configuration. Used for SKU resolution during variant selection.

base_price.description:
Regular selling price for this SKU variant.

Standard price charged for this product configuration in the platform's base currency. Must be greater than 0 with maximum 2 decimal places. This is the default price when no promotional sale price is active. May differ from other SKUs in the same sale based on variant attributes (e.g., premium materials, larger sizes).

compare_at_price.description:
Original or manufacturer's suggested retail price.

Used to display discounts and savings to buyers by comparing against the base_price or sale_price. Must be greater than or equal to base_price if provided. Helps communicate value proposition by showing price reductions. Optional field that can be null if no comparison pricing is needed.

sale_price.description:
Temporary promotional price for limited-time sales.

Special discounted price active between sale_start_at and sale_end_at timestamps. Must be less than base_price if provided. When a valid sale price is active, it overrides the base_price for buyer-facing displays and checkout. Enables time-bound promotional campaigns and flash sales.

sale_start_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price becomes active.

ISO 8601 datetime indicating when the promotional sale_price should start being applied. Optional field accompanying sale_price. Used for scheduled promotions that activate automatically at a specific time. System validates that sale_start_at is before sale_end_at when both are provided.

sale_end_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price expires and base price resumes.

ISO 8601 datetime indicating when the promotional sale_price should stop being applied and revert to base_price. Optional field accompanying sale_price. Enables automatic promotion expiration without manual intervention. Must be after sale_start_at when both are provided.

cost_price.description:
Seller's cost for profit tracking and analytics.

The amount the seller paid to acquire or produce this SKU variant. Not visible to buyers. Used for internal profit margin calculations, business analytics, and financial reporting. Optional field that sellers can use to track profitability per variant.

barcode.description:
Barcode, UPC, or EAN identifier for this SKU.

Standard product barcode used for inventory scanning and point-of-sale integration. Optional field for sellers who manage physical inventory with barcode systems. Supports integration with warehouse management and retail POS systems.

enabled.description:
Whether this SKU is offered to buyers.

Controls whether this SKU variant is available for selection and purchase. When false, the SKU is hidden from product pages and cannot be added to cart, regardless of inventory levels. Allows sellers to temporarily disable variants without deleting them, preserving historical order data and configuration.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU was created (ISO 8601 format).

Records when the SKU variant was first added to the sale listing. Useful for tracking product expansion and variant introduction history. Used in analytics to understand product catalog growth over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this SKU was last modified (ISO 8601 format).

Automatically updated whenever any SKU field changes, including price adjustments, barcode updates, or enabled status changes. Useful for cache invalidation and tracking recent inventory or pricing updates. Helps identify recently modified SKUs for audit purposes.

sale.description:
Reference to the parent product sale listing that owns this SKU.

Provides context about the product this SKU belongs to, including product name, seller information, and category. Essential for displaying complete product information when showing SKU details. Contains lightweight sale information without full product description.

variant_values.description:
Array of variant attribute values that define this specific SKU configuration.

Each variant value represents one attribute choice (e.g., color: red, size: large). The combination of all variant values uniquely identifies this SKU within the sale's variant structure. Used to display the specific options selected for this SKU and to validate variant uniqueness.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.description:
Complete product sale image entity with all metadata and responsive image variants.

Represents a single product image associated with either a sale listing or a specific SKU variant. Product images are critical visual assets that help buyers evaluate products before purchase. The entity includes multiple pre-processed image URLs optimized for different display contexts and sizes.

Images undergo automatic processing during upload to generate size-optimized variants (original, large, medium, small, thumbnail). This responsive image strategy ensures fast loading times across different devices and display contexts while maintaining visual quality. Each size variant serves specific use cases: thumbnails for lists, medium for galleries, large for detail views.

Images are organized by display_order to control their presentation sequence in product galleries. The is_primary flag designates which image appears first in galleries and serves as the main product thumbnail in search results. Each image belongs to either a sale-level gallery or a SKU-specific gallery, enabling variant-specific product photography.

The entity tracks creation timestamps for audit purposes and integrates with the shopping_mall_sales or shopping_mall_sale_skus tables through foreign key relationships. Sellers manage these images to optimize product presentation and improve conversion rates through high-quality visual content.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the product image record.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this image record across the platform. Used for referencing the image in update and delete operations. Generated automatically upon image upload and remains immutable.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent product sale listing.

Links this image to the sale listing it belongs to. Populated when the image represents general product imagery shown for all SKU variants. Either this field or shopping_mall_sale_sku_id will be populated, but not both, depending on the image's association level.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the specific SKU variant.

Links this image to a specific SKU variant of the product. When populated, this image represents variant-specific photography (e.g., different colors of the same product). When buyers select a variant, the system displays SKU-specific images if available, otherwise falls back to sale-level images. Either this field or shopping_mall_sale_id will be populated.

url_original.description:
URL to original uploaded image without compression.

Highest quality version stored as uploaded by the seller. Preserves original resolution and quality for archival purposes and potential future reprocessing. Used when maximum quality is required or for generating new size variants.

url_large.description:
URL to large image variant (1600x1600 pixels).

High-resolution variant used for product page main display and zoom functionality. Provides detailed product visualization for buyers examining product details. Optimized for desktop product detail pages and high-DPI displays.

url_medium.description:
URL to medium image variant (800x800 pixels).

Mid-resolution variant used for product page gallery thumbnails and tablet displays. Balances visual quality with loading performance for gallery views. Suitable for product cards in category browsing on larger screens.

url_small.description:
URL to small image variant (400x400 pixels).

Lower-resolution variant used for product listings, search results, and mobile displays. Optimized for fast loading in list views where many products are displayed simultaneously. Provides adequate quality while minimizing bandwidth usage.

url_thumbnail.description:
URL to thumbnail image variant (150x150 pixels).

Minimal-resolution variant used for shopping cart displays, order history, and compact UI elements. Extremely fast loading for contexts where many small product images are shown. Maintains recognizability while prioritizing performance.

is_primary.description:
Whether this is the primary image displayed first in galleries and listings.

When true, this image serves as the main product representation in search results, category listings, and as the first image in product galleries. Only one image per product or SKU should be marked as primary. The primary image significantly impacts click-through rates and buyer first impressions.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for image gallery presentation.

Determines the position of this image in the product gallery, with lower numbers appearing first. The primary image typically has display_order 0. Allows sellers to control the visual narrative and product presentation flow in gallery views.

alt_text.description:
Alternative text description for accessibility compliance and SEO.

Textual description of the image content for screen readers and search engines. Enhances accessibility for visually impaired users and improves SEO discoverability. Should concisely describe the product aspect shown in the image (e.g., 'Red leather handbag front view', 'Product packaging').

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the image record was created in the system.

ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicating when this image was first uploaded and processed into the product listing. Used for audit trails, chronological ordering of image additions, and tracking product catalog evolution over time.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the variant attribute.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this variant attribute within the platform. Used for referencing the attribute in variant values, SKUs, and API operations.

shopping_mall_sale_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent product sale.

Links this variant attribute to the specific product sale listing it belongs to. Each variant attribute is scoped to a single sale, ensuring that product variation configurations are organized per product.

This field establishes the ownership relationship between the variant attribute and its parent sale, enabling proper access control and data organization.

name.description:
Name of the variant attribute.

Display name shown to buyers when selecting product options. Examples include 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', 'Style', etc. This name appears in product configuration interfaces and SKU displays.

The attribute name must be between 2 and 50 characters in length and should clearly describe the variation dimension it represents.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for variant selector presentation to buyers.

Controls the order in which variant attributes appear in product configuration interfaces. Lower numbers appear first, allowing sellers to prioritize the most important variation dimensions (e.g., Size before Color).

This ordering affects the user experience by determining which variant selectors buyers encounter first when configuring their desired product variant.

sale.description:
Summary information of the product sale this variant attribute belongs to.

Provides essential sale context including sale name, code, and basic product information. This association links the variant attribute to its parent product listing.

values.description:
List of variant values associated with this attribute.

Contains all possible option values for this attribute (e.g., for 'Color' attribute: 'Red', 'Blue', 'Green'). Each variant value represents a selectable option that buyers can choose. These values are combined with values from other attributes to form complete SKU configurations.

The values are ordered by their display_order property for consistent presentation in product configuration interfaces.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant attribute was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Useful for tracking when variant configurations were established and for audit trail purposes.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.description:
Complete variant attribute entity with all properties and relationships.

Represents a product variant attribute in the shopping mall marketplace. Variant attributes define the dimensions along which products can vary (such as Color, Size, Material, etc.). Each attribute can have multiple variant values that represent the specific options buyers can select.

Variant attributes are fundamental to the product variant system. Products with multiple configurations (like a t-shirt available in multiple colors and sizes) use variant attributes to define those configuration dimensions. The combination of values from different attributes creates unique SKUs.

For example, a t-shirt might have two variant attributes: 'Color' (with values Red, Blue, Green) and 'Size' (with values S, M, L, XL). Combining these creates 12 possible SKUs (3 colors × 4 sizes).

This entity includes the attribute name, its associated variant values, and the relationship to the parent product sale. It provides the complete structure needed for managing product variant configurations.

Security: Access is controlled based on sale ownership. Sellers can view and manage attributes for their own products, while admins have full access across the platform.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.description:
Specific value selection for a variant attribute defining part of a SKU's configuration.

This schema represents one attribute choice in a product variant configuration (e.g., color: red, size: large). Multiple variant values combine to uniquely define a SKU. The entity links SKUs to their defining attribute values through the shopping_mall_sale_variant_values table.

Variant values are part of the product variant structure that enables sellers to offer multiple configurations of the same product. Each value belongs to a specific variant attribute (e.g., 'color' attribute) and represents one possible choice within that attribute.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the variant value record.

System-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this variant value selection across the platform.

shopping_mall_sale_variant_attribute_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent variant attribute.

Links this value to its attribute definition (e.g., this 'red' value belongs to the 'color' attribute).

value.description:
The actual value text for this variant option.

The specific choice within the attribute (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', '256GB'). Displayed to buyers when selecting product variants.

Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length and should be clear and descriptive to help buyers make informed product configuration choices.

color_code.description:
Hexadecimal color code for visual swatch display.

Optional field that enables visual color representation in product configuration interfaces. When present, contains a hexadecimal color value (e.g., '#FF0000' for red, '#0000FF' for blue) that can be rendered as a color swatch alongside or instead of the text value.

This field is particularly useful for color attributes, allowing buyers to see the actual color rather than relying solely on color names. For non-color attributes (Size, Material, etc.), this field should remain null.

display_order.description:
Numeric position determining the display order of this value within its attribute.

Controls the sequence in which values appear in variant selection UIs. Lower numbers appear first (e.g., Small before Medium before Large).

attribute.description:
Reference to the parent variant attribute this value belongs to.

Provides context about the attribute type and name (e.g., 'Color', 'Size') that this value represents a choice within.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant value was created.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Tracks when this specific variant option was added to the product's configuration, useful for audit trails and understanding product variant evolution over time.

code.description:
Unique business identifier for the product sale listing.

This code serves as a human-readable identifier used in URLs and external references throughout the platform. It must be globally unique across all sales in the marketplace.

The code is used for seller's internal SKU tracking and product references, enabling easy identification and management of product listings. Recommended format includes seller identifier and product identifier for clarity and collision prevention.

This field is indexed in the database with a unique constraint to ensure no duplicate codes can exist.

shopping_mall_category_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the product category for marketplace organization and discovery.

This field assigns the product to a specific category within the hierarchical taxonomy, enabling buyers to find products through category browsing and filtering. The referenced category must exist in the shopping_mall_categories table.

The system validates that the assigned category is a valid leaf-level category in the hierarchy, preventing assignment to parent categories that serve only organizational purposes. Category assignment affects product visibility in category-based navigation and search.

Changing the category after creation is supported through update operations but may affect product discoverability and search rankings.

title.description:
Product name displayed to buyers in listings and search results.

This is the primary display name that identifies the product across the marketplace. It should be concise yet descriptive, clearly communicating what the product is to potential buyers.

The title must be between 3 and 200 characters in length to ensure it's substantive enough to be meaningful while remaining displayable across various interface contexts. The title should meet content guidelines and marketplace quality standards.

This field is indexed for full-text search to enable efficient product discovery through buyer searches.

description.description:
Detailed product description providing comprehensive information to buyers.

This field contains full product details including features, specifications, materials, dimensions, usage instructions, and any other information buyers need to make informed purchasing decisions. The description should be thorough and accurate to reduce buyer questions and returns.

The description must be between 50 and 5000 characters, ensuring sufficient detail while preventing excessively long content. It supports plain text formatting and should meet marketplace content guidelines and quality standards.

This field is indexed for full-text search, contributing to product discoverability when buyers search for specific features or characteristics.

brand.description:
Brand name of the product.

This optional field identifies the manufacturer or brand associated with the product, helping buyers filter and search for products by their preferred brands. Brand information contributes to buyer trust and product authenticity.

When provided, the brand name should be accurate and match the actual product branding. Maximum length is 100 characters.

This field is optional and can be omitted for unbranded or generic products.

oneOf.description:
Product condition indicating the state of the item being sold.

This required field provides buyer transparency about whether the product is brand new, refurbished, or previously used. The condition significantly affects buyer expectations, pricing, and return policies.

Valid values are:
- 'new': Brand new, unused product in original packaging
- 'refurbished': Previously used product that has been restored to working condition
- 'used': Previously owned product sold as-is

Accurate condition reporting is essential for marketplace trust and helps prevent buyer disputes.

short_description.description:
Brief product summary for listing displays and previews.

This optional field provides a concise overview of the product, displayed in contexts where the full description would be too lengthy, such as search results, category listings, and product cards.

When provided, the short description should be between 100 and 500 characters, capturing the most important product highlights and selling points in a condensed format.

If omitted, the system may automatically generate a short description by truncating the main description field.

meta_keywords.description:
SEO keywords for search optimization.

This optional field contains comma-separated keywords that help optimize the product listing for search engines and internal marketplace search. Keywords should be relevant to the product and reflect terms buyers might use when searching.

While this field supports SEO efforts, the primary search ranking factors are the title and description fields. Keywords should be natural and relevant rather than stuffed or spammy.

This field is optional and primarily used for advanced search optimization strategies.

weight.description:
Product weight in kilograms for shipping calculations.

This optional field specifies the product's weight, which is used to calculate shipping costs and determine appropriate shipping methods. Accurate weight information helps ensure correct shipping charges and prevents carrier issues.

Weight should be expressed as a decimal number in kilograms. For example, a 500-gram product would be entered as 0.5.

This field is optional but highly recommended for physical products to enable accurate shipping cost estimation.

dimension_length.description:
Product length dimension in centimeters for shipping calculations.

This optional field specifies the product's length, which combined with width and height, determines the package size for shipping purposes. Dimensional information helps calculate dimensional weight and identify appropriate shipping methods.

Length should be expressed as a decimal number in centimeters. Accurate dimensions prevent shipping cost surprises and ensure carriers can handle the package.

This field is optional but recommended for products where size affects shipping costs or carrier selection.

dimension_width.description:
Product width dimension in centimeters for shipping calculations.

This optional field specifies the product's width, contributing to the overall package size calculation for shipping purposes. Along with length and height, width determines dimensional weight and shipping carrier compatibility.

Width should be expressed as a decimal number in centimeters. Accurate dimensional data ensures proper shipping cost calculation and carrier selection.

This field is optional but recommended for products where package dimensions affect shipping logistics.

dimension_height.description:
Product height dimension in centimeters for shipping calculations.

This optional field specifies the product's height, completing the three-dimensional package size specification. Height, length, and width together determine the volumetric weight and shipping carrier options.

Height should be expressed as a decimal number in centimeters. Complete dimensional information enables accurate shipping cost estimation and prevents carrier restrictions.

This field is optional but recommended for products where dimensions impact shipping costs or carrier selection.

manufacturer.description:
Manufacturer name for product identification and warranty purposes.

This optional field identifies the company that manufactured the product, which may differ from the brand name. Manufacturer information is relevant for warranty claims, product authenticity verification, and regulatory compliance.

When provided, the manufacturer name should be accurate and match official product documentation. Maximum length is 100 characters.

This field is optional and primarily used for products where manufacturer identity is relevant to buyers or warranty processing.

oneOf.description:
Number of days buyers can request returns after delivery.

This required field establishes the return window for the product, setting buyer expectations and defining the seller's return policy. The return period affects buyer confidence and purchase decisions.

Valid values are:
- 0: No returns accepted
- 7: 7-day return window
- 14: 14-day return window
- 30: 30-day return window
- 60: 60-day return window

The return policy must be clearly communicated to buyers and consistently enforced. Longer return windows generally increase buyer confidence but may increase seller costs.

warranty_info.description:
Warranty details and duration provided by the seller.

This optional field describes the warranty coverage, duration, and terms offered with the product. Warranty information increases buyer confidence and clarifies the seller's commitments for product quality and support.

The warranty description should specify the coverage period, what is covered, what is excluded, and how to claim warranty service. Maximum length is 1000 characters to allow comprehensive warranty details.

This field is optional and can be omitted for products sold without warranty coverage.

status.description:
Current product lifecycle status controlling visibility and purchasing capability.

This optional field determines the product's state in its lifecycle and controls whether it's visible to buyers and available for purchase. If not provided, the system typically defaults to 'draft' status.

Valid status values:
- 'draft': Product is being created, not visible to buyers
- 'pending_approval': Awaiting admin review before publication
- 'published': Live on marketplace, visible and purchasable by buyers
- 'suspended': Temporarily hidden from buyers, not purchasable
- 'archived': Permanently delisted, preserved for historical reference

The status field allows sellers to control product visibility throughout the listing lifecycle without deleting data.

IShoppingMallSale.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new product sale listing in the shopping mall marketplace.

This DTO contains all product information needed to create a comprehensive product listing. It includes both required fields essential for a valid product listing and optional fields that enhance product presentation and enable advanced features like shipping calculation and SEO optimization.

The authenticated seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and does not need to be provided in the request body. The shopping_mall_seller_id foreign key is populated server-side from the authentication context to ensure proper ownership assignment and prevent unauthorized listing creation.

System-managed fields are excluded from this DTO:
- id: Auto-generated UUID primary key
- created_at: System timestamp of creation
- updated_at: System timestamp of last modification
- deleted_at: Soft deletion timestamp
- shopping_mall_seller_id: Extracted from JWT token

The operation validates that the assigned category exists and is a valid leaf-level category in the hierarchy. Product information must meet content guidelines, and pricing must be within acceptable marketplace ranges. The status defaults to 'draft' if not provided, allowing sellers to complete variant setup, SKU configuration, and image uploads before activating the listing.

Upon successful creation, the system returns the complete sale entity including the generated ID, which is required for subsequent operations such as adding variant attributes, creating SKUs, uploading images, and managing inventory.

code.description:
Unique business identifier code for the product sale listing.

This human-readable code serves as a persistent identifier used in URLs and external references. Updating the code allows sellers to rebrand or reorganize their product identifier system while maintaining the same database record.

If updated, the new code must be globally unique across all sales in the marketplace. The unique constraint is validated server-side to prevent conflicts.

Code changes should be rare as external references and bookmarks may use the code in URLs.

title.description:
Product sale title or name that buyers will see in listings and search results.

This is the primary display name for the product and should be descriptive and informative. The title should accurately represent the product being sold and help buyers understand what is being offered.

Updating the title allows sellers to improve product discoverability through better keyword optimization or to correct inaccurate product names. The title must remain between 3 and 200 characters in length.

Title changes are immediately reflected in search results and product listings, potentially affecting product discoverability and SEO rankings.

description.description:
Detailed product description providing comprehensive information about the sale item.

This field should contain full product details including features, specifications, materials, dimensions, usage instructions, care instructions, warranty information, and any other relevant details that help buyers make informed purchase decisions.

Updating the description allows sellers to add more detail, correct errors, or improve clarity. The description must remain between 50 and 5000 characters to ensure adequate detail.

Description updates are immediately visible to buyers and can improve buyer confidence, reduce support inquiries, and decrease return rates through better product understanding.

brand.description:

Updating the brand field allows sellers to correct brand information or add brand details to previously unbranded listings. Accurate brand information helps buyers filter and search for products by their preferred brands.

The brand name should match the actual product branding. Setting this to null removes brand association for generic or unbranded products. Maximum length is 100 characters.

Setting to null removes weight information, which may impact shipping cost estimation accuracy.

IShoppingMallSale.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing product sale listing.

This DTO represents all mutable properties of a product sale that sellers can modify after initial creation. All fields are optional to support partial updates - only the fields included in the request will be updated, leaving other fields unchanged.

The update operation maintains data integrity by:
- Validating category references exist and are valid leaf-level categories
- Enforcing business rules for status transitions
- Ensuring code uniqueness if the code is being changed
- Validating enum values for condition, return_policy_days, and status
- Checking minimum and maximum length constraints

Immutable fields excluded from updates:
- id: Primary key, never changes
- shopping_mall_seller_id: Ownership cannot be transferred
- created_at: Historical creation timestamp
- updated_at: Automatically set by system on any update
- deleted_at: Managed through soft-delete operations only

SKU-level updates, variant configuration changes, and image management require separate dedicated API operations to maintain clear separation of concerns and prevent unintended data cascading.

Only the authenticated seller who owns the listing can perform updates. Authorization is enforced through JWT token validation matching against the sale's shopping_mall_seller_id.

Defaults to 1 if not specified.

Defaults to a reasonable value (e.g., 20) if not specified.

Supports partial matching to find attributes whose names contain the search term.
Useful for quickly locating specific attribute types like 'Color' or 'Size'.

Defaults to display_order if not specified to show attributes in their intended presentation order.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.IReque.description:
Search and filter parameters for retrieving variant attributes of a product sale.

This DTO defines the query criteria for paginated retrieval of variant attribute records.
All fields are optional to allow flexible searching with sensible defaults.

Variant attributes represent the configurable dimensions of a product (such as Color, Size, Material) that define how products can be customized.
This request enables filtering and sorting these attributes to display product configuration options in the desired order.

Pagination parameters control result set size and navigation through multiple pages of attributes.
Search and sorting options allow finding specific attributes and presenting them in logical order for the product configuration interface.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.ISumma.description:
Lightweight summary representation of a product variant attribute for display in SKU selection interfaces.

Defines a customization dimension for product variants (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'). Each attribute contains multiple selectable values that buyers choose to configure their desired product variant.

Used in product detail pages for variant selection UI, shopping cart displays, and anywhere product configuration options need to be shown.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the variant attribute.

Primary key used to reference this attribute definition across the platform. Generated automatically upon attribute creation.

sale_id.description:
Reference to the parent sale listing.

Foreign key linking this variant attribute to its owning product sale. Each attribute belongs to exactly one sale.

name.description:
Attribute name displayed to buyers.

Descriptive label for the variant dimension (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Storage Capacity'). Shown as selection prompt in product configuration UI.

Must be between 2 and 50 characters as defined in the Prisma schema constraints.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for variant selector presentation to buyers.

Controls the position in which this attribute appears in the product configuration interface. Lower numbers are displayed first, allowing sellers to arrange variant options in the most intuitive order for their products.

For example, a product might show 'Color' first (display_order=1), then 'Size' (display_order=2), then 'Material' (display_order=3) to guide buyers through the configuration process logically.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant attribute was created.

Records the exact date and time when this attribute definition was added to the sale. Useful for tracking when product configuration options were established and for audit trail purposes.

Automatically set by the system upon attribute creation and remains immutable thereafter.

values.description:
Available option values for this variant attribute.

Array of selectable values that buyers can choose from (e.g., ['Red', 'Blue', 'Green'] for Color attribute). Each value may have different price adjustments.

Supports up to 50 values per variant attribute to accommodate extensive option ranges while preventing overwhelming buyer choice.

name.description:
Display name of the variant attribute to create.

This field specifies the human-readable name that describes the variation dimension, such as 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', 'Style', or 'Capacity'. The name should be clear, concise, and meaningful to help buyers understand the configuration options available for the product.

The name must be unique within the context of a specific sale to prevent confusion and ensure clear distinction between different variant dimensions. It should follow consistent naming conventions across similar product categories to maintain a coherent user experience throughout the marketplace.

Examples of valid variant attribute names include 'Color', 'Size', 'Storage Capacity', 'Material', 'Finish', 'Style', and 'Pattern'.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for variant selector presentation to buyers.

This field controls the position in which this variant attribute appears in the product configuration interface. Lower numerical values cause the attribute to appear earlier in the selection sequence, while higher values position it later.

For example, if creating multiple variant attributes for a product, you might set Color with display_order: 0, Size with display_order: 1, and Material with display_order: 2. This ensures buyers encounter the variant selectors in that exact order when configuring their purchase, with Color presented first as the primary differentiation dimension.

The display order significantly impacts user experience by determining the logical flow of product configuration. Sellers should consider common buyer selection patterns for their product category when assigning display order values. The value must be a non-negative integer, with 0 being the first position in the presentation sequence.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.ICreat.description:
Request body for creating a new variant attribute definition for a product sale.

This DTO contains the required information to establish a new variant attribute that defines a dimension of product variation. The variant attribute serves as a foundational structure that will later be populated with specific variant values representing the available options for that attribute.

The creation operation is scoped to a specific sale, with the sale identification provided through the path parameter rather than in the request body. Both the attribute name and display order must be specified, as these define the attribute's identity and presentation position. Other fields such as identifiers and timestamps are automatically generated by the system.

Security: The authenticated seller's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT token and used to validate ownership of the target sale. The seller_id is not included in this request body as it is derived from the authentication context.

name.description:
Name of the variant attribute (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material').

This field defines the display name for the variant attribute that buyers will see when selecting product options. The name should clearly indicate what product characteristic this attribute represents.

Common examples include 'Color', 'Size', 'Material', 'Style', 'Capacity', etc. The name is used throughout the product configuration interface and in SKU displays.

Changes to the attribute name are reflected across all associated variant values and SKU configurations to maintain consistency.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for variant selector presentation to buyers.

This field controls the position in which this variant attribute appears in the product configuration interface. Lower numerical values cause the attribute to appear earlier in the selection sequence, while higher values position it later.

For example, if a product has Color (display_order: 0), Size (display_order: 1), and Material (display_order: 2) attributes, buyers will see the variant selectors in that exact order when configuring their purchase.

Updating this value allows sellers to reorganize the presentation order of variant attributes to optimize the buyer experience and match common selection patterns for their product category. The value must be a non-negative integer.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantAttribute.IUpdat.description:
Request body for updating an existing variant attribute for a product sale.

This DTO represents the mutable properties of a variant attribute that sellers can modify after creation. Since variant attributes are structural components of product configurations, modifications are limited to non-breaking changes to maintain data integrity with existing SKUs.

All fields are optional following the partial update pattern, allowing sellers to update only the specific properties they want to change. The system preserves existing values for any fields not included in the update request.

Security: The seller's identity comes from JWT authentication and is validated against sale ownership. Path parameters provide the sale code and variant attribute ID, so these are not included in the request body.

Business rules: Updates must not invalidate existing SKU configurations. The system may restrict certain modifications if they would break relationships with variant values or SKUs.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Combined with limit to implement cursor-based pagination for large variant value collections.

limit.description:
Number of variant values to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Maximum of 100 items per page to ensure reasonable response sizes. Recommended values are 10-50 depending on the interface requirements.

search.description:
Search term for filtering variant values by name.

Performs case-insensitive partial matching against variant value names. Useful for finding specific values in attributes with many options (e.g., searching 'navy' in a color attribute with 50+ color options).

oneOf.description:
Field to sort variant values by.

Controls the ordering of results in the response. Options include:
- 'display_order': Sort by the configured display order (default, maintains seller-defined presentation order)
- 'name': Alphabetical sorting by value name
- 'created_at': Chronological order based on creation timestamp

Field to sort variant values by.

Controls the ordering of results in the response. Options include:
- 'display_order': Sort by the configured display order (default, maintains seller-defined presentation order)
- 'name': Alphabetical sorting by value name
- 'created_at': Chronological order based on creation timestamp

Field to sort variant values by.

Controls the ordering of results in the response. Options include:
- 'display_order': Sort by the configured display order (default, maintains seller-defined presentation order)
- 'name': Alphabetical sorting by value name
- 'created_at': Chronological order based on creation timestamp

sort.description:
Field to sort variant values by.

Controls the ordering of results in the response. Options include:
- 'display_order': Sort by the configured display order (default, maintains seller-defined presentation order)
- 'name': Alphabetical sorting by value name
- 'created_at': Chronological order based on creation timestamp

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Applies to the field specified in the 'sort' parameter.

Sort order direction.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Applies to the field specified in the 'sort' parameter.

order.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Applies to the field specified in the 'sort' parameter.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering variant attribute values.

This DTO defines the query parameters for retrieving a paginated and filtered list of variant values within a specific variant attribute. All fields are optional, allowing flexible querying from simple listings to complex filtered searches.

The operation returns variant values that match the search criteria, sorted according to the specified parameters, and paginated for efficient data transfer. Default behavior (when no parameters provided) returns values in display_order with standard pagination.

Typical use cases include:
- Listing all values for a variant attribute in the seller's product management interface
- Searching for specific values when managing large variant configurations
- Retrieving values in specific orders for different display contexts

Security context: The variant attribute ID from the path parameter determines the scope of the search. The operation validates that the requesting user has permission to view the parent sale's variant configuration.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a sale variant option value.

Provides essential information about a specific option value within a variant attribute (e.g., "Red" for Color, "Large" for Size). Used in product listing displays and variant selection interfaces where buyers choose specific product configurations.

This lightweight view excludes detailed metadata and relationships, focusing on the core identification and display information needed for variant selection. Optimized for list views, embedded references, and quick variant option lookups in shopping interfaces.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the variant value.

Primary key used to reference this specific option value throughout the system. Generated automatically upon creation and remains immutable.

shopping_mall_sale_variant_attribute_id.description:
Reference to the parent variant attribute this value belongs to.

Links this value to its containing attribute (e.g., linking "Red" value to the "Color" attribute). Essential for understanding the context and grouping of variant options.

value.description:
Display value of the variant option.

Human-readable text representing this specific option choice (e.g., "Red", "Large", "Cotton"). Shown to buyers when selecting product variants during shopping.

Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length.

color_code.description:
Hexadecimal color code for visual swatch display.

Optional field for color attributes enabling visual representation (e.g., #FF0000 for red). When present, allows the interface to display color swatches alongside or instead of text labels.

This field is particularly useful for color variant attributes where visual representation enhances the buyer's selection experience. For non-color attributes (size, material, etc.), this field remains null.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for option presentation within the attribute selector.

Controls the sequence in which variant options are presented to buyers. Lower numbers appear first in the selection interface.

Sellers configure this order to optimize the presentation of variant options, typically placing most popular or default options first.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the variant value was created.

Records the exact date and time this variant option was added to the system. Useful for tracking variant configuration history and auditing changes to product variant structures.

Format follows ISO 8601 date-time specification.

value.description:
Display text for the new variant attribute value option.

This is the human-readable label that will appear when buyers configure product variants. Examples include size options ('XL', '2XL'), color names ('Forest Green', 'Navy Blue'), material types ('100% Cotton', 'Polyester Blend'), or any other characteristic that distinguishes product variants.

The value must be unique within its parent variant attribute - for example, you cannot have two 'Red' values under the same 'Color' attribute. The text should be clear, descriptive, and meaningful to buyers who will use it to select their desired product configuration. Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length as defined in the Prisma schema.

Best practices: Keep values concise but descriptive, use consistent naming conventions within each attribute, and consider the order in which values will be presented to buyers.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order position for the new variant value within its parent attribute.

This numeric field controls where this value appears in the list of options presented to buyers. Lower numbers appear first, allowing you to create a logical, intuitive ordering such as sizes from smallest to largest (S=1, M=2, L=3, XL=4) or colors in a specific brand sequence.

This field is required as it determines the presentation order of variant options to buyers. Providing explicit display orders ensures your variant options are presented exactly as you intend, improving the buyer's product configuration experience and making selection more intuitive.

color_code.description:
Optional hexadecimal color code for visual swatch display.

When this variant value represents a color option, providing a hexadecimal color code (e.g., '#FF0000' for red, '#0000FF' for blue) enables the platform to display visual color swatches alongside or instead of text labels. This significantly enhances the buyer experience by allowing visual color selection rather than relying solely on color names.

The color code should be a valid hexadecimal format starting with '#' followed by 6 characters (RGB format). This field is optional and primarily relevant for color-based variant attributes. For non-color attributes like size or material, this field can be omitted or set to null.

Best practices: Use standard web color codes, ensure sufficient contrast for visibility, and consider color-blind accessibility when selecting color representations.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new variant attribute value within a product sale's variant configuration.

This DTO captures the required information to add a new selectable option to a variant attribute. Sellers use this when expanding their product variant configurations, such as adding a new color option to an existing 'Color' attribute or introducing an additional size to the 'Size' attribute.

The creation process validates that the value text is unique within its parent variant attribute to prevent duplicate options. The display_order field is required to ensure proper sequencing of variant options in the buyer interface. Once created, the variant value becomes immediately available for SKU configuration, allowing sellers to create new SKU combinations that include this option.

Example usage scenarios:
- Adding 'XL' and '2XL' sizes to a clothing product that previously only offered 'S', 'M', 'L'
- Introducing a new 'Rose Gold' color option to a product's existing color variants
- Expanding material choices by adding 'Bamboo Fiber' to textile products

The parent variant attribute and sale context are provided via path parameters, so this DTO only needs to specify the value's own properties.

value.description:
Display text for the variant attribute value option.

This is the user-facing label shown in product configuration interfaces (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). Sellers may update this to improve clarity or correct spelling.

The value should be concise and descriptive, clearly representing the variant option to buyers during product selection. Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length.

display_order.description:
Display sequence order for presenting this value option in the variant attribute's value list.

Controls the sequence in which variant value options appear in product configuration interfaces. Lower numbers appear first (e.g., display_order: 1 before display_order: 2).

Sellers use this to present options in logical sequences such as size progression (Small, Medium, Large) or color preference ordering. Updating the display order allows reorganization of variant options to optimize the buyer's selection experience.

color_code.description:
Hexadecimal color code for visual swatch display.

When this variant value represents a color option, this field stores the hexadecimal color code (e.g., '#FF0000' for red) that enables visual color swatch rendering in product configuration interfaces. Sellers can update this to correct color representations or adjust visual appearance.

The color code should follow standard hexadecimal format with '#' prefix and 6 characters representing RGB values. Setting this field to null removes the color swatch, reverting to text-only display. This field is primarily relevant for color-based variant attributes.

Updating the color code immediately affects how the variant option appears to buyers in product selection interfaces, enabling sellers to maintain accurate visual representations of their product colors.

IShoppingMallSaleVariantValue.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing variant attribute value within a product sale's variant configuration.

This DTO allows sellers to modify the display text, display order, and color code of a variant value option. All properties are optional, enabling partial updates to specific value attributes.

Typical use cases include renaming value options for clarity (e.g., 'Crimson Red' to 'Red'), reordering options to follow logical sequences (size progressions, popularity rankings), or updating color codes to improve visual swatch accuracy.

Security: The seller's identity is validated from JWT authentication. Only the sale owner can update variant values. Path parameters (saleCode, variantAttributeId, valueId) provide context - these identifiers are NOT included in the request body to prevent duplication and conflicts.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve. Must be a positive integer starting from 1.

Example: page: 1 returns the first set of results, page: 2 returns the second set.

limit.description:
Number of SKU records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Higher limits reduce the number of requests needed but increase response size.

Recommended range: 10-100 items per page for optimal performance and usability.

search.description:
General search query text for finding SKUs by SKU code, variant value combinations, or product identifiers.

Searches across SKU codes and related variant attribute value combinations. Case-insensitive partial matching.

Example: searching 'red large' might match SKUs with Color='Red' and Size='Large'.

variant_value_ids.description:
Array of variant attribute value IDs to filter SKUs by specific variant combinations.

When provided, only SKUs that include ALL specified variant values are returned (AND logic). This enables precise filtering like 'show me all SKUs with Color=Red AND Size=Large'.

Useful for finding specific variant combinations or checking SKU existence for particular attribute value sets.

min_price.description:
Minimum price filter for SKU search (inclusive).

Returns only SKUs with base_price greater than or equal to this value. Prices are in the platform's base currency (typically USD).

Example: min_price: 50.00 returns SKUs priced at $50 or higher.

max_price.description:
Maximum price filter for SKU search (inclusive).

Returns only SKUs with base_price less than or equal to this value. Prices are in the platform's base currency (typically USD).

Combine with min_price to create price range filters (e.g., $50-$100).

min_stock.description:
Minimum stock quantity filter (inclusive).

Returns only SKUs with current stock levels (from related inventory_stocks table) greater than or equal to this value. Useful for finding SKUs with sufficient inventory.

Example: min_stock: 10 returns SKUs with 10 or more units in stock.

max_stock.description:
Maximum stock quantity filter (inclusive).

Returns only SKUs with current stock levels (from related inventory_stocks table) less than or equal to this value. Useful for identifying low-stock or overstocked SKUs.

Example: max_stock: 5 returns SKUs with 5 or fewer units remaining.

is_active.description:
Filter SKUs by enabled/disabled status (maps to Prisma 'enabled' field).

When true, returns only enabled SKUs available for purchase. When false, returns only disabled SKUs (discontinued or unavailable variants).

Omit this filter to retrieve all SKUs regardless of enabled status. This filter controls visibility based on the SKU's enabled field in the database.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines the ordering criteria for the SKU list:
- 'created_at': Sort by SKU creation date (newest or oldest first)
- 'price': Sort by SKU base_price (lowest to highest or vice versa)
- 'sku_code': Sort alphabetically by SKU code

Combine with sort_order to specify ascending or descending direction. Note: These fields exist directly in the shopping_mall_sale_skus table.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for results.

- 'asc': Ascending order (A-Z, 0-9, oldest to newest, lowest to highest)
- 'desc': Descending order (Z-A, 9-0, newest to oldest, highest to lowest)

Works in combination with sort_by to determine result ordering.

IShoppingMallSaleSku.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, sorting, and paginating product SKU lists.

This request DTO enables comprehensive SKU discovery with multiple filtering dimensions including variant attribute combinations, price ranges, stock levels, and availability status. Essential for inventory management, product browsing, and variant selection workflows.

Sellers can use this to manage inventory (e.g., 'find all low-stock red SKUs'), while buyers can use it to explore available product variants (e.g., 'show me all large blue shirts under $50').

All filter parameters are optional and can be combined for complex queries. The pagination parameters (page, limit) control result batching, while sort parameters determine ordering.

Security: Response data is filtered based on the requesting user's authorization level. Buyers see only enabled SKUs with available stock, while sellers see all SKUs including disabled variants for management purposes.

IShoppingMallSaleSku.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a product SKU variant for lightweight references.

Provides essential product variant information for order items, cart displays, and inventory references.
Includes key identifiers, variant configuration, pricing, and availability status without full composition details.

Used when embedding SKU information in other entities like order items or cart items.
For complete SKU details including all pricing tiers and inventory relationships, use the main IShoppingMallSaleSku type.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the SKU variant.

Primary key used to reference this specific product variant across the system.
Generated automatically when the SKU is created and remains immutable.

sku_code.description:
Stock Keeping Unit code for inventory tracking.

Unique alphanumeric identifier used for inventory management and order fulfillment.
Typically follows a pattern combining product and variant information.
Used by warehouse systems and sellers to identify specific product configurations.

variant_combination.description:
JSON object containing the selected variant attribute values that define this SKU.

Stores the complete variant configuration as a JSON string (e.g., {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}).
Defines this SKU's specific combination of variant attributes, distinguishing it from other SKUs of the same product.

Each key represents a variant attribute name, and each value represents the selected option for that attribute.
This field enables precise variant identification and display of variant details to buyers.

base_price.description:
Regular selling price for this SKU variant.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD).
Represents the standard price before any promotional discounts or sales.
May differ across SKU variants of the same product (e.g., larger sizes may cost more).

Supports up to 2 decimal places for cents.
Used as the reference price for calculating discounts and displaying original pricing.

price.description:
Current effective selling price for this SKU variant.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD).
Represents the actual price buyers will pay, which may be the sale_price (if active) or the base_price.
This computed field provides convenience for displaying the current price without client-side price logic.

May differ from base_price when promotional pricing is active.
Supports up to 2 decimal places for cents.

enabled.description:
Availability status indicating whether this SKU variant is currently offered for purchase.

When true, the SKU is active and can be added to cart and purchased by buyers.
When false, the SKU is disabled (discontinued, out of season, or temporarily unavailable).

Disabled SKUs are hidden from product pages and search results but preserved in historical order data.
Sellers can disable SKUs to control which variant combinations are available without deleting data.

sale.description:
Reference to the parent product sale listing.

Provides essential product information including name, seller, and category.
Links this SKU variant back to its parent product listing.
Contains lightweight product information without full composition arrays.

IShoppingMallSaleSku.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new SKU variant within a product sale listing.

Contains the essential information needed to define a new product variant configuration including unique identification, variant attribute specifications, pricing, and availability. The parent sale context is provided via the path parameter (saleCode), not in the request body.

Variant combinations are stored as JSON objects containing selected variant attribute values. Each SKU must have a unique variant combination within the sale to ensure each SKU represents a distinct product configuration. The pricing model supports base pricing, compare-at pricing for discount displays, and optional sale pricing with time windows.

sku_code.description:
Unique SKU identifier within the product. Format: BASE-SKU-ATTR1-ATTR2.

This business identifier must be unique across the seller's entire product catalog. Used for inventory tracking, order processing, and external system integration.

Should follow a consistent naming pattern that indicates the variant configuration (e.g., 'TSHIRT-RED-L', 'PHONE-256GB-BLACK').

variant_combination.description:
JSON object containing selected variant attribute values. Example: {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}.

Defines this SKU's specific configuration by mapping each variant attribute to its selected value. The combination must be unique within the parent sale listing to prevent duplicate SKU definitions.

This JSON structure enables flexible variant definitions supporting any number of attributes (up to 3 as per platform limits).

base_price.description:
Regular selling price for this SKU. Must be greater than 0 with maximum 2 decimal places.

This is the standard price buyers pay when no promotional pricing is active. Individual SKUs within the same sale may have different base prices based on their variant attributes (e.g., larger sizes or premium materials may cost more).

The price must comply with platform minimum pricing policies and should be set to cover costs while remaining competitive.

compare_at_price.description:
Original or manufacturer's suggested retail price. Used to display discounts.

When provided, must be greater than or equal to base_price to show valid discount percentages. This creates urgency by showing buyers how much they're saving.

Optional field - leave null if not using discount display strategy for this SKU.

sale_price.description:
Temporary promotional price. Must be less than base_price if provided.

Active between sale_start_at and sale_end_at timestamps. When a valid sale price is active, it overrides the base_price for buyer-facing displays and checkout.

Optional field - use for limited-time promotions, flash sales, or seasonal discounts.

sale_start_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price becomes active. Optional field accompanying sale_price.

Must be provided if sale_price is set. The system automatically activates the promotional pricing at this timestamp.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2024-12-01T00:00:00Z').

sale_end_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price expires and base price resumes. Optional field accompanying sale_price.

Must be provided if sale_price is set and should be after sale_start_at. The system automatically reverts to base_price after this timestamp.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2024-12-31T23:59:59Z').

cost_price.description:
Seller's cost for profit tracking. Not visible to buyers.

Used internally for profit margin calculations and business analytics. Helps sellers track profitability at the SKU level and make informed pricing decisions.

Optional field for seller analytics and reporting purposes.

barcode.description:
Barcode, UPC, or EAN identifier for this SKU.

Standard product identifier used for inventory management, point-of-sale integration, and warehouse operations. Supports integration with barcode scanning systems.

Optional field for inventory integration and retail operations.

enabled.description:
Whether this SKU is offered to buyers. Disabled SKUs hide from product pages while preserving order history.

Set to false to temporarily remove this variant from sale without deleting the SKU record. Useful for managing seasonal availability, stock issues, or quality concerns.

Disabled SKUs remain in the database for historical order references and can be re-enabled later.

IShoppingMallSaleSku.IUpdate.description:
Update request DTO for modifying an existing SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) variant within a product sale listing.

This schema represents the partial update payload for SKU variant modifications. All fields are optional to support granular updates where sellers can modify specific attributes without affecting others. Common update scenarios include price adjustments based on market conditions, inventory restocking updates, variant configuration modifications, and availability status changes.

The update operation enforces business validation rules including minimum price thresholds, non-negative price values, unique SKU codes within the sale, and unique variant combinations. The schema excludes system-managed fields (id, created_at, updated_at, shopping_mall_sale_id) as these cannot be modified after SKU creation.

Security note: The authenticated seller's identity is automatically validated against the parent sale's ownership through JWT token extraction. Only the sale owner can update their SKU variants.

sku_code.description:
Unique SKU identifier within the product. Format: BASE-SKU-ATTR1-ATTR2.

Must remain unique across the seller's catalog if changed. While modifiable, changing SKU codes should be done carefully as they may be referenced in external inventory systems, order histories, or buyer bookmarks.

Typically updated to align with new naming conventions or correct initial configuration errors.

variant_combination.description:
JSON object containing selected variant attribute values. Example: {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}.

Updating this field changes which variant attributes define this SKU. The new combination must remain unique within the parent sale listing to prevent conflicts with existing SKUs.

Use cautiously - changing variant combinations may confuse buyers who previously viewed or bookmarked this SKU.

base_price.description:
Regular selling price for this SKU. Must be greater than 0 with maximum 2 decimal places.

Price updates are common for promotional campaigns, market adjustments, competitive positioning, or cost changes. The updated price applies immediately to new purchases but doesn't affect existing orders.

Must comply with platform minimum pricing policies.

compare_at_price.description:
Original or manufacturer's suggested retail price. Used to display discounts.

Update this field to adjust discount percentages shown to buyers. Must be greater than or equal to base_price if provided. Set to null to remove discount display.

Updating compare_at_price changes the perceived value and urgency for buyers.

sale_price.description:
Temporary promotional price. Must be less than base_price if provided.

Update to modify active promotional pricing or set to null to end the promotion immediately. Changes take effect based on sale_start_at and sale_end_at timestamps.

Useful for flash sales, seasonal promotions, or inventory clearance.

sale_start_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price becomes active. Optional field accompanying sale_price.

Update to reschedule promotional pricing windows. Must be coordinated with sale_price updates. Set to null to remove scheduled pricing.

Format: ISO 8601 date-time string.

sale_end_at.description:
Timestamp when sale price expires and base price resumes. Optional field accompanying sale_price.

Update to extend or shorten promotional periods. Must be after sale_start_at. Set to null to remove the expiration (sale runs until manually ended).

Format: ISO 8601 date-time string.

cost_price.description:
Seller's cost for profit tracking. Not visible to buyers.

Update when supplier costs change to maintain accurate profit margin tracking. Used for business analytics and financial reporting.

Optional field for seller's internal cost management.

barcode.description:
Barcode, UPC, or EAN identifier for this SKU.

Update to correct barcode information or assign barcodes to previously un-barcoded SKUs. Essential for inventory integration and point-of-sale systems.

Optional field for inventory and warehouse management integration.

enabled.description:
Whether this SKU is offered to buyers. Disabled SKUs hide from product pages while preserving order history.

Set to false to temporarily remove this variant from sale due to quality issues, supplier problems, or seasonal unavailability. Set to true to re-enable previously disabled SKUs.

Availability changes are immediately reflected in product listing displays and checkout validation.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the inventory stock record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for tracking this specific inventory stock entry in the shopping_mall_inventory_stocks table. Generated automatically upon record creation and remains immutable throughout the record's lifecycle.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the associated product SKU variant.

Links this inventory stock record to a specific shopping_mall_sale_skus entry, establishing which product variant this inventory tracking applies to. This relationship is unique (one-to-one), meaning each SKU has exactly one inventory stock record.

This field establishes ownership context, as the inventory stock inherits access permissions from the seller who owns the parent sale listing.

total_quantity.description:
Total inventory quantity including both available and reserved units.

Represents the complete stock level for this SKU variant before accounting for reservations. This is the absolute inventory count that the seller has physically available, updated through inventory transactions including restocks, manual adjustments, and inventory corrections.

Must be a non-negative integer. This value serves as the foundation for calculating available_quantity (total_quantity minus reserved_quantity).

reserved_quantity.description:
Quantity currently reserved during checkout processes.

Represents inventory that has been temporarily allocated to pending orders but not yet confirmed as sold. These are units held during the checkout process to prevent overselling while buyers complete their purchase.

This value increases when orders are placed and decreases when orders are fulfilled, cancelled, or reservations expire. Must be non-negative and cannot exceed total_quantity.

available_quantity.description:
Calculated available quantity for immediate purchase.

Derived value computed as (total_quantity minus reserved_quantity), representing the actual inventory available for new customer purchases. This is the quantity displayed to buyers in product listings and used in availability checks during checkout.

When this value reaches zero, the SKU becomes unavailable for purchase until restocked. This field is automatically recalculated whenever total_quantity or reserved_quantity changes.

low_stock_threshold.description:
Seller-configured threshold triggering low stock alerts.

When available_quantity falls below or equals this value, the system notifies sellers to restock. This threshold helps sellers maintain adequate inventory levels and avoid stockouts.

Default value is 10 units if not configured by the seller. Sellers can customize this threshold based on their restocking lead times and sales velocity.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory stock record was first created.

Records when inventory tracking was initially established for this SKU variant, typically when the seller first listed the product variant or added inventory for a newly created SKU.

This timestamp is immutable and provides the baseline for tracking the inventory record's age and history.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this inventory stock record was last modified.

Updated whenever quantity changes occur through restocking, sales, reservations, manual adjustments, or threshold modifications. Used for tracking inventory change frequency, cache invalidation, and audit purposes.

This field helps identify stale inventory data and supports real-time inventory synchronization across the platform.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for archived inventory records.

When set, indicates the inventory record has been archived but preserved for historical data integrity and audit trails. Soft-deleted records are excluded from active inventory queries but remain accessible for reporting and historical analysis.

Typically set when a SKU variant is discontinued or removed from the catalog, allowing the platform to maintain complete transaction history while hiding the SKU from active inventory management.

IShoppingMallInventoryStock.description:
Current inventory stock levels for each product SKU variant.

Tracks the real-time available quantity for each SKU across the platform. This entity maintains the single source of truth for how many units of each product variant are currently in stock and available for purchase.

Every SKU must have a corresponding inventory stock record to support purchase operations. When buyers add items to cart or place orders, the system validates against these stock levels to prevent overselling. Stock quantities are updated through inventory transactions (additions, sales, returns, adjustments).

The available quantity is calculated as total quantity minus reserved quantity. Reserved quantities represent units in pending checkouts that are temporarily held but not yet sold. Low stock thresholds trigger seller alerts when inventory falls below configured levels.

This table integrates with the order management system for inventory deduction on sales and restoration on cancellations. It provides real-time availability data to the product catalog for displaying stock status to buyers.

IShoppingMallSaleImage.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving paginated lists of product images associated with sale listings.

This schema defines the query parameters for advanced product image searches. It supports filtering by display order, image status, creation date ranges, and various metadata attributes. The schema enables sellers to efficiently manage large product image galleries and admins to moderate visual content across the platform.

Pagination and sorting capabilities ensure optimal performance when handling sales with extensive image collections. The search functionality is essential for organizing product presentations, reordering image galleries, and maintaining visual consistency across product listings.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Combined with limit to implement efficient data pagination for large image collections.

limit.description:
Maximum number of image records to return per page.
