Sort direction for the results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. Descending order is typically used for viewing recent transactions first, while ascending order supports chronological analysis from oldest to newest.

IShoppingMallInventoryTransaction.IReque.description:
Search and filter criteria for querying inventory transaction records.

Defines the complete set of parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating inventory transaction history. Supports flexible querying by SKU, transaction type, date ranges, with configurable sorting and pagination to efficiently navigate and analyze large transaction datasets.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing for broad queries (all transactions) or highly targeted searches (specific SKU, type, and date range). The combination of filters enables complex inventory analysis scenarios such as auditing specific product movements over defined periods or investigating particular types of inventory events.

id.description:
Unique identifier for this inventory reservation record.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the reservation and is automatically generated by the system when the reservation is created during the buyer checkout process. The ID is used to reference and update specific reservations throughout their lifecycle, from creation through expiration or completion.

Corresponds to the `id` column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Identifier of the product SKU variant for which inventory is reserved.

This foreign key references the specific product variant (SKU) in the shopping_mall_sale_skus table. Each reservation holds inventory for exactly one SKU, representing a specific product configuration with selected color, size, and other variant attributes. If a buyer's cart contains multiple SKUs, separate reservation records exist for each.

This field enables retrieval of product information, pricing details, and inventory availability for the reserved SKU. The SKU reference is immutable once the reservation is created, ensuring inventory accounting integrity.

Corresponds to {@link shopping_mall_sale_skus.id} in the Prisma schema.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Identifier of the buyer who owns this inventory reservation.

This foreign key references the authenticated buyer in the shopping_mall_buyers table. Reservations are tied to specific buyers to track who is holding the inventory during checkout. This buyer-reservation linkage prevents buyers from interfering with each other's reservations and enables proper authorization checks.

The buyer reference is immutable once the reservation is created. When buyers abandon checkout or the reservation expires, the buyer association is preserved for historical tracking and analytics purposes.

Corresponds to {@link shopping_mall_buyers.id} in the Prisma schema.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order created from this reservation when payment is confirmed.

This foreign key references the order in the shopping_mall_orders table that was created when the buyer successfully completed payment and the reservation was converted. Nullable until payment completes and order is created.

When null, indicates the reservation is still active, has expired without conversion, or was released before completing checkout. When populated with an order ID, establishes the link between the temporary inventory hold and the final purchase transaction.

This relationship enables tracking of the complete buyer journey from cart reservation through order fulfillment, and supports inventory audit trails showing how reserved quantities became sold quantities.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_order_id column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

reserved_quantity.description:
Number of inventory units reserved for this SKU.

This value represents how many units of the product variant are being held for the buyer during checkout. The reserved quantity reduces available inventory for other buyers until the reservation expires, is released, or is completed through purchase.

The quantity must be a positive integer and cannot exceed available stock at the time of reservation creation. During checkout, the system validates that sufficient inventory exists before creating the reservation. If inventory becomes insufficient due to concurrent purchases, the reservation may fail.

This field aligns with the reserved_quantity column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table, ensuring consistent naming across request, update, and entity representations.

reservation_status.description:
Current status of the inventory reservation.

Indicates the lifecycle state of this reservation, determining whether inventory is still held or has been released. Valid values correspond to distinct states: 'active' means inventory is currently reserved and holding, 'released' indicates manual cancellation before expiration (such as abandoned checkout), 'expired' means the time limit was reached and inventory was automatically released, and 'converted' indicates successful payment confirmation with order creation.

The status determines whether inventory is counted as reserved in availability calculations and affects how the reservation can be modified or cancelled. Status transitions follow business rules defined in the system, ensuring proper inventory accounting throughout the reservation lifecycle.

Corresponds to the reservation_status column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

expires_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation will automatically expire and release inventory.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicates when the system will automatically release the reserved inventory if the buyer hasn't completed their purchase. Typical reservation periods are 10-30 minutes, balancing buyer convenience (allowing sufficient time to complete checkout) with inventory availability (preventing indefinite locks on products).

When the expiration time is reached, the reservation status changes to 'expired' and the reserved quantity is returned to available inventory for other buyers to purchase. The expiration mechanism prevents abandoned checkouts from indefinitely holding inventory.

Corresponds to the `expires_at` column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation record was created.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime is automatically set by the system when the reservation is first created, typically when a buyer adds items to their cart and begins the checkout process. This field is immutable and provides audit trail information for tracking reservation history.

Used for chronological sorting of reservations, analyzing checkout patterns, and identifying stuck reservations that may need manual cleanup.

Corresponds to the `created_at` column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this reservation record was last modified.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime is automatically updated by the system whenever any field in the reservation is changed, such as status transitions (active to expired), quantity adjustments, or expiration time extensions. This field tracks the most recent modification for audit purposes and conflict resolution.

Used for tracking reservation lifecycle events and debugging reservation processing issues.

Corresponds to the `updated_at` column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations Prisma schema table.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.description:
Complete inventory reservation entity representing a temporary hold on product inventory during checkout.

Inventory reservations are critical components of the e-commerce checkout process that prevent overselling by temporarily holding product SKU inventory while buyers complete their purchases. When a buyer adds items to their cart and proceeds to checkout, the system creates reservation records to ensure those items remain available until the buyer finishes payment or the reservation expires.

Each reservation record tracks a specific quantity of a single SKU reserved for a particular buyer. The reservation has an expiration time (typically 10-30 minutes) after which the inventory is automatically released if the purchase isn't completed. This time-limited hold balances buyer convenience (allowing sufficient time to complete checkout) with inventory availability (preventing indefinite locks on products).

Reservations integrate with the broader inventory management system by deducting reserved quantities from available inventory calculations, preventing other buyers from purchasing items that are temporarily held. When reservations expire, are released, or are completed through purchase, the inventory accounting updates accordingly to maintain accurate availability information.

The reservation lifecycle follows these states: created as 'active' when checkout begins, transitions to 'converted' when purchase succeeds and payment is confirmed, changes to 'expired' if the time limit is reached without completion, or becomes 'released' if manually cancelled by the buyer abandoning checkout. Converted, expired, and released reservations provide historical data for inventory auditing and buyer behavior analysis.

This entity corresponds to the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table in the Prisma schema and is returned as the response body from inventory reservation search and monitoring operations. It provides complete reservation information including temporal data (creation time, expiration time, last update), quantity data (how many units reserved), relationship data (which buyer, which SKU, which order if converted), and status data (current reservation state).

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IReque.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying inventory reservations.

This request DTO enables comprehensive filtering and pagination of inventory reservation records. It supports queries by buyer, SKU, reservation status, reserved quantity ranges, and time ranges to facilitate reservation monitoring and management.

Users can search for active reservations to understand current inventory commitments, identify expired reservations that may need cleanup, track completed reservations linked to orders, or find cancelled reservations for audit purposes. The filtering capabilities enable sellers to monitor reservations for their products and administrators to oversee platform-wide reservation activity.

Pagination parameters ensure efficient handling of potentially large numbers of concurrent reservations across the marketplace.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Determines which subset of results to return when the total number of matching reservations exceeds the page size limit.

limit.description:
Maximum number of reservation records to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Accepts values between 1 and 100 to balance between data transfer efficiency and usability.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Filter reservations by specific buyer.

When provided, returns only reservations created by the specified buyer account. Useful for buyers viewing their own checkout sessions or admins investigating buyer-specific reservation patterns.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Filter reservations by specific product SKU variant.

When provided, returns only reservations for the specified SKU. Enables sellers to monitor inventory holds for particular product variants.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Filter reservations by associated order.

When provided, returns only reservations that have been converted to the specified order. Useful for tracking which reservations resulted in completed purchases or investigating order-reservation linkage.

This filter targets the shopping_mall_order_id foreign key field in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table, which references the order created when the reservation is successfully converted after payment confirmation.

reservation_status.description:
Filter reservations by current reservation status.

When provided, returns only reservations in the specified state. Valid values correspond to the reservation lifecycle: 'active' for currently holding inventory, 'released' for manually released or abandoned checkout, 'expired' for timeout occurred, and 'converted' for payment confirmed and converted to sale.

Useful for finding active holds, identifying expired reservations needing cleanup, or tracking converted reservations that became orders.

reserved_quantity_min.description:
Filter reservations with reserved quantity greater than or equal to this value.

Enables filtering by minimum reserved quantity to find large inventory holds or analyze reservation size patterns.

reserved_quantity_max.description:
Filter reservations with reserved quantity less than or equal to this value.

Enables filtering by maximum reserved quantity to find small inventory holds or limit results to specific quantity ranges.

reserved_after.description:
Filter reservations created on or after this timestamp.

Enables time-based queries to find recent reservations or analyze reservation patterns within specific time periods. Compares against the created_at timestamp of reservation records.

reserved_before.description:
Filter reservations created before this timestamp.

Enables time-based queries to find historical reservations or limit searches to specific time windows. Compares against the created_at timestamp of reservation records.

expires_after.description:
Filter reservations that expire on or after this timestamp.

Useful for finding long-duration reservations or those with extended expiration times. Compares against the expires_at field to identify reservations with specific expiration characteristics.

expires_before.description:
Filter reservations that expire before this timestamp.

Useful for identifying reservations about to expire or finding those with short expiration windows. Compares against the expires_at field to locate time-sensitive reservations.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines the ordering of returned reservations. Common use cases include sorting by created_at to see newest first, by expires_at to identify urgent reservations, by reserved_quantity to find large holds, or by updated_at to see recently modified reservations.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the specified sort field.

Controls whether results are returned in ascending or descending order based on the sort_by field.

reserved_quantity.description:
Updated quantity of inventory units reserved for this reservation.

This value represents the number of SKU units being held for the buyer during checkout. The quantity can be increased if the buyer adds more of the same item to their cart, or decreased if they reduce the quantity before completing purchase.

When increasing the reserved quantity, the system validates that sufficient unreserved inventory exists to fulfill the request. The new quantity cannot exceed the available stock for the SKU. When decreasing the quantity, the released units become available for other buyers to reserve or purchase.

Quantity updates must maintain inventory integrity - the system ensures that total reserved quantities across all active reservations plus sold quantities never exceed the physical inventory stock levels. This field corresponds to the reserved_quantity column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table.

reservation_status.description:
Updated status of the inventory reservation.

The reservation status indicates its current lifecycle state and determines whether the reserved inventory is still held or has been released back to available stock.

Status values have specific meanings as defined in the Prisma schema: 'active' indicates the reservation is currently holding inventory and has not expired, 'expired' means the reservation time limit was reached and inventory has been automatically released, 'released' indicates the reservation was manually released before expiration (such as when a buyer abandons checkout), and 'converted' means the reservation fulfilled its purpose when payment was confirmed and the order was created.

Status transitions follow specific rules: active reservations can be updated to released or expired, expired and released reservations cannot be reactivated, and converted reservations are immutable. Manual status updates are typically restricted to admin users for special cases or issue resolution. This field corresponds to the reservation_status column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table.

expires_at.description:
Updated expiration timestamp for this inventory reservation.

This ISO 8601 formatted datetime indicates when the reservation will automatically expire and release the reserved inventory back to available stock. Extending the expiration time gives buyers more time to complete their checkout process.

The expiration time must be set to a future timestamp - past or current times are not allowed. Typical reservation periods range from 10-30 minutes, balancing buyer convenience with inventory availability for other customers. The system automatically releases reservations when this timestamp is reached.

Business scenarios for updating expiration include: extending time for buyers who need additional time to enter payment information, shortening time if the buyer is taking too long and inventory demand is high, or set a new expiration after cart modifications that reset the checkout timer. This field corresponds to the expires_at column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order created from this reservation when payment is confirmed.

This optional field allows administrators to manually link a reservation to an order when converting the reservation to a completed sale. Typically set automatically by the system when payment processing succeeds and the reservation transitions to 'converted' status.

When null, indicates the reservation has not yet been converted to an order. When set to a valid order ID, establishes the relationship between the temporary inventory hold and the final order record. This field corresponds to the shopping_mall_order_id column in the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table and references the shopping_mall_orders table.

Manual updates to this field are restricted to admin users for special cases such as reconciling payment processing issues or correcting reservation-order linkage errors.

IShoppingMallInventoryReservation.IUpdat.description:
Data transfer object for updating an existing inventory reservation.

This DTO defines the mutable fields that can be modified on an inventory reservation after it has been created. Inventory reservations are temporary holds on product SKU inventory during the buyer's checkout process, preventing overselling while the buyer completes their purchase.

All fields in this update DTO are optional, following the partial update pattern. Only the fields provided in the request will be modified, while omitted fields retain their current values. This allows targeted updates such as only extending the expiration time or only adjusting the quantity without affecting other reservation parameters.

The update operation validates all provided values to ensure they maintain inventory integrity and follow business rules. For example, quantity increases are validated against available inventory, expiration times must be future timestamps, and status transitions must follow the allowed state machine.

This DTO corresponds to the shopping_mall_inventory_reservations table in the Prisma schema and is used in conjunction with the PUT operation on the /shoppingMall/admin/inventoryReservations/{reservationId} endpoint.

page.description:
Page number for pagination of cart items.

Specifies which page of results to return when the buyer's cart contains more items than the specified limit. Page numbering starts at 1. If omitted, defaults to the first page.

For buyers with large carts containing many items, pagination ensures efficient data retrieval and display. The page parameter works in conjunction with the limit parameter to determine which subset of cart items to return.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cart items to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, limiting how many cart items are included in a single response. Values typically range from 10 to 100 items per page. If omitted, a sensible default (such as 20) is applied.

Smaller limits provide faster response times and better mobile experience, while larger limits reduce the number of requests needed for buyers with many cart items. The maximum allowed value prevents excessive data transfer in a single request.

search.description:
Search query to filter cart items by product name or description.

Allows buyers to search within their cart contents by entering keywords that match against product names, descriptions, or other searchable attributes. This helps buyers quickly find specific items in large carts without scrolling through all items.

The search is case-insensitive and typically matches partial words. For example, searching for 'laptop' would find items like 'Gaming Laptop' or 'Laptop Stand'. If omitted, no text-based filtering is applied.

category_ids.description:
Filter cart items by product category identifiers.

Restricts results to cart items whose products belong to the specified categories. Multiple category IDs can be provided to filter by several categories simultaneously. This allows buyers to view only cart items from specific product categories.

Category filtering is particularly useful for buyers organizing their carts by product type, such as viewing only electronics or only clothing items. If omitted, cart items from all categories are included in the results.

min_price.description:
Minimum price threshold for filtering cart items.

Filters cart items to include only those with a unit price greater than or equal to this value. The price is specified in the platform's base currency (typically USD). This allows buyers to filter their cart by price range, such as viewing only higher-priced items.

Price filtering helps buyers organize their carts and make purchasing decisions based on budget constraints. When combined with max_price, it creates a price range filter. If omitted, no minimum price restriction is applied.

max_price.description:
Maximum price threshold for filtering cart items.

Filters cart items to include only those with a unit price less than or equal to this value. The price is specified in the platform's base currency. This enables buyers to view cart items within a specific price range or budget.

When used with min_price, creates a price range filter allowing buyers to focus on items within their target budget. If omitted, no maximum price restriction is applied.

oneOf.description:
Filter cart items by product availability status.

Restricts results based on whether products are currently in stock. The 'in_stock' value shows only items available for immediate purchase, 'out_of_stock' shows only items that are currently unavailable, and 'all' includes items regardless of availability.

This filter helps buyers identify which items in their cart can be purchased immediately versus which items they may need to remove or wait for restocking. Product availability can change between when items are added to cart and when the buyer views their cart, so this filter provides current status information.

If omitted, defaults to showing all items regardless of availability status, but the response includes availability information for each item so buyers can make informed decisions.

oneOf.description:
Sorting criterion for ordering cart items in the response.

Determines the order in which cart items are returned. Available options include: 'date_added' sorts by when items were added to the cart (most recent first), 'price_asc' sorts by price from lowest to highest, 'price_desc' sorts by price from highest to lowest, 'name_asc' sorts alphabetically by product name A-Z, and 'name_desc' sorts reverse alphabetically by product name Z-A.

Sorting helps buyers organize their cart view according to their preferences, such as reviewing recently added items or organizing by price for budget planning. If omitted, a default sort order (typically by date added descending) is applied.
