id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the order.

This UUID serves as the permanent, immutable identifier for the order throughout its entire lifecycle. It is used as the primary reference in all related tables including order items, payment transactions, status histories, and shipping records.

The ID is generated automatically when the order is created and never changes, providing a stable reference point for tracking orders across the system.

order_number.description:
Unique order number displayed to buyers and used for tracking. Format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN.

This human-readable order number is shown to customers in confirmation emails, invoices, and the order history interface. It follows a structured format that includes the order creation date and a sequential number for easy identification.

Unlike the internal UUID, this order number is designed for customer-facing contexts and customer service interactions. It provides an easier way for buyers to reference their orders when contacting support or tracking shipments.

status.description:
Current order status indicating the order's position in its lifecycle.

Represents the current state of the order as it progresses from creation through payment, fulfillment, and delivery. Valid status values include: pending_payment, payment_confirmed, processing, ready_to_ship, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, completed, cancelled_payment_failed, cancelled_buyer_request, cancelled_seller_unavailable, cancelled_admin_action, delivery_failed, returned_to_sender, refund_requested, refund_approved, refund_denied, refunded.

The status is updated throughout the order lifecycle and tracked in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table for complete audit trail. This field enables users to quickly understand the current state of each order in list views.

subtotal.description:
Sum of all order item line totals before shipping and taxes.

Represents the base cost of all items in the order calculated as the sum of (item price × quantity) for each order item. This amount does not include shipping costs, taxes, or discounts.

The subtotal is a key component of the order total calculation: total_amount = subtotal + shipping_total + tax_total - discount_total. Displaying the subtotal in order summaries helps buyers understand how the final total is composed.

shipping_total.description:
Total shipping cost for all items in the order across all sellers.

Represents the combined shipping fees charged for delivering all items in the order. In multi-seller orders, this may include shipping costs from multiple sellers aggregated into a single total.

Shipping costs are calculated based on the selected shipping method, destination address, item weights and dimensions, and seller shipping policies. This field helps buyers understand the delivery cost component of their order total.

tax_total.description:
Total tax amount charged on the order.

Represents the sum of all applicable taxes (sales tax, VAT, etc.) calculated based on the order subtotal, shipping charges, buyer's delivery address, and applicable tax regulations. Tax calculation considers product tax categories, seller locations, and jurisdictional tax rules.

The tax total is added to the subtotal and shipping cost when calculating the final order amount. Displaying the tax separately helps buyers understand the tax component of their purchase and ensures transparency in pricing.

discount_total.description:
Total discount amount applied to the order from promotions or coupons.

Represents the sum of all discounts applied to the order, including promotional codes, coupon discounts, bulk purchase discounts, loyalty rewards, and any other price reductions. Discounts may be applied at the item level, order level, or shipping level.

The discount total is subtracted from the sum of subtotal, shipping, and taxes when calculating the final order amount. Showing the total savings helps buyers understand the value they're receiving and encourages future purchases.

total_amount.description:
Final total amount paid by buyer.

This is the complete order total calculated as subtotal + shipping_total + tax_total - discount_total. It represents the actual amount charged to the buyer's payment method and is the definitive cost of the order.

The total amount is prominently displayed in order summaries and is the primary metric for order value analysis, revenue reporting, and financial reconciliation.

estimated_delivery_start.description:
Earliest estimated delivery date based on shipping method and processing time.

Provides the start of the estimated delivery window, calculated from the order creation time, seller processing time, and selected shipping method transit duration. This helps buyers understand when they can expect to receive their order.

May be null if the delivery estimate has not been calculated yet (e.g., for pending_payment orders) or if the shipping method does not provide delivery estimates. Updated when the order ships with more accurate tracking information.

Displayed in order list views to help buyers prioritize and track expected deliveries without needing to open order details.

estimated_delivery_end.description:
Latest estimated delivery date based on shipping method and processing time.

Provides the end of the estimated delivery window, representing the latest date by which the order should arrive. Combined with estimated_delivery_start, this creates a delivery timeframe that accounts for variability in processing and shipping.

May be null if the delivery estimate has not been calculated yet or if the shipping method does not provide delivery estimates. The estimate becomes more precise once the order ships and tracking information is available.

Showing the delivery window in order summaries helps buyers plan for order receipt and identifies orders that may need attention if they're approaching or past the estimated delivery date.

actual_delivery_at.description:
Actual delivery timestamp when package was successfully delivered to recipient.

Records the precise moment when the order was confirmed as delivered, typically based on carrier tracking confirmation or recipient signature. This timestamp represents successful completion of the delivery process.

Remains null for orders that have not yet been delivered. Once set, this timestamp is used to calculate actual delivery times, measure carrier performance, determine when the buyer can leave reviews, and trigger post-delivery workflows such as payment release to sellers.

Displaying the actual delivery time in order summaries helps buyers confirm receipt and provides definitive proof of delivery for customer service purposes.

cancelled_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was cancelled.

Records the exact moment when the order was cancelled, whether by the buyer, seller, or system administrator. This timestamp marks the transition to one of the cancelled status states (cancelled_payment_failed, cancelled_buyer_request, cancelled_seller_unavailable, or cancelled_admin_action).

Remains null for orders that have not been cancelled. Used to track cancellation rates, measure time-to-cancellation, enforce cancellation policies (e.g., preventing cancellation after certain stages), and calculate refund processing timelines.

Showing the cancellation timestamp in order summaries helps users understand when the cancellation occurred and supports customer service in resolving cancellation-related inquiries.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order reached completed status after successful delivery and completion period.

Records when the order was marked as completed, typically after a confirmation period following delivery during which the buyer can report issues or request returns. Completion signifies that the transaction is finalized and the seller can expect payment release.

Remains null for orders that have not reached completed status. This timestamp triggers final payment processing to sellers, enables buyers to leave reviews, archives the order from active fulfillment queues, and marks the end of the order lifecycle for analytics purposes.

Displaying the completion timestamp helps users understand when the order was finalized and supports revenue recognition calculations for financial reporting.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was created and placed by the buyer.

Records the exact moment when the order was submitted and entered the system, typically when the buyer completed the checkout process. This timestamp is immutable and serves as the official order creation time for all business purposes.

Used for sorting orders chronologically, calculating processing times, determining applicable pricing and promotions, and generating time-based reports. Displayed in order lists to help users identify recent orders and understand order age.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the order record was last modified.

Tracks the most recent update to any field in the order record, automatically updated whenever the order is modified. This includes status changes, address updates, amount adjustments, or any other field modifications.

Useful for identifying recently changed orders, tracking order modification history, synchronizing data across systems, and auditing order changes. The updated timestamp helps administrators identify orders requiring attention and supports cache invalidation strategies.

IShoppingMallOrder.ISummary.description:
Lightweight order summary for list displays and references.

Provides essential order information optimized for order list views, search results, and embedded references in other entities such as refund transactions and payout records. This summary variant includes key identifiers, current status, pricing breakdown, and delivery estimates without the full order details.

The summary includes enough information for buyers to quickly scan their orders, track deliveries, and understand costs, while sellers can identify orders requiring action and monitor fulfillment progress. Administrators use summaries for order oversight and reporting.

For complete order details including item breakdowns, payment information, and full status history, use the detail DTO via GET /orders/{orderId} endpoint.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the order record used for internal references and API operations.
Generated automatically upon order creation.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who placed this order.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_buyers table. Identifies the authenticated buyer account that created and owns this order. Used for authorization checks, order filtering, and buyer-specific order queries.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_buyer_id column in the shopping_mall_orders Prisma schema.

shopping_mall_buyer_address_id.description:
Delivery address for this order.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_buyer_addresses table. Captures the selected delivery address at time of order placement. Ensures order fulfillment uses correct shipping destination even if buyer modifies their address book after order creation.

Corresponds to the shopping_mall_buyer_address_id column in the shopping_mall_orders Prisma schema.

order_number.description:
Unique order number displayed to buyers and used for tracking.

Format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN where YYYYMMDD is the order date and NNNNNN is a sequential number.
Used for customer service inquiries, order tracking, and buyer communication.

status.description:
Current order status.

Valid values: pending_payment, payment_confirmed, processing, ready_to_ship, shipped, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, completed, cancelled_payment_failed, cancelled_buyer_request, cancelled_seller_unavailable, cancelled_admin_action, delivery_failed, returned_to_sender, refund_requested, refund_approved, refund_denied, refunded.

Determines order visibility, available actions, and workflow progression.

buyer.description:
Buyer who placed this order.

Provides buyer information for order fulfillment, customer service, and communication.
References the authenticated buyer account that created this order.

deliveryAddress.description:
Delivery address for this order.

Captured snapshot of the selected delivery address at time of order placement.
Ensures order fulfillment uses correct shipping destination even if buyer modifies their address book.

subtotal.description:
Sum of all order item line totals before shipping and taxes.

Calculated by summing line_total from all order items.
Represents total product cost excluding shipping fees, taxes, and discounts.

shipping_total.description:
Total shipping cost for all items in the order across all sellers.

Sum of shipping costs from all seller sub-orders.
Represents total delivery charges paid by buyer.

tax_total.description:
Total tax amount charged on the order.

Calculated based on applicable tax rates for the delivery address jurisdiction.
Includes sales tax, VAT, or other applicable taxes.

discount_total.description:
Total discount amount applied to the order from promotions or coupons.

Sum of all discounts applied at item level and order level.
Reduces the final amount paid by buyer.

total_amount.description:
Final total amount paid by buyer.

Calculated as subtotal + shipping_total + tax_total - discount_total.
Represents the actual payment amount charged to buyer's payment method.

estimated_delivery_start.description:
Earliest estimated delivery date based on shipping method and processing time.

Provides buyer with expected delivery window start.
Calculated from order date, seller processing time, and carrier transit time.

estimated_delivery_end.description:
Latest estimated delivery date based on shipping method and processing time.

Provides buyer with expected delivery window end.
Used for setting buyer expectations and tracking delayed orders.

actual_delivery_at.description:
Actual delivery timestamp when package was successfully delivered to recipient.

Confirmed by carrier tracking or recipient confirmation.
Triggers completion workflow and review eligibility.

cancelled_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was cancelled.

Records cancellation time for audit trail and refund processing.
Set when order transitions to any cancelled status.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the order reached completed status after successful delivery and completion period.

Marks the final successful state of order lifecycle.
Triggers seller payout eligibility and closes dispute window.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for order archival.

When set, the order is marked as deleted and hidden from active buyer views while being retained for historical records, audit trails, and compliance purposes. Soft deletion preserves all order data including items, status history, and payment information for administrative review and regulatory reporting.

Deleted orders are filtered from normal buyer and seller queries but remain fully accessible through administrative interfaces for customer support, dispute resolution, and financial reconciliation.

sellers.description:
Seller-specific portions of the multi-seller order.

Array of sub-orders representing items from each seller.
Each seller processes and fulfills their portion independently.

items.description:
Individual line items within the order representing purchased products.

Each item represents one product SKU variant with quantity and pricing captured at purchase time.
Used for order fulfillment, invoicing, and buyer order history.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the order was created and placed by the buyer.

Marks the beginning of the order lifecycle.
Used for order history sorting, analytics, and reporting.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the order record was last modified.

Automatically updated on any order field changes.
Used for tracking order modification history and sync operations.

IShoppingMallOrder.description:
Parent order record representing a buyer's complete purchase transaction.

Stores the main order information including buyer, delivery address, payment details, and order totals.
Serves as the parent entity for multi-seller orders where items come from different sellers.

Each order is created when a buyer completes checkout and payment is confirmed.
The order may contain items from multiple sellers, with each seller portion tracked in seller sub-orders.
Order items are stored separately referencing specific product SKUs.

Order status progresses through a defined lifecycle tracked in status histories.
Buyers can independently search, filter, and manage their orders including cancellation and refund requests.

IShoppingMallOrder.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new order from shopping cart items with payment processing.

This DTO captures all information required for the complete checkout workflow including cart item selection, shipping address, payment method, and delivery preferences. The order creation operation transforms selected cart items into a confirmed purchase order with payment processing, inventory reservation, and multi-seller order splitting.

Security considerations: The buyer_id is automatically injected from the authenticated user's JWT token and must never be accepted from the request body. All referenced entities (cart items, shipping address, payment method) must be owned by the authenticated buyer. The operation validates inventory availability, processes payment, and creates inventory reservations atomically.

This schema maps to the shopping_mall_orders table in the Prisma database schema and drives the creation of associated records in shopping_mall_order_sellers, shopping_mall_order_items, shopping_mall_inventory_reservations, and shopping_mall_payment_transactions tables.

cart_item_ids.description:
List of shopping cart item IDs to include in this order.

Specifies which items from the buyer's cart should be converted into this order. All cart items must belong to the authenticated buyer and must be currently available with sufficient inventory. The operation validates each cart item's availability before proceeding with order creation. After successful order creation, these cart items are automatically removed from the cart.

buyer_address_id.description:
ID of the buyer's saved shipping address to use for order delivery.

References an existing address in the buyer_addresses table that belongs to the authenticated buyer. The selected address will be used for shipping label generation, delivery logistics, and shipping cost calculations. The address is captured at order creation time and typically remains fixed even if the buyer later modifies their saved addresses.

payment_method_id.description:
ID of the buyer's saved payment method to use for this order.

References an existing payment instrument in the payment_methods table that belongs to the authenticated buyer. The selected payment method will be charged for the order total including items, shipping, and taxes. Payment processing occurs synchronously during order creation.

notes.description:
Optional buyer-provided notes or special instructions for the order.

Allows buyers to communicate delivery preferences, gift messages, special handling requests, or other contextual information to sellers. These notes are visible to sellers during order fulfillment and may influence packaging, delivery timing, or customer service interactions. Maximum length should be reasonable for display purposes.

shipping_address_id.description:
Unique identifier of the delivery address for order shipment.

This references a saved buyer address from the shopping_mall_buyer_addresses table. Buyers can update the shipping address for orders that haven't been shipped yet, allowing them to correct address errors or redirect shipments to different locations before fulfillment begins.

Maps to the shopping_mall_buyer_address_id foreign key column in the shopping_mall_orders table.

IShoppingMallOrder.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an existing order's mutable properties.

This DTO represents the fields that can be modified after an order has been placed but before it enters non-editable states in the order lifecycle. Only specific order properties are editable to maintain order integrity and prevent fraud. Fields like order totals, purchased items, payment information, and buyer identity are immutable once the order is created.

The update operation is subject to business rules that prevent modifications to orders that are already being processed, shipped, or delivered. Typical use cases include correcting shipping addresses before order fulfillment begins.

Security validation ensures only the order owner can update the order, and the order must be in a state that allows modifications. All updates are tracked in the order audit trail.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the delivery address record.

recipient_name.description:
Full name of the recipient who will receive deliveries at this address.

Displayed on shipping labels and delivery confirmations.

street_address_line1.description:
Primary street address line containing street number, street name, and unit/apartment/suite number if applicable.

Core address component for delivery location.

city.description:
City or district name for the delivery address.

Used for carrier routing and delivery zone determination.

state.description:
State, province, or region name for the delivery address.

Required for carrier routing and shipping cost calculation.

postal_code.description:
Postal code, ZIP code, or postcode for the delivery address.

Required for precise delivery location.

country.description:
Country name for the delivery address.

Required for international shipping validation.

address_label.description:
Custom label assigned by buyer for easy address identification.

Examples: Home, Office, Parents House.

IShoppingMallBuyerAddress.ISummary.description:
Lightweight delivery address representation for order references.

Provides essential address information for order displays and shipping labels.
Excludes optional fields and delivery instructions for concise summary.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the seller sub-order record.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Parent order this seller portion belongs to.

References the main order containing this seller's items.

shopping_mall_seller_id.description:
Seller fulfilling this portion of the order.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_sellers table identifying which merchant is responsible for fulfilling this seller sub-order segment. This field establishes the direct database relationship between the order seller segment and the seller account.

Used for seller identification, authorization checks, and payout processing. The seller object provides the denormalized seller details while this field maintains referential integrity at the database level.

sub_order_number.description:
Unique sub-order number for this seller portion.

Format: ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN-S# where S# indicates seller sequence number.
Used for seller fulfillment tracking and buyer communication.

status.description:
Current status for this seller's portion.

Same status values as parent order but tracked independently for seller-specific fulfillment.
Allows each seller to progress through their fulfillment workflow independently.

seller.description:
Seller fulfilling this portion of the order.

Provides seller information for order fulfillment coordination and buyer communication.
References the merchant account responsible for shipping these items.

subtotal.description:
Sum of all item line totals for this seller's items before shipping and taxes.

Calculated from items belonging to this seller sub-order.
Used for seller payout calculation.

shipping_cost.description:
Shipping cost for this seller's items based on selected shipping method.

Charged to buyer and included in seller payout after platform commission.
Calculated based on shipping method, destination, and package dimensions.

shipping_method.description:
Shipping method selected for this seller's items.

Valid values: standard, express, next_day, economy, international.
Determines delivery timeline and shipping cost.

tracking_number.description:
Carrier tracking number provided by seller when order is shipped.

Enables buyer to track package delivery progress.
Required when seller marks order as shipped.

carrier_name.description:
Shipping carrier name for tracking and delivery.

Examples: UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL.
Provided by seller when order is shipped.

shipped_at.description:
Timestamp when seller marked this sub-order as shipped and provided tracking.

Triggers buyer notification with tracking information.
Used for calculating delivery estimates.

delivered_at.description:
Timestamp when carrier confirmed delivery for this seller's shipment.

Updated from carrier tracking API or manual confirmation.
Triggers completion workflow and review eligibility.

items.description:
Order items belonging to this seller sub-order.

Filtered subset of parent order items that this seller is responsible for fulfilling.
Used for seller fulfillment workflow and payout calculation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller sub-order was created from the parent order.

Marks when the order was split into seller-specific portions.
Used for seller order history and fulfillment tracking.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this seller sub-order was last modified.

Automatically updated on fulfillment status changes, tracking updates, or other modifications.
Used for sync operations and audit trails.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this seller sub-order.

When set, marks the seller sub-order as logically deleted while preserving historical order data.
Enables data retention for audit trails and historical reporting without physical deletion.

Null for active seller sub-orders that have not been deleted.

IShoppingMallOrderSeller.description:
Seller-specific portion of a multi-seller order.

When a buyer's order contains items from multiple sellers, the order is split into sub-orders for each seller.
Each sub-order is represented by one record, containing seller-specific information and totals.

Each seller processes and fulfills their portion of the order independently with their own shipping and tracking.
The parent order maintains the buyer's unified view while this enables seller-specific fulfillment workflows.

id.description:
Primary Key.

Unique identifier for the order item record.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Parent order this item belongs to.

References the main order containing this line item.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order this item is part of for multi-seller order management.

References the specific seller portion containing this item.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Product SKU variant that was purchased.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_sale_skus table identifying the exact product variant ordered. This field establishes the direct database relationship between the order item and the product SKU variant.

Used for inventory tracking, product identification, and linking to current product information. The saleSku object provides the denormalized SKU details while this field maintains referential integrity at the database level.

saleSku.description:
Product SKU variant that was purchased.

References the specific product variant selected by buyer.
Provides link to current product information while preserving purchase-time snapshot.

product_name.description:
Product name captured at time of purchase for historical accuracy.

Preserves product title even if seller later modifies the product listing.
Displayed in order history and invoices.

sku_code.description:
SKU code captured at time of purchase for reference.

Preserves SKU identifier for inventory reconciliation and order fulfillment.
Used for matching ordered items to seller inventory.

variant_attributes.description:
JSON string capturing selected variant attributes at time of purchase.

Example: {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}.
Preserves exact product configuration ordered by buyer.

unit_price.description:
Price per unit at the time of purchase.

Captures the actual price paid per item, preserving historical pricing.
Used for accurate order totals and refund calculations.

quantity.description:
Number of units purchased for this line item.

Must be a positive integer.
Used for calculating line totals and inventory adjustments.

line_total.description:
Total price for this line item calculated as unit_price × quantity.

Represents the subtotal for this specific item before discounts.
Used for order subtotal calculation.

discount_amount.description:
Discount amount applied to this specific line item from promotions or coupons.

Item-level discount reducing the line total.
Separately tracked from order-level discounts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item was created as part of order placement.

Matches parent order creation time.
Used for order history and analytics.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item record was last modified.

Automatically updated on any item changes.
Used for tracking modifications and sync operations.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order item.

When set, marks the order item as logically deleted while preserving historical order data and maintaining referential integrity with the parent order.
Enables data retention for audit trails, refund processing, and historical reporting without physical deletion.

Null for active order items that have not been deleted.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.description:
Individual line items within an order representing purchased products.

Each record represents one product SKU variant purchased with specific quantity and pricing.
Order items capture product information as it existed at the time of purchase for historical accuracy.

Items reference the specific sale SKU variant purchased, preserving color, size, and option selections.
Pricing is captured at order time to maintain accurate records even if product prices change later.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this payment transaction record.

Generated as a UUID v4 value upon transaction creation.
Used to track and reference this specific payment processing attempt across all reconciliation and audit operations.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key to the order this payment transaction is processing.

References shopping_mall_orders.id.
Establishes which order purchase this payment is for.
Multiple transactions may exist for one order due to authorization, capture, and potential retry attempts.

order.description:
Summary information about the order being paid for with this transaction.

Provides essential order context including order number and total amount.
Useful for payment reconciliation and financial reporting views.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Foreign key to the buyer who initiated this payment.

References shopping_mall_buyers.id.
Establishes buyer accountability for payment processing attempts.
Required for payment history tracking and fraud analysis.

buyer.description:
Summary information about the buyer who initiated this payment.

Provides essential buyer identification for administrative and reconciliation purposes.
Useful when reviewing transaction history and investigating payment issues.

shopping_mall_payment_method_id.description:
Foreign key to the payment method used for this transaction.

References shopping_mall_payment_methods.id.
Null if buyer entered payment details directly at checkout without using a saved payment method.
Useful for tracking which saved payment instruments are being used successfully.

paymentMethod.description:
Summary of the saved payment method used for this transaction.

Null if buyer entered payment details directly without using a saved method.
Provides payment instrument identification for transaction reconciliation.

transaction_type.description:
Type of payment transaction indicating the operation being performed.

Valid values: authorization, capture, void, refund.
Authorization holds funds on the payment method, capture completes the payment transfer.
Void cancels an authorization, refund returns captured funds to the buyer.
Determines the financial effect and reversibility of the transaction.

amount.description:
Transaction amount in the order's currency.

Stored as decimal value for precise financial calculations without floating-point errors.
For authorization and capture, equals the order total or partial amount.
For refunds, represents the amount being returned to the buyer.
Always positive - transaction_type indicates the direction of fund movement.

currency.description:
Currency code for the transaction amount.

Three-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD, EUR, GBP.
Must match the order's currency for consistency.
Required for multi-currency platform support and accurate financial reporting.

status.description:
Current status of this payment transaction in its lifecycle.

Valid values: pending, authorized, captured, failed, voided, refunded.
Pending indicates processing in progress, authorized means funds are held, captured means payment completed.
Failed indicates the payment provider rejected the transaction.
Voided means an authorization was cancelled, refunded means captured funds were returned.
Status transitions are immutable - new transaction records are created for state changes.

provider.description:
Payment service provider that processed this transaction.

Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree.
Identifies which payment processor's API was used.
Required for routing support requests and reconciliation to the correct provider.

provider_transaction_id.description:
Unique transaction identifier assigned by the payment provider.

Used for reconciliation with provider transaction records and dispute resolution.
Null for transactions that failed before reaching the provider.
Required for successful transactions to enable refunds and chargebacks.

provider_response.description:
Raw JSON response from the payment provider for this transaction.

Stored for debugging, reconciliation, and regulatory compliance purposes.
Contains provider-specific transaction details including authorization codes and risk scores.
Useful for investigating payment failures and resolving customer disputes.

failure_reason.description:
Human-readable reason for transaction failure if status is failed.

Examples: insufficient_funds, card_declined, invalid_card, fraud_detected, network_error.
Null for successful transactions.
Helps customer support and buyers understand why payment didn't process.
May be displayed to buyers or used for automated retry logic.

failure_code.description:
Provider-specific error code for failed transactions.

Machine-readable code enabling detailed error analysis and conditional retry logic.
Null for successful transactions.
Used by payment processing system to determine if transaction should be retried automatically.

ip_address.description:
IP address from which the payment was initiated.

Captured for fraud detection, security auditing, and geographic analysis.
Used to identify suspicious payment patterns and potential account compromise.
May be null for server-initiated transactions like scheduled subscription payments.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string for the payment request.

Captured for fraud analysis and device fingerprinting.
Helps identify automated attacks and unusual device patterns.
May be null for server-initiated transactions or API-based payments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment transaction was initiated.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Immutable audit timestamp establishing exact time of payment attempt.
Used for transaction sequencing, financial reporting, and reconciliation with payment provider records.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.description:
Complete payment transaction record for order purchases.

Immutable audit record tracking all payment processing attempts and outcomes for orders.
Each order payment progresses through authorization, capture, and confirmation stages tracked via transaction status.

Payment transactions maintain complete financial history including amount, payment method, provider transaction ID, and processing timestamps.
Supports multiple states throughout the payment lifecycle from pending authorization through successful capture or failure.

The platform uses payment provider tokens to process payments securely without storing sensitive card data.
All transactions record the payment provider's response for reconciliation and dispute resolution.

Refund transactions are tracked separately in shopping_mall_refund_transactions table.
This ensures clean audit trails and supports partial refunds without corrupting original payment records.

IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.description:
Historical record of all order status transitions for complete audit trail.

Captures every status change throughout the order lifecycle including timestamps and the actor who triggered the change.
Provides transparency into order progression from placement through completion, cancellation, or refund.

Each record represents a single status transition with the previous status, new status, and optional change reason.
The actor type and actor ID identify whether the change was triggered by buyer, seller, admin, or system automation.

This snapshot table enables audit trail review, dispute resolution, and performance analytics on order processing speed.

id.description:
Primary Key uniquely identifying this order status history record.

Generated as a UUID v4 value upon status transition record creation.
Used to track and reference specific status change events in the audit trail.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key to the order whose status changed.

References shopping_mall_orders.id.
Establishes which order this status transition belongs to.
Multiple status history records exist for each order tracking its complete lifecycle.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Foreign key to the seller sub-order whose status changed.

References shopping_mall_order_sellers.id.
Used for tracking seller-specific fulfillment progress when orders contain items from multiple sellers.
Null for order-level status changes that affect the entire order rather than individual seller portions.

previous_status.description:
Order status before this transition occurred.

Captures the state the order was in prior to this status change.
Null for the initial status history record when the order is first created.
Useful for understanding the status flow and validating legitimate status transitions.

new_status.description:
Order status after this transition occurred.

Represents the new state the order moved to at the recorded timestamp.
Valid values align with order status enumeration: pending_payment, payment_confirmed, processing, ready_to_ship, shipped, in_transit, delivered, completed, cancelled, refunded.
This field is the primary indicator of what status change this history record represents.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor who triggered the status change.

Valid values: buyer, seller, admin, system.
Identifies the category of entity that initiated this status transition.
System indicates automated status changes from scheduled jobs or event-driven workflows.
Required for audit accountability and understanding manual vs automated status progression.

actor_id.description:
ID of the actor who triggered the status change.

References the specific buyer_id, seller_id, admin_id, or system identifier who initiated the transition.
Combined with actor_type provides complete identification of who made the change.
Null for system-initiated automatic transitions where no specific user triggered the change.

change_reason.description:
Optional explanation or reason for the status change provided by the actor.

Free-text field allowing actors to document why they triggered this status transition.
Particularly useful for manual changes like cancellations or admin interventions.
Helps customer service understand the context and reasoning behind status changes for dispute resolution.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the actor when the status change occurred for security audit.

Captured for fraud detection and security investigation purposes.
Used to identify suspicious patterns or unauthorized access attempts.
Null for system-initiated automated status changes or when IP cannot be determined.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change occurred.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Immutable audit timestamp establishing exact moment of status transition.
Critical for order tracking, SLA monitoring, and analyzing order processing performance.

id.description:
Primary key identifier of the order cancellation request.

This UUID serves as the unique identifier for the cancellation record and is auto-generated by the system upon creation. It is used in API operations to reference specific cancellation requests, such as when admins review and update cancellation statuses or when tracking cancellation history.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order being cancelled.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_orders.id and links the cancellation request to the specific order that the buyer wants to cancel. The order must exist and belong to the requesting buyer. This relationship enables the system to validate cancellation eligibility, process refunds correctly, and maintain referential integrity.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order being cancelled for multi-seller order partial cancellations.

This optional foreign key references shopping_mall_order_sellers.id and identifies which specific seller's portion of a multi-seller order is being cancelled. When null, the cancellation applies to the entire order rather than a specific seller segment.

This field enables partial cancellations in marketplace scenarios where a single order contains items from multiple sellers, allowing buyers to cancel individual seller portions independently.

requested_by_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who requested the cancellation if buyer-initiated.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_buyers.id and identifies the authenticated buyer who submitted the cancellation request. The buyer_id is automatically populated from the JWT token during cancellation creation and cannot be modified.

This field is null when the cancellation is seller-initiated or admin-initiated rather than buyer-initiated. The field ensures accountability and enables buyers to track their own cancellation history.

requested_by_seller_id.description:
Seller who requested the cancellation if seller-initiated.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_sellers.id and identifies the seller who initiated the cancellation request. Sellers may initiate cancellations when they cannot fulfill orders due to inventory issues, pricing errors, or operational problems.

This field is null when the cancellation is buyer-initiated or admin-initiated. It provides accountability for seller-initiated cancellations and enables tracking of seller fulfillment reliability.

requested_by_admin_id.description:
Admin who requested the cancellation if admin-initiated.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_admins.id and identifies the platform administrator who initiated the cancellation. Admins may cancel orders for fraud detection, policy violations, or dispute resolution.

This field is null when the cancellation is buyer-initiated or seller-initiated. It maintains audit trails for administrative interventions in the order lifecycle.

approved_by_seller_id.description:
Seller who approved the cancellation request if seller approval was required.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_sellers.id and records which seller approved the cancellation request. In some business workflows, seller approval may be required before a buyer-initiated cancellation can proceed.

This field is null when seller approval is not required or when the cancellation has not yet been approved. It provides accountability for seller decisions in the cancellation workflow.

approved_by_admin_id.description:
Admin who approved the cancellation request if admin approval was required.

This foreign key references shopping_mall_admins.id and records which administrator approved the cancellation request. Admin approval is typically required for high-value orders, disputed cancellations, or policy exceptions.

This field is null when admin approval is not required or when the cancellation has not yet been approved. It maintains audit trails for administrative decisions.

cancellation_reason.description:
Reason code for cancellation.

This required field contains a standardized reason code explaining why the cancellation was requested. Valid values include: buyer_changed_mind, buyer_ordered_by_mistake, seller_out_of_stock, seller_cannot_deliver, seller_product_discontinued, seller_pricing_error, admin_fraud_detected, admin_policy_violation, payment_failed, other.

The reason code enables systematic analysis of cancellation patterns, helps identify problematic sellers or products, and supports data-driven business decisions. It works in conjunction with cancellation_explanation for complete context.

cancellation_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation or notes about the cancellation reason provided by the requestor.

This optional field contains free-form text providing additional context beyond the standardized cancellation_reason code. It may include specific details, customer concerns, or operational notes that help reviewers understand the situation.

The explanation is valuable for customer service, dispute resolution, and understanding edge cases that standard reason codes cannot fully capture.

approval_status.description:
Current approval status of the cancellation request.

This field tracks the lifecycle state of the cancellation request. Valid values and their meanings:

- pending: Initial state when request is submitted, awaiting review
- auto_approved: Automatically approved based on business rules (e.g., order not yet processed)
- seller_approved: Approved by the seller for their portion of the order
- admin_approved: Approved by platform administrator after manual review
- denied: Request was rejected, order continues normal fulfillment
- expired: Request expired without action (e.g., order already shipped, time limit exceeded)

Status transitions trigger different business workflows, refund processing, and inventory adjustments. Each transition is audited with corresponding timestamps (approved_at, denied_at, completed_at).

refund_amount.description:
Amount refunded to buyer as a result of this cancellation.

This field records the monetary value refunded when the cancellation is approved and processed. The refund amount may differ from the original order total due to partial cancellations, restocking fees, promotional discounts, or payment processing fees.

This field is null when the cancellation is pending, denied, or expired. It is populated when the refund transaction is executed, providing financial transparency and enabling reconciliation reporting.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation was requested.

This required field records the exact date and time when the cancellation request was submitted by the buyer, seller, or admin. It serves as the starting point for the cancellation workflow timeline.

The timestamp is used for calculating processing times, determining if cancellations are within allowed time windows, and generating audit reports. It is automatically set by the system and cannot be modified.

approved_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation was approved.

This field records when the cancellation request was approved (auto_approved, seller_approved, or admin_approved). It marks the transition from pending review to approved status and triggers refund processing workflows.

This field is null when the cancellation is still pending, was denied, or expired. It provides accountability for approval timing and helps measure cancellation processing efficiency.

denied_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was denied.

This field records when the cancellation request was rejected by a seller or administrator. It marks the point at which the order returned to normal fulfillment processing.

This field is null when the cancellation was not denied (approved, pending, or expired instead). It supports audit trails and helps analyze denial patterns.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation was fully processed and refund completed.

This field marks the final completion of the cancellation workflow, including all refund processing and inventory adjustments. It indicates that no further action is required on this cancellation.

This field is null while the cancellation is in progress or if it was denied/expired without completion. It provides closure timing for operational metrics and customer service tracking.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation record was created.

This system-managed field records when the cancellation record was first inserted into the database. It is automatically set by the database on record creation and cannot be modified.

This field typically matches requested_at but is maintained separately for database integrity and audit purposes. It serves as the immutable creation timestamp for the entire record lifecycle.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation record was last modified.

This system-managed field records the most recent update to any field in the cancellation record. It is automatically updated by the database on any modification, including status changes, approval decisions, or refund amount updates.

This field helps track when the record last changed, supports cache invalidation strategies, and provides audit trail completeness for compliance purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this cancellation record.

This field implements soft-delete functionality, recording when the cancellation record was marked as deleted without physically removing it from the database. Soft deletion preserves historical data for audit trails and compliance while hiding records from normal queries.

This field is null for active (non-deleted) records. When set, the record is excluded from standard queries but remains accessible for historical reporting and audit purposes.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.description:
Complete order cancellation request entity with full workflow details.

This response DTO represents a complete order cancellation record including request details, approval workflow state, actor identities, and timeline information. It is returned after successful cancellation operations and when retrieving cancellation details for review.

The entity tracks the complete lifecycle of a cancellation request from initial submission through approval/denial to final completion. It supports multiple cancellation initiators (buyer, seller, admin) and multiple approval workflows (auto-approval, seller approval, admin approval) to accommodate various business scenarios.

Relationships: Links to shopping_mall_orders (parent order), shopping_mall_order_sellers (for partial cancellations), shopping_mall_buyers (requesting buyer), shopping_mall_sellers (requesting/approving seller), and shopping_mall_admins (requesting/approving admin). The approval_status affects order processing workflows and triggers refund transactions.

Audit trail: Maintains comprehensive timeline tracking with requested_at, approved_at, denied_at, and completed_at timestamps. Records actor identities for all participants in the workflow (requestors and approvers) to ensure full accountability.

Security: Actor identity fields are populated from JWT authentication context and are read-only in responses. The entity exposes only the information necessary for buyers to track their cancellation requests and for administrators to manage the approval workflow.

id.description:
Unique identifier of the refund request.

This UUID serves as the primary key for the refund request record and is automatically generated when a buyer submits a refund request for a delivered order.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order for which refund is requested.

This foreign key links the refund request to the specific order in the shopping_mall_orders table. Only delivered orders are eligible for refund requests according to business rules. The system validates order existence, delivery status, and buyer ownership before accepting refund request submissions.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order for which refund is requested, supporting partial refunds in multi-seller orders.

This optional foreign key references a specific seller's portion of a multi-seller order in the shopping_mall_order_sellers table. When present, it indicates that the buyer is requesting a refund for only this seller's items rather than the entire order. This supports scenarios where buyers want refunds for items from one seller while keeping items from other sellers.

When null, the refund request applies to the entire order across all sellers.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who submitted the refund request.

This foreign key identifies the authenticated buyer from the shopping_mall_buyers table who initiated the refund claim. The buyer must be the owner of the associated order to submit a refund request. The buyer's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token during refund request creation.

refund_request_number.description:
Unique refund request number for tracking and reference.

This system-generated unique identifier follows the format REF-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN where YYYYMMDD is the date and NNNNNN is a sequential number. It provides a human-readable reference for buyers, sellers, and admins to track and discuss specific refund requests.

The number is automatically generated upon refund request creation and remains immutable throughout the request lifecycle. It is used in communications, customer service interactions, and refund processing workflows.

refund_reason.description:
Reason category for the refund request.

This field captures the categorized reason for the refund using predefined reason codes. Valid values include: defective_product, not_as_described, wrong_item, damaged_in_shipping, never_arrived, buyer_changed_mind, other.

The reason category helps classify refund patterns for analytics, policy enforcement, fraud detection, and seller performance metrics. It is set by the buyer during refund request submission and influences admin approval decisions.

refund_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation provided by buyer describing the issue and reason for refund request.

This required field contains the buyer's free-text explanation elaborating on the refund_reason category. Buyers must provide clear and detailed justification including specific circumstances, product issues encountered, or other relevant details that support their refund claim.

This information is crucial for admin review, helps ensure legitimate refund claims, supports seller feedback, and aids in dispute resolution. The explanation is reviewed by admins as part of the approval decision process.

requested_amount.description:
Amount buyer is requesting to be refunded (may be full order amount or partial).

This field specifies the monetary amount the buyer is requesting as a refund. It must be a positive value and cannot exceed the original order total amount. The system validates this constraint before accepting the refund request.

The requested amount may be the full order total or a partial amount for scenarios such as refunding only some items, accounting for restocking fees, or requesting partial refunds for quality issues. The amount is specified in the platform's base currency with decimal precision.

status.description:
Current status of the refund request.

This field tracks the lifecycle of the refund request through various states: requested, under_review, information_requested, approved, processing, completed, denied, cancelled.

- requested: Initial state when buyer submits the request
- under_review: Admin is actively reviewing the claim
- information_requested: Admin needs additional information from buyer
- approved: Admin approved the refund, triggering payment processing
- processing: Refund payment is being processed
- completed: Refund payment completed and funds returned to buyer
- denied: Admin rejected the refund request
- cancelled: Buyer cancelled their own refund request

Status transitions are controlled by approval workflows with audit trails maintained through timestamp fields.

admin_decision.description:
Admin decision on the refund request.

This field records the administrator's decision regarding the refund claim. Valid values are: approve_full, approve_partial, deny, escalate, pending.

- approve_full: Approve refund for the full requested amount
- approve_partial: Approve refund for a partial amount (see approved_refund_amount)
- deny: Reject the refund request
- escalate: Escalate to senior admin or special review
- pending: No decision made yet

The decision influences subsequent workflow steps including refund transaction creation and buyer/seller notifications.

admin_decision_notes.description:
Admin notes explaining the decision rationale for transparency and record-keeping.

This optional field contains the administrator's detailed reasoning and justification for their refund decision. When approving refunds, admins may document special circumstances, policy considerations, or evidence reviewed. When denying refunds, clear explanation helps buyers understand the platform's decision.

The notes are recorded with the admin's identity and timestamp for complete audit trail compliance and accountability. This field is null when the refund request has not yet been reviewed or decided.

approved_refund_amount.description:
Actual refund amount approved by admin, which may differ from requested amount for partial refunds.

This optional field specifies the monetary amount actually approved for refund by the administrator. It may equal the requested_amount for full refunds, be less than requested_amount for partial refunds (such as when accounting for restocking fees or partial responsibility), or be null when the refund is denied.

For admin_decision values of 'approve_partial', this field contains the partial amount approved. For 'approve_full', this typically matches requested_amount. For 'deny', this field is null. The approved amount is used to create refund transaction records.

return_required.description:
Whether buyer must return the product to receive the refund.

This field indicates if the buyer is required to ship the product back to the seller as a condition of receiving the refund. Return requirements depend on the refund reason, product condition, seller policies, and platform rules.

When true, the buyer must provide return shipping information and the seller must confirm receipt before refund processing completes. When false, the refund can be processed without product return (such as for defective products the seller does not want returned).

return_tracking_number.description:
Tracking number provided by buyer when returning the product.

This optional field captures the shipping carrier tracking number for the product return shipment. Buyers provide this when shipping products back to sellers as part of the refund process. The tracking number enables sellers to monitor return shipments and confirm receipt.

This field is null when return is not required, the buyer has not yet shipped the return, or the refund is still in early stages. It must be provided when return_required is true before refund processing can complete.

return_received_at.description:
Timestamp when seller confirmed receipt of returned product.

This optional system-managed field records the exact date and time when the seller confirmed receiving the returned product from the buyer. Seller confirmation of return receipt is typically required before final refund payment processing when return_required is true.

This field is null when return is not required, the product has not yet been returned, or the seller has not confirmed receipt. It is set when the seller marks the return as received in the system.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the buyer submitted the refund request.

This system-managed field records the exact date and time when the buyer submitted the refund request. It serves as the official start of the refund review workflow and is used for audit trails, time-based business rules (such as refund request windows), and reporting.

The timestamp is automatically set by the database when the refund request record is created and cannot be modified.

reviewed_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was reviewed by an administrator.

This optional system-managed field records the exact date and time when the admin made their approval or rejection decision. It marks the point at which the refund request moved from pending review to decided status.

This field is null for pending requests that have not yet been reviewed. It is automatically set when the admin makes their decision and is used to calculate review processing times.

approved_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund was approved.

This optional system-managed field records the exact date and time when the refund request was approved by an administrator. It marks the point at which the refund enters the payment processing workflow.

This field is null when the refund is pending, denied, or under review. It is automatically set when the status transitions to approved.

denied_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was denied.

This optional system-managed field records the exact date and time when the refund request was denied by an administrator. It marks the final state of a rejected refund claim.

This field is null when the refund was approved or is still pending. It is automatically set when the admin_decision is set to 'deny'.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund processing was completed and funds returned to buyer.

This optional system-managed field records the exact date and time when all refund processing steps were completed, including payment processing and funds transfer to the buyer. It marks the final successful state of the refund workflow.

This field is null when the refund is pending, denied, or approved but payment processing is still in progress. It is automatically set when the status transitions to 'completed'.

reviewed_by_admin_id.description:
Reference to the administrator who reviewed and processed the refund request.

This optional foreign key identifies which administrator from the shopping_mall_admins table made the approval or rejection decision, supporting accountability and audit trail requirements. The admin's identity is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token when they process the refund request.

This field is null for pending requests that have not yet been reviewed.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request was initially submitted by the buyer.

This system-managed field records the exact date and time when the refund request record was created in the database. It is used for audit trails, reporting, and chronological ordering.

The timestamp is automatically set by the database on record insertion and remains immutable throughout the request lifecycle.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund request record was last modified.

This system-managed field records when any field in the refund request was last updated, including status changes, admin decisions, and other modifications. It helps track processing activity and maintain complete audit trail information.

The timestamp is automatically updated by the database on any record modification.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this refund request.

This optional field supports soft deletion patterns where refund request records are marked as deleted rather than physically removed from the database. When set, the record is considered deleted and excluded from normal queries while being retained for audit and historical purposes.

This field is null for active (non-deleted) refund requests. It is set to the deletion timestamp when a refund request record is soft-deleted.

order.description:
Summary information of the order associated with this refund request.

Provides essential order details including order number, total amount, and current status to give context for the refund claim. This relationship enables users to understand which order the refund applies to without requiring separate API calls.

buyer.description:
Summary information of the buyer who submitted the refund request.

Includes buyer identification details and contact information relevant to processing the refund claim. This relationship provides context about who is requesting the refund and supports customer service interactions.

reviewed_by_admin.description:
Summary information of the administrator who reviewed the refund request.

Provides admin identification details for accountability and audit purposes. This relationship shows who made the refund decision and supports administrative oversight. This is null for pending requests that have not yet been reviewed.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.description:
Complete refund request entity with full details including buyer information, order context, and administrative review status.

This response DTO represents a buyer's request to refund a delivered order, capturing the complete workflow from initial submission through administrative review to final approval or rejection. It includes buyer-provided information, order references, admin review details, status tracking, and return processing information.

The refund request system maintains a comprehensive audit trail with timestamps and admin identification for all review actions. Approved refunds trigger the creation of corresponding refund transaction records in the shopping_mall_refund_transactions table. The entity supports both full and partial refunds, return requirement tracking, and multi-seller order scenarios.

Relationships: Links to shopping_mall_orders (order being refunded), shopping_mall_order_sellers (seller sub-order for partial refunds), shopping_mall_buyers (buyer submitting request), and shopping_mall_admins (admin reviewer). The refund status affects order state and may trigger payment transaction creation.

The request enables complex queries such as finding all shipped segments from a specific seller, identifying segments by tracking number, or analyzing delivery performance. Pagination controls ensure efficient handling of large result sets.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing flexible query construction. When multiple filters are specified, they are combined with AND logic.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.IRequest.description:
Search and pagination parameters for retrieving order items within a specific order.

Provides comprehensive filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities for finding specific items in an order. Particularly useful for orders with many items where buyers or sellers need to locate specific products.

Supports free-text search across product names and SKU codes captured at purchase time, price range filtering, seller-specific filtering, and flexible sorting options. All filter fields align with the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma schema columns.

Pagination controls prevent performance issues with large orders. Used in order detail interfaces where users need to search or filter items, and in seller dashboards where sellers need to view only their assigned items in multi-seller orders.

IShoppingMallOrderItem.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order item for lightweight list views and embedded references.

Provides essential order line item information including product details, quantity, pricing, and fulfillment status. This DTO captures product information as it existed at the time of purchase, preserving historical accuracy even if product details change later.

Used in order summaries, order lists, and embedded contexts where full order item detail is not required. Aligns with the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma schema to ensure accurate representation of database entities.

This summary excludes detailed nested composition arrays to optimize for list performance and reduce payload size. For complete order item details including full product information, use the main IShoppingMallOrderItem type.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order item.

Primary key used to reference this specific line item within an order. Corresponds to the id field in the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma table.

Generated automatically upon order placement and remains immutable throughout the item's lifecycle.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent order containing this item.

Links this order item to its parent order record in the shopping_mall_orders table. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_order_id column in the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma schema.

This field establishes the relationship between individual line items and their containing order. Every order item must belong to exactly one order, making this a required non-nullable field.

Used for order aggregation queries, order detail displays, and ensuring referential integrity between orders and their component items.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the seller segment this item belongs to within the order.

Links this order item to the specific seller sub-order in multi-seller order scenarios. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_order_seller_id column in the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma schema.

In orders containing products from multiple sellers, items are grouped into seller segments for independent fulfillment tracking. This field identifies which seller is responsible for fulfilling this specific item.

Essential for seller dashboards, fulfillment workflows, and commission calculations where items must be attributed to the correct merchant.

shopping_mall_sale_sku_id.description:
Foreign key reference to the product SKU variant that was purchased.

Links this order item to the specific product variant in the shopping_mall_sale_skus table. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_sale_sku_id column in the shopping_mall_order_items Prisma schema.

This field provides the direct relationship to the exact product configuration (size, color, options) that the buyer ordered. Used for inventory tracking, product analytics, and linking order history to current product catalog.

While the DTO also includes a transformed 'sku' reference object for convenience, this raw foreign key is preserved for database operations and direct relationship queries.

product_name.description:
Product name captured at time of purchase for historical accuracy.

Stores the product title as it existed when the order was placed, preserving the exact name shown to the buyer during checkout. This field corresponds to the product_name column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Even if the seller later changes the product name in the catalog, this historical record remains unchanged. This ensures order history displays accurate information and prevents confusion in invoices and receipts.

sku_code.description:
SKU code captured at time of purchase for reference.

Records the Stock Keeping Unit identifier as it existed when the order was placed. Corresponds to the sku_code column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Provides a permanent reference to the specific product variant purchased, enabling accurate inventory tracking and product identification even if SKU codes are later modified or products are discontinued.

variant_attributes.description:
JSON string capturing selected variant attributes at time of purchase.

Stores a JSON-encoded representation of the product configuration selected by the buyer, such as {"Color": "Red", "Size": "Large"}. Corresponds to the variant_attributes column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Preserves the exact variant selection for historical accuracy in order records and customer service inquiries. May be null for products without variant attributes or simple single-variant products.

quantity.description:
Quantity of the product SKU ordered.

Must be a positive integer representing the number of units purchased. Corresponds to the quantity column in shopping_mall_order_items.

This quantity is validated against available inventory at the time of order placement and used to calculate the total line item cost.

unit_price.description:
Price per unit at the time of purchase.

Captures the per-unit price of the SKU at the moment the order was placed, preserving historical pricing. Corresponds to the unit_price column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD). Supports up to 2 decimal places for cents. This price remains fixed in the order record even if the product's current selling price changes.

line_total.description:
Total price for this line item calculated as unit_price × quantity.

Represents the total cost for all units of this SKU in the order before applying any line-level discounts. Corresponds to the line_total column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD). Supports up to 2 decimal places for cents. This is the subtotal for the line item, which may be further reduced by the discount_amount.

discount_amount.description:
Discount amount applied to this specific line item from promotions or coupons.

Records any price reduction applied exclusively to this order item, separate from order-level discounts. Corresponds to the discount_amount column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Expressed in the platform's base currency (USD). A value of 0 indicates no discount was applied. When non-zero, the final item cost is calculated as line_total - discount_amount.

sku.description:
Reference to the product SKU variant that was ordered.

Provides essential product variant information including name, attributes, and identifiers. Links this order item to the specific product configuration (size, color, options) that the buyer purchased.

Contains lightweight product information without full composition details. The shopping_mall_sale_sku_id foreign key in the Prisma schema establishes this relationship.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item was created.

Records when this line item was added to the order during the checkout process. Corresponds to the created_at column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information. Managed automatically by the system and immutable after creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this order item record was last modified.

Tracks the most recent update to any field in this order item record. Corresponds to the updated_at column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information. Automatically updated by the system whenever the record changes, supporting audit trails and change tracking.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this order item.

When set, indicates this order item has been logically deleted while preserving the historical record. Corresponds to the deleted_at column in shopping_mall_order_items.

Null for active order items. When populated, the item is excluded from standard queries but retained for order history, reporting, and compliance purposes.

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction (ascending or descending).

Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order of the sort_by field. 'desc' (newest first) is typical for status timelines, while 'asc' (oldest first) shows the complete progression from order creation. Defaults to 'desc'.

Controls whether results are sorted in ascending or descending order of the sort_by field. 'desc' (newest first) is typical for status timelines, while 'asc' (oldest first) shows the complete progression from order creation. Defaults to 'desc'.

order.description:
