IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of an order status transition record for audit trail displays.

Provides essential status change information for order tracking and history views.
Used in order detail pages to show the progression of order fulfillment.

Each record captures a single state transition with timestamp, actor information, and optional reason.
Ordered chronologically, these records form the complete order lifecycle audit trail.

Optimized for timeline displays and status tracking interfaces.
For complete status change details, use the main IShoppingMallOrderStatusHistory type.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the status history record.

Primary key used to reference this specific status transition.
Generated automatically when the status change occurs and remains immutable.

Corresponds to the 'id' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Identifier of the order whose status changed.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_orders table.
Links this status transition to the parent order entity for tracking the complete order lifecycle.

Every status history record must be associated with a specific order.
Corresponds to the 'shopping_mall_order_id' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Identifier of the seller sub-order whose status changed, for tracking seller-specific fulfillment progress.

Foreign key reference to the shopping_mall_order_sellers table.
Used in multi-seller orders to track status changes at the seller level rather than the entire order.

When null, the status change applies to the entire order rather than a specific seller's portion.
When set, enables granular tracking of individual seller fulfillment in marketplace orders.

Corresponds to the 'shopping_mall_order_seller_id' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

previous_status.description:
Order status before this transition occurred.

Captures the state the order was in immediately before this status change.
Useful for understanding the complete state machine progression and validating state transitions.

Can be null for the initial status record when an order is first created.
For all subsequent transitions, contains the prior status value.

Corresponds to the 'previous_status' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

new_status.description:
Order status after this transition occurred.

Represents the target state of this status change event.
Possible values include statuses like 'pending', 'confirmed', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', 'refunded'.

Forms part of the ordered sequence of status changes that define the order lifecycle.
This is the authoritative status value after the transition completes.

Corresponds to the 'new_status' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

actor_type.description:
Type of actor who triggered the status change.

Identifies the category of user or system component that initiated this state transition.
Possible values include: 'buyer', 'seller', 'admin', 'system'.

Used for audit trail analysis to understand who has permission to trigger specific status changes.
Enables accountability tracking and helps identify manual vs automated status transitions.

Corresponds to the 'actor_type' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

actor_id.description:
ID of the actor who triggered the status change.

Contains the specific identifier of the user or system component that initiated the transition.
For buyer-triggered changes, contains buyer_id; for seller-triggered, seller_id; for admin, admin_id.

Can be null for system-automated transitions or when actor tracking is not applicable.
Combined with actor_type, provides complete accountability for status changes.

Corresponds to the 'actor_id' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

change_reason.description:
Optional explanation or reason for the status change provided by the actor.

Provides additional context about why the status changed or relevant details about the transition.
May include information like tracking numbers when shipped, cancellation reasons, fulfillment notes, or admin override justifications.

Can be null if no additional context is needed for the status change.
Particularly valuable for manual transitions to document decision rationale.

Corresponds to the 'change_reason' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the actor when the status change occurred for security audit.

Captures the network origin of the status change request for security monitoring and fraud detection.
Used in audit trails to verify the legitimacy of status transitions and detect suspicious activity.

Can be null for system-automated transitions or when IP tracking is not applicable.
Stored in string format to support both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

Corresponds to the 'ip_address' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this status change occurred.

Records the exact moment the order transitioned to the new status.
Expressed in ISO 8601 date-time format with timezone information.

Used to order status changes chronologically and calculate time spent in each status.
Managed automatically by the system when status transitions occur and remains immutable.

Corresponds to the 'created_at' column in the shopping_mall_order_status_histories table.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering order cancellation requests.

This request DTO enables comprehensive querying of order cancellation records with support for multiple filter criteria including cancellation status, order identifiers, buyer information, date ranges, and approval workflow states. The parameters allow administrators and authorized sellers to efficiently search through cancellation requests to track workflow status, identify patterns, and manage the cancellation approval process.

Pagination and sorting capabilities enable efficient handling of large cancellation datasets. Users can configure page sizes, navigate through result pages, and sort cancellation requests by various fields to optimize their workflow management.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve from the filtered cancellation request set. Defaults to 1 if not specified. Combined with limit parameter to implement efficient pagination through large result sets.

limit.description:
Maximum number of cancellation requests to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination. Typical values range from 10 to 100. The system may enforce a maximum limit to prevent excessive resource usage. Defaults to a reasonable value (e.g., 20) if not specified.

sort_by.description:
Field name to sort cancellation requests by.

Specifies which field should be used for sorting the result set. Common values include 'created_at', 'approved_at', 'cancellation_reason', 'status'. The available sort fields depend on the cancellation entity's properties.

oneOf.description:
Sort order direction.

Determines whether results should be sorted in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. Defaults to 'desc' for timestamp fields to show most recent cancellations first.

Sort order direction.

Determines whether results should be sorted in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. Defaults to 'desc' for timestamp fields to show most recent cancellations first.

order.description:
Sort order direction.

Determines whether results should be sorted in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order based on the sort_by field. Defaults to 'desc' for timestamp fields to show most recent cancellations first.

status.description:
Filter cancellation requests by their current status.

Narrows results to cancellations in a specific workflow state such as 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'processed'. This enables tracking cancellations at different stages of the approval and refund workflow.

order_id.description:
Filter by specific order identifier.

Restricts results to cancellation requests associated with a particular order. Useful when investigating all cancellation attempts for a specific order or when navigating from an order detail view to its cancellation history.

buyer_id.description:
Filter by buyer identifier.

Narrows results to cancellation requests submitted by a specific buyer. Enables analysis of cancellation patterns for individual customers, which can be valuable for customer service investigations or fraud detection.

from_date.description:
Filter cancellations created on or after this date.

Defines the start of a date range filter for cancellation request creation timestamps. Combines with to_date to enable date range queries. Uses ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

to_date.description:
Filter cancellations created on or before this date.

Defines the end of a date range filter for cancellation request creation timestamps. Combines with from_date to enable date range queries. Uses ISO 8601 format with timezone information.

approval_status.description:
Filter by approval workflow status.

Narrows results to cancellations in specific approval states such as 'pending_approval', 'approved', 'rejected'. This is distinct from the overall cancellation status and specifically tracks the administrative approval workflow state.

search.description:
Free-text search query.

Enables searching across multiple cancellation fields such as cancellation reason, order reference, buyer name, or other text content. The specific fields searched depend on the implementation but typically include user-visible text fields relevant to cancellation identification and investigation.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.ISummary.description:
Lightweight summary view of order cancellation records for list displays and embedded references.

Provides essential cancellation information including the reason, approval status, refund amount, and requesting actor. Designed for efficient rendering in cancellation history lists, order detail pages, and dashboard widgets.

Includes summary references to the associated order and requesting actor (buyer, seller, or admin) to provide context without requiring additional API calls. Includes key workflow timestamps to track cancellation progression through the approval and refund process.

Used in paginated cancellation lists, order status timelines, and actor-specific cancellation views.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the order cancellation record.

This is the primary key used to reference this specific cancellation request across the system. Used in API endpoints for retrieving, updating, or tracking cancellation status.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order being cancelled.

References the parent order record in the shopping_mall_orders table. This foreign key establishes the relationship between the cancellation request and the order it affects.

Every cancellation request must be associated with a specific order. This field is non-nullable as defined in the Prisma schema.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order being cancelled for multi-seller order partial cancellations.

References the shopping_mall_order_sellers table when cancelling only a specific seller's portion of a multi-seller order. Null when cancelling the entire order rather than a specific seller segment.

Enables partial order cancellations where a buyer cancels items from one seller while keeping items from other sellers.

requested_by_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who requested the cancellation if buyer-initiated.

References the shopping_mall_buyers table when the cancellation was initiated by the buyer. Null when the cancellation was initiated by seller or admin.

Used to track buyer-initiated cancellations for pattern analysis and customer service workflows.

requested_by_seller_id.description:
Seller who requested the cancellation if seller-initiated.

References the shopping_mall_sellers table when the cancellation was initiated by the seller. Null when the cancellation was initiated by buyer or admin.

Common when sellers cannot fulfill orders due to inventory issues or pricing errors.

requested_by_admin_id.description:
Admin who requested the cancellation if admin-initiated.

References the shopping_mall_admins table when the cancellation was initiated by an administrator. Null when the cancellation was initiated by buyer or seller.

Tracks administrative interventions for fraud prevention, policy violations, or dispute resolution.

approved_by_seller_id.description:
Seller who approved the cancellation request if seller approval was required.

References the shopping_mall_sellers table when seller approval was granted. Null when cancellation did not require seller approval or is still pending.

Tracks seller responsiveness to cancellation requests and provides accountability in the approval workflow.

approved_by_admin_id.description:
Admin who approved the cancellation request if admin approval was required.

References the shopping_mall_admins table when administrative approval was granted. Null when cancellation did not require admin approval or is still pending.

Provides accountability for admin approval decisions and enables auditing of administrative interventions.

cancellation_reason.description:
Standardized reason code explaining why the cancellation was requested.

Valid values include: buyer_changed_mind, buyer_ordered_by_mistake, seller_out_of_stock, seller_cannot_deliver, seller_product_discontinued, seller_pricing_error, admin_fraud_detected, admin_policy_violation, payment_failed, other.

This categorization enables analytics on cancellation patterns and helps identify systematic issues with products or sellers.

cancellation_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation or notes about the cancellation reason provided by the requestor.

Free-text field allowing the requesting party (buyer, seller, or admin) to provide additional context beyond the standardized cancellation_reason code. May be null if no additional explanation was provided.

Used for customer service investigations, dispute resolution, and understanding specific circumstances around cancellation requests.

approval_status.description:
Current state of the cancellation request in the approval workflow.

Valid values: pending (awaiting review), auto_approved (automatically approved based on business rules), seller_approved (approved by seller), admin_approved (approved by administrator), denied (request rejected), expired (approval window closed).

Determines whether the cancellation can proceed and whether refund processing should begin.

refund_amount.description:
Monetary amount refunded to the buyer as a result of this cancellation.

Represents the actual refund value in the platform's base currency. May be null if cancellation is still pending approval or if the order was cancelled before payment processing.

Used for financial reconciliation and buyer refund tracking.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was initially submitted.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Used for calculating approval timeframes, expiration windows, and chronological sorting of cancellation requests.

Critical for determining eligibility based on order status and time-based business rules.

approved_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was approved.

Null if the cancellation is still pending approval or was denied. Records the exact moment when seller or admin approval was granted, enabling SLA tracking for approval processing times.

Used for workflow analytics and determining when refund processing should begin.

denied_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation request was denied.

Null if the cancellation was approved or is still pending. Records when a seller or admin rejected the cancellation request, preventing further processing.

Used for dispute tracking and understanding rejection patterns in cancellation workflows.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the cancellation was fully processed and refund completed.

Null if cancellation processing is still in progress or was denied. Marks the final step of the cancellation workflow when all refunds have been issued and order status updated.

Used for calculating total cancellation processing times and confirming completion for customer service.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation record was created in the database.

Recorded automatically upon initial cancellation request submission. Used for audit trails, chronological sorting, and analytics on cancellation request patterns over time.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this cancellation record was last modified.

Automatically updated whenever any field in the cancellation record changes, including status updates, approval actions, or refund amount changes. Used for tracking record freshness and change history.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for this cancellation record.

Null for active cancellation records. When set, indicates the record has been soft-deleted and should be hidden from standard queries while retained for historical audit purposes.

Enables data retention compliance while removing cancelled cancellation requests from active views.

order.description:
Summary information about the order being cancelled.

Provides essential order details including order number, buyer information, and order status. Enables cancellation list views to display relevant order context without requiring additional API calls.

orderSeller.description:
Seller sub-order portion being cancelled for multi-seller order partial cancellations.

Null when cancelling the entire order rather than a specific seller's portion. In multi-seller orders where items come from different sellers, this identifies which seller's portion is being cancelled.

Enables partial order cancellations where a buyer cancels items from one seller while keeping items from other sellers.

requestedByBuyer.description:
Buyer who initiated this cancellation request, if the cancellation was buyer-initiated.

Null when the cancellation was initiated by seller or admin rather than the buyer. Provides buyer context for customer service and dispute resolution workflows.

Used to identify buyers with high cancellation rates for pattern analysis and fraud detection.

requestedBySeller.description:
Seller who initiated this cancellation request, if the cancellation was seller-initiated.

Null when the cancellation was initiated by buyer or admin rather than the seller. Helps identify sellers with high cancellation rates for platform monitoring.

Common when sellers cannot fulfill orders due to inventory issues or pricing errors.

requestedByAdmin.description:
Admin who initiated this cancellation request, if the cancellation was admin-initiated.

Null when the cancellation was initiated by buyer or seller rather than admin. Tracks administrative interventions in order management for fraud prevention, policy violations, or dispute resolution.

Provides accountability for admin-initiated cancellations and enables auditing of administrative actions.

approvedBySeller.description:
Seller who approved the cancellation request if seller approval was required.

Null when cancellation did not require seller approval or is still pending. Certain cancellation scenarios require seller consent, particularly for buyer-initiated cancellations after order processing has begun.

Tracks seller responsiveness to cancellation requests and provides accountability in the approval workflow.

approvedByAdmin.description:
Admin who approved the cancellation request if admin approval was required.

Null when cancellation did not require admin approval or is still pending. High-value orders, disputed cancellations, or policy-sensitive cases may require administrative approval.

Provides accountability for admin approval decisions and enables auditing of administrative interventions.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Reference to the order being cancelled.

This field identifies which order the buyer is requesting to cancel, corresponding to the shopping_mall_orders.id primary key. The system validates that the order exists, is in a cancellable state (typically orders that haven't been shipped yet), and belongs to the authenticated buyer before creating the cancellation request.

This prevents buyers from submitting cancellation requests for orders that are no longer eligible for cancellation or that belong to other buyers. The order ownership verification is a critical security measure in the cancellation workflow.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order being cancelled for multi-seller order partial cancellations.

This optional field references shopping_mall_order_sellers.id and is used when the buyer wants to cancel only a specific seller's portion of a multi-seller order rather than the entire order. If null or omitted, the cancellation request applies to the entire order.

Partial cancellations are important in marketplaces where a single buyer order may contain items from multiple sellers. This allows granular cancellation control at the seller level.

cancellation_reason.description:
Reason code for the cancellation request.

This required field captures a standardized reason code explaining why the buyer wants to cancel. Valid values include: buyer_changed_mind, buyer_ordered_by_mistake, seller_out_of_stock, seller_cannot_deliver, seller_product_discontinued, seller_pricing_error, admin_fraud_detected, admin_policy_violation, payment_failed, other.

The reason code enables systematic analysis of cancellation patterns and helps administrators make informed approval decisions. It differs from cancellation_explanation which provides free-form details.

cancellation_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation or notes about the cancellation reason.

This optional field allows buyers to provide additional context beyond the standardized cancellation_reason code. For example, if cancellation_reason is 'buyer_changed_mind', the explanation might be 'Found the same product at a lower price on another website'.

Detailed explanations improve customer service quality and help administrators make more informed decisions on edge cases. While optional, providing clear explanations typically results in faster approval processing.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new order cancellation request.

This DTO captures the information required from buyers when they initiate an order cancellation. Buyers must specify which order (and optionally which seller sub-order) they want to cancel, provide a standardized cancellation_reason code, and optionally include a detailed cancellation_explanation.

The system automatically populates server-managed fields including requested_by_buyer_id (from JWT authentication token), requested_at timestamp (current time), approval_status (initially 'pending'), and audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at).

Security measures ensure that buyers can only create cancellation requests for their own orders. The buyer's identity is never accepted from the request body but is instead extracted from the authenticated session. The operation validates order ownership and cancellation eligibility before creating the request.

This DTO corresponds to the create operation on the shopping_mall_order_cancellations table and initiates the cancellation approval workflow that may require seller or administrative review depending on order status and platform policies.

approval_status.description:
Updated approval status of the cancellation request.

This field represents the decision on the buyer's cancellation request. Valid status values and their meanings:

- pending: Initial state awaiting review
- auto_approved: Automatically approved based on business rules (e.g., order not yet processed)
- seller_approved: Approved by the seller for their portion of the order
- admin_approved: Approved by platform administrator
- denied: Request was rejected and order continues normal fulfillment
- expired: Request expired without action (e.g., order already shipped)

When status is set to any approved variant, the system triggers refund processing and inventory restoration workflows. When set to 'denied', the order continues its normal fulfillment process and the buyer is notified. Status transitions are audited with timestamps (approved_at, denied_at, completed_at).

refund_amount.description:
Amount refunded to buyer as a result of this cancellation.

This optional field records the monetary amount refunded when the cancellation is approved. The refund amount may differ from the original order amount due to partial cancellations, restocking fees, or promotional adjustments.

The field is typically populated when approval_status transitions to an approved state and the refund transaction is processed. It provides transparency in the cancellation workflow and is used for financial reporting and reconciliation.

IShoppingMallOrderCancellation.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating an order cancellation request status.

This DTO is used by administrators or sellers to review and process cancellation requests submitted by buyers. All fields are optional to support partial updates. Administrators typically update the approval_status field and may include refund_amount when approving cancellations.

Security considerations: This DTO must never accept actor identity fields (approved_by_seller_id, approved_by_admin_id) or timestamp fields (approved_at, denied_at, updated_at) from the request body. These are populated from the authenticated user's JWT token and system timestamps respectively. The approver's identity is automatically injected by the backend from the authentication context.

Business rules: Status updates trigger different workflows - approved statuses initiate refund processing and inventory restoration, 'denied' continues normal order fulfillment, and 'expired' closes the request without action. Each status transition is audited with appropriate timestamps for complete accountability.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

This field determines which page of results to return in the paginated response. Combined with the limit parameter, it enables efficient navigation through large result sets. For example, page=2 with limit=20 returns results 21-40.

limit.description:
Maximum number of refund requests to return per page.

This field controls the page size in the paginated response. The system enforces a maximum limit of 100 to prevent excessive data retrieval and maintain performance. Default value is typically 20 if not specified.

Lower limits improve response times, while higher limits reduce the number of API calls needed to retrieve all results.

buyer_id.description:
Filter refund requests by the specific buyer who submitted them.

When provided, this filter restricts results to refund requests created by the specified buyer. This is useful for admins reviewing all refund requests from a particular customer, or for buyer-specific support inquiries.

The buyer_id must be a valid UUID referencing an existing buyer account in the shopping_mall_buyers table.

order_id.description:
Filter refund requests associated with a specific order.

When provided, this filter restricts results to refund requests related to the specified order. This is useful when reviewing the complete refund history for a particular order, especially for orders with multiple items or partial refunds.

The order_id must be a valid UUID referencing an existing order in the shopping_mall_orders table.

status.description:
Filter refund requests by their current approval and processing status.

This filter allows admins to focus on refund requests in a specific state throughout the entire refund lifecycle:
- 'requested': Newly submitted requests awaiting initial admin review
- 'under_review': Requests currently being evaluated by administrators
- 'information_requested': Requests where admin needs additional information from buyer
- 'approved': Requests that have been approved and are queued for refund processing
- 'processing': Approved requests currently being processed for payment
- 'completed': Requests fully processed with refund issued to buyer
- 'denied': Requests that have been rejected by administrators
- 'cancelled': Requests cancelled by buyer or system before completion

Filtering by status is essential for workflow management, allowing admins to queue pending requests, track processing stages, or review historical decisions.

min_amount.description:
Minimum refund amount filter (inclusive).

When provided, this filter restricts results to refund requests with requested amounts greater than or equal to this value. This is useful for prioritizing high-value refund requests or identifying refund patterns based on monetary thresholds.

The amount is in the platform's base currency (typically USD). Must be non-negative.

max_amount.description:
Maximum refund amount filter (inclusive).

When provided, this filter restricts results to refund requests with requested amounts less than or equal to this value. Combined with min_amount, this enables range-based filtering for refund request analysis and queue management.

The amount is in the platform's base currency (typically USD). Must be non-negative.

submitted_after.description:
Filter refund requests submitted after this timestamp (inclusive).

This date range filter restricts results to refund requests created on or after the specified date and time. Useful for reviewing recent refund requests or analyzing refund patterns within specific time periods.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. When combined with submitted_before, enables precise date range queries.

submitted_before.description:
Filter refund requests submitted before this timestamp (inclusive).

This date range filter restricts results to refund requests created on or before the specified date and time. Useful for historical analysis or closing out refund requests from specific periods.

Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. When combined with submitted_after, enables precise date range queries.

search.description:
Search term for partial text matching on refund reasons and admin decision notes.

This field enables full-text search across refund_reason and admin_decision_notes fields. Useful for finding refund requests related to specific issues, product problems, or administrative decisions. Search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching.

Examples: 'damaged product', 'shipping delay', 'wrong size', 'policy exception'.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort results by.

Determines which field is used for ordering the result set:
- 'created_at': Sort by submission timestamp (default)
- 'amount': Sort by requested refund amount
- 'status': Sort by approval status
- 'updated_at': Sort by last modification timestamp

Combined with sort_order to achieve desired result ordering.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for the results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending or descending order:
- 'asc': Ascending order (oldest first for dates, lowest first for amounts)
- 'desc': Descending order (newest first for dates, highest first for amounts)

Default is typically 'desc' for created_at to show newest refund requests first.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering refund requests.

This DTO provides comprehensive search, filtering, sorting, and pagination capabilities for administrative refund request management. All fields are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple list retrieval to complex multi-criteria searches.

Pagination: Use page and limit to navigate through result sets efficiently. Default pagination typically starts at page 1 with 20 results per page.

Filtering: Multiple filter criteria can be combined for precise result sets. Filters include buyer, order, status, amount ranges, and date ranges. All filters use AND logic when combined.

Search: The search field performs partial text matching across refund_reason and admin_decision_notes fields, enabling keyword-based discovery of refund requests.

Sorting: Results can be ordered by submission date, refund amount, status, or last update timestamp in ascending or descending order.

Security: This operation is restricted to admin actors only. No buyer_id authentication is required as admins can view all refund requests across the platform.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the refund request.

This UUID serves as the primary key in the shopping_mall_refund_requests table and uniquely identifies each refund request across the entire platform. It is automatically generated upon refund request creation and remains immutable throughout the request lifecycle.

This identifier is used for referencing the refund request in related entities such as refund transactions, audit logs, and administrative workflow systems.

refund_request_number.description:
Unique refund request number for tracking and reference. Format: REF-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN.

This human-readable tracking number is generated automatically when a refund request is created and follows a standardized format that includes the creation date and a sequential number. It serves as the primary identifier for customer service interactions and administrative tracking.

The format REF-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN ensures chronological sorting and provides immediate visual indication of when the refund request was submitted. This number appears on buyer communications, admin dashboards, and all refund-related documentation.

oneOf.description: Reason category for the refund request.
Reason category for the refund request.
Reason category for the refund request.
Reason category for the refund request.

Reason category for the refund request.

refund_reason.description:
Reason category for the refund request.

This categorizes the buyer's reason for requesting a refund into predefined categories that help with analytics, policy enforcement, and workflow routing. The categories cover the most common refund scenarios in e-commerce:

- defective_product: Product has manufacturing defects or quality issues
- not_as_described: Product differs from listing description or images
- wrong_item: Buyer received incorrect product or variant
- damaged_in_shipping: Product damaged during transit
- never_arrived: Order not received within expected timeframe
- buyer_changed_mind: Buyer no longer wants the product (subject to return policy)
- other: Reason not covered by standard categories (requires detailed explanation)

This categorization enables automated policy checks, routing to specialized review teams, and analytics on refund patterns across the platform.

requested_amount.description:
Amount buyer is requesting to be refunded (may be full order amount or partial).

This field captures the monetary amount the buyer is requesting as a refund, which may represent the full order value, partial refund for specific items, or adjusted amount based on the issue. The amount is in the platform's base currency (typically USD) and includes the original product price and applicable taxes, but may exclude shipping costs depending on the refund reason.

For partial refunds in multi-item orders, this amount reflects only the portion being disputed. The actual approved refund amount may differ and is tracked separately in the approved_refund_amount field after admin review.

oneOf.description: Current status of the refund request.
Current status of the refund request.
Current status of the refund request.
