status.description:
Current status of the refund request in its lifecycle workflow.

This field tracks the refund request through its complete processing pipeline from initial submission to final resolution. The status determines what actions are available to admins and what information is displayed to buyers:

- requested: Initial state when buyer submits the refund request
- under_review: Admin has begun evaluating the request and evidence
- information_requested: Admin needs additional details from buyer before decision
- approved: Admin has approved the refund and queued it for payment processing
- processing: Approved refund is being processed through payment systems
- completed: Refund successfully issued and funds returned to buyer
- denied: Admin has rejected the refund request with explanation
- cancelled: Request cancelled by buyer or system before completion

Each status transition is logged in the order_status_histories table for complete audit trail and compliance tracking.

requested_at.description:
Timestamp when the buyer submitted the refund request.

This immutable timestamp records the exact moment the buyer created this refund request, serving as the starting point for all refund processing timelines and SLA calculations. It is set automatically by the system upon request creation and never modified.

This timestamp is critical for:
- Determining refund eligibility based on time-since-delivery policies
- Calculating processing SLAs for admin review requirements
- Analytics on refund request patterns and timing
- Audit trails and compliance documentation
- Sorting and filtering refund queues by submission order

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order for which refund is requested. References shopping_mall_orders.id.

This foreign key establishes the relationship between the refund request and the original order that is being disputed. Every refund request must be associated with a valid completed order, as buyers can only request refunds for products they have received.

This relationship enables:
- Validation that the buyer actually purchased the items being refunded
- Access to complete order details including items, prices, and payment information
- Tracking of partial vs full order refunds
- Prevention of duplicate refund requests for the same order
- Integration with order management workflows and seller notifications

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order for which refund is requested, supporting partial refunds in multi-seller orders. References shopping_mall_order_sellers.id.

This foreign key identifies the specific seller portion of a multi-seller order that is subject to the refund request. In orders containing products from multiple sellers, buyers may request refunds for items from specific sellers while keeping others. This field enables seller-specific refund processing and ensures refunds are properly attributed to the correct merchant.

This relationship is essential for:
- Supporting partial refunds in orders with multiple sellers
- Routing refund notifications to the correct seller
- Tracking seller-specific refund rates and patterns
- Ensuring refund amounts are deducted from the correct seller's earnings
- Analytics on seller-level refund performance and product quality

When null, the refund applies to the entire order (single-seller scenario or full order refund).

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Buyer who submitted the refund request. References shopping_mall_buyers.id.

This foreign key identifies the authenticated buyer account that created this refund request. It is automatically populated from the buyer's authentication context when the request is submitted and cannot be modified.

This relationship is essential for:
- Verifying the buyer has authorization to request refunds for this order
- Displaying refund history and status in the buyer's account dashboard
- Preventing unauthorized refund requests from other users
- Analytics on buyer refund patterns and repeat refund requesters
- Customer service lookup and support case management

refund_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation provided by buyer describing the issue and reason for refund request.

This free-text field captures the buyer's detailed description of why they are requesting a refund, complementing the categorical refund_reason field. Buyers use this to explain product issues, describe discrepancies, provide context for their dissatisfaction, or detail shipping problems.

This explanation is critical for admin review as it provides:
- Specific details about product defects or quality issues
- Evidence of how the product differs from listing description
- Context that may not fit standard refund categories
- Buyer's expectations vs actual product received
- Additional information supporting the refund claim

Admins rely on this field along with any uploaded images to make informed decisions about refund approval, especially for subjective issues like 'not as described' or 'other' reason categories.

admin_decision.description:
Admin decision on the refund request indicating approval type or denial.

This field records the administrator's official decision after reviewing the refund request, evidence, and policy compliance. It determines the next steps in the refund workflow and impacts both the buyer experience and financial processing:

- approve_full: Admin approves refund for the full requested amount
- approve_partial: Admin approves refund for less than requested (amount in approved_refund_amount)
- deny: Admin rejects the refund request with explanation in admin_decision_notes
- escalate: Case requires higher-level review or special handling
- pending: Admin has not yet made a final decision (default state)
- null: No admin review has occurred yet (newly submitted requests)

Partial approvals are common when:
- Only some items in multi-item orders are eligible for refund
- Restocking fees or return shipping costs are deducted
- Product was used or packaging damaged, reducing refund amount
- Time-based depreciation policies apply to the refund value

approved_refund_amount.description:
Actual refund amount approved by admin, which may differ from requested amount for partial refunds.

This field stores the final approved refund amount after admin review and decision. It may differ from the requested_amount when admins approve partial refunds due to policy considerations, restocking fees, return shipping costs, or partial order disputes.

This amount represents:
- The exact monetary value that will be refunded to the buyer's payment method
- Admin's calculated refund after applying platform policies and fee deductions
- The basis for financial reconciliation and accounting entries
- The amount used for refund transaction processing

When admin_decision is 'approve_full', this typically equals requested_amount. When admin_decision is 'approve_partial', this contains the reduced amount with explanation provided in admin_decision_notes. This field remains null until admin makes an approval decision.

reviewed_at.description:
Timestamp when admin reviewed the refund request and made a decision.

This timestamp records the exact moment when an administrator completed their review of the refund request and recorded an official decision (approve_full, approve_partial, or deny). It marks the transition from pending status to a decided state.

This timestamp is essential for:
- SLA tracking on admin review turnaround times
- Performance metrics for administrative refund processing efficiency
- Audit trails showing when decisions were made and by whom
- Buyer communication about review completion timing
- Analytics on average review duration and backlog management

This field remains null for newly submitted requests that have not yet been reviewed. Once set, it indicates the request has moved past the initial review stage, though the final refund may still be processing.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ISummary.description:
Lightweight refund request summary for administrative list views and references.

Provides essential refund request information optimized for display in paginated admin dashboards and refund management interfaces. This summary includes all critical fields needed for admins to quickly assess refund requests, prioritize reviews, and make informed decisions without loading complete request details.

Includes key identifiers (id, refund_request_number), buyer and order context (shopping_mall_buyer_id, shopping_mall_order_id, shopping_mall_order_seller_id for multi-seller scenarios), request details (refund_reason, refund_explanation, requested_amount), current status throughout the workflow lifecycle, admin decision information (admin_decision, approved_refund_amount), and relevant timestamps (requested_at, reviewed_at).

This summary balances completeness with performance, providing enough context for effective refund queue management while minimizing data transfer overhead for list operations with potentially hundreds of refund requests. The inclusion of shopping_mall_order_seller_id enables proper handling of partial refunds in multi-seller order scenarios.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order for which refund is requested.

Must reference an existing order in the shopping_mall_orders table that belongs to the authenticated buyer and has a status of 'delivered'. The system validates that the order exists and is eligible for refund request submission before creating the refund request record.

This is a required foreign key relationship ensuring that every refund request is associated with a valid, delivered order.

shopping_mall_order_seller_id.description:
Seller sub-order for which refund is requested, supporting partial refunds in multi-seller orders.

When an order contains items from multiple sellers, buyers can request refunds for specific seller portions rather than the entire order. This optional field references the shopping_mall_order_sellers table to identify which seller's portion of the order is being refunded.

If null or omitted, the refund request applies to the entire order. If specified, the refund request is scoped to only the items fulfilled by that specific seller.

refund_reason.description:
Reason category for the refund request.

Buyers must select a categorical reason that best describes why they are requesting a refund. This field accepts predefined values that help administrators quickly understand and categorize refund claims for processing and analytics.

Valid values include:
- defective_product: Item has manufacturing defects or quality issues
- not_as_described: Product does not match listing description or images
- wrong_item: Buyer received incorrect product
- damaged_in_shipping: Item was damaged during delivery
- never_arrived: Order was marked delivered but buyer never received it
- buyer_changed_mind: Buyer no longer wants the product (may affect refund eligibility)
- other: Reason not covered by standard categories

This categorical field works in conjunction with refund_explanation to provide both structured classification and detailed context.

refund_explanation.description:
Detailed explanation provided by buyer describing the issue and reason for refund request.

Buyers must provide a comprehensive written explanation that elaborates on the categorical refund_reason they selected. This detailed text helps administrators understand the specific circumstances of the refund claim and make informed approval decisions.

The explanation should include relevant details such as:
- Specific product defects or quality issues observed
- Differences between expected and received items
- Timeline of when the issue was discovered
- Any communication with the seller about the problem
- Supporting evidence or documentation references

Minimum 10 characters ensures meaningful explanations. Maximum 2000 characters keeps descriptions focused and processable.

requested_amount.description:
Amount buyer is requesting to be refunded (may be full order amount or partial).

Specifies the monetary value the buyer wishes to receive back. This amount must be a positive value and cannot exceed the original order total amount. The system validates this constraint before accepting the refund request.

For full refunds, this typically matches the order's total_amount. For partial refunds (such as when only some items are being returned), buyers can specify a lower amount corresponding to the affected items.

Amount should be specified in the platform's base currency with decimal precision for cents (e.g., 29.99 for $29.99).

return_required.description:
Whether buyer must return the product to receive the refund.

Indicates if the buyer is required to physically return the purchased item(s) to the seller as a condition for refund approval. This field must be specified by the buyer during refund request creation.

Typical scenarios:
- true: Physical product returns (most common for tangible goods)
- false: Keep-the-item refunds (defective low-value items, digital goods, or goodwill refunds)

When true, the buyer will need to provide a return_tracking_number once they ship the item back. Admins typically wait for return confirmation before processing the refund payment.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new refund request for a delivered order.

This DTO captures the essential information a buyer must provide when submitting a refund request. The buyer must specify which order they want to refund (shopping_mall_order_id), optionally identify a specific seller portion for multi-seller orders (shopping_mall_order_seller_id), select a categorical reason (refund_reason), provide a detailed written explanation (refund_explanation), indicate the refund amount requested (requested_amount), and specify whether product return is required (return_required).

The buyer's identity (shopping_mall_buyer_id) is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and does not need to be included in the request body. This ensures that buyers can only create refund requests for their own orders and prevents authorization bypass vulnerabilities.

The refund request is initialized with a status of 'requested' upon creation and automatically captures the submission timestamp (requested_at, created_at). The request then enters the admin review queue where platform administrators will evaluate the claim and make an approval or rejection decision.

Business validation rules enforced during creation include: verifying the order exists, confirming the order belongs to the authenticated buyer, ensuring the order status is 'delivered', validating that the requested amount does not exceed the order total, and preventing duplicate refund requests for the same order. For multi-seller orders, if shopping_mall_order_seller_id is specified, the system validates that the seller portion exists and the requested amount does not exceed that seller's portion total.

Security considerations include authentication requirement to ensure only legitimate buyers can submit requests, automatic shopping_mall_buyer_id population from JWT to prevent impersonation, and authorization validation to prevent buyers from creating refund requests for orders they do not own.

oneOf.description:
Updated status indicating admin approval of the refund request.

When set to 'approved', the refund claim is accepted and the system initiates refund payment processing. This status transition triggers the creation of corresponding refund transaction records in the shopping_mall_refund_transactions table.

Approval indicates the admin has validated the buyer's claim and authorized the refund payment per platform policies.

Updated status indicating admin rejection of the refund request.

When set to 'denied', the refund claim is rejected and no refund payment will be processed. This status is the terminal state for unsuccessful refund requests per the Prisma schema valid status values.

Denial indicates the admin has reviewed the claim and determined it does not meet refund policy requirements or lacks sufficient justification.

status.description:
Updated status of the refund request.

Admins can change the status to either 'approved' to accept the buyer's refund claim or 'denied' to reject it. This status update triggers downstream processes such as refund transaction creation for approved requests.

The status transition must follow business rules where requests in 'requested' or 'under_review' status can be approved or denied by administrators. The valid status value for rejection is 'denied' as defined in the Prisma schema (not 'rejected'). Approved refunds trigger the creation of corresponding refund transaction records in the shopping_mall_refund_transactions table for payment processing.

oneOf.description:
Admin decision to approve the full requested refund amount.

Indicates the administrator has reviewed the refund claim and determined that the buyer is entitled to receive the complete amount they requested. The approved_refund_amount will match the original requested_amount.

Admin decision to approve a partial refund amount.

Indicates the administrator has determined that only a portion of the requested amount is justified. The approved_refund_amount field will contain the specific partial amount approved, which is less than the requested_amount.

Admin decision to reject the refund request entirely.

Indicates the administrator has reviewed the claim and determined it does not meet refund policy requirements or lacks sufficient justification. No refund will be processed.

Admin decision to escalate the request for higher-level review.

Indicates the refund claim requires senior admin review, special handling, or involves complex circumstances beyond standard processing. The request is forwarded to appropriate review channels.

Admin decision indicating the review is not yet complete.

Indicates the administrator is delaying final decision pending additional information from the buyer, seller consultation, or further investigation of the claim.

admin_decision.description:
Admin decision on the refund request.

Provides a granular decision classification with specific const enum values that capture the administrative determination made during the review process. Valid values are: approve_full, approve_partial, deny, escalate, pending.

- approve_full: Approve the full requested refund amount
- approve_partial: Approve a partial refund (less than requested amount)
- deny: Reject the refund request entirely
- escalate: Requires higher-level review or special handling
- pending: Decision delayed pending additional information

This field works in conjunction with the status field to provide complete decision context. When null, the status field alone indicates the decision state.

admin_decision_notes.description:
Admin notes explaining the decision rationale for transparency and record-keeping.

This field captures detailed administrative reasoning and any relevant details about the review decision. These notes provide transparency in the refund review process and serve as documentation for audit trails, potential disputes, and quality assurance.

Admins should provide clear, comprehensive explanations that:
- Justify their approval or denial decision
- Reference any policy guidelines applied
- Note any evidence reviewed (photos, seller responses, etc.)
- Document special circumstances or considerations
- Explain partial refund amount calculations if applicable

These notes are typically visible to the buyer to help them understand the decision, though sensitive internal reasoning may be recorded separately.

approved_refund_amount.description:
Actual refund amount approved by admin, which may differ from requested amount for partial refunds.

When admins approve a refund, they can specify the exact amount to be refunded. This field is particularly important for partial refund scenarios where the admin determines that only a portion of the requested amount is justified.

For example:
- Buyer requests $100 refund for a damaged item
- Admin determines 30% damage warrants $30 refund
- approved_refund_amount is set to 30.00

If null, the system typically uses the full requested_amount for approved refunds. For denied refunds, this field remains null.

This amount is used to create the actual refund transaction record in shopping_mall_refund_transactions when the refund is processed.

return_required.description:
Whether buyer must return the product to receive the refund.

Admins can update this field during review to change the return requirement based on their assessment. This allows flexibility in handling different refund scenarios.

Typical update scenarios:
- Set to false for low-value defective items (keep-the-item refund)
- Set to false for goodwill refunds where return is impractical
- Set to true when buyer initially indicated no return but admin requires it
- Maintain original value when buyer's initial specification is appropriate

When set to true, the buyer must provide a return_tracking_number before the refund is fully processed.

return_tracking_number.description:
Tracking number provided by buyer when returning the product.

This field is populated when the buyer ships the product back to the seller as part of the refund process. The tracking number allows both the seller and admin to verify that the return shipment is in progress and confirm delivery.

Admins may update this field if:
- Buyer provides tracking number through customer support channels
- Seller reports receiving a return shipment
- Tracking number needs correction

Typically, the refund payment is not released until the return is confirmed received (return_received_at is set), which is verified using this tracking number.

IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating refund request status and administrative review information.

This DTO is used exclusively by platform administrators to process buyer refund requests. It contains the admin's decision (approval or denial) along with optional fields that provide detailed decision context, refund amount adjustments, return requirements, and tracking information.

Only the status field is required as the minimum update operation. All other fields are optional and can be provided based on the specific refund scenario:
- admin_decision and admin_decision_notes provide detailed decision reasoning
- approved_refund_amount allows for partial refund approvals
- return_required can be adjusted based on admin assessment
- return_tracking_number can be recorded when buyer ships return

The update operation automatically captures additional metadata such as the reviewing admin's ID (reviewed_by_admin_id) and the timestamp of the review (reviewed_at, approved_at, or denied_at), which are not included in this request body but are populated server-side from the authentication context and system time.

Business rules enforce that approved refunds with approved_refund_amount specified will trigger the creation of corresponding refund transaction records in shopping_mall_refund_transactions for the specified amount.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-indexed).

Specifies which page of results to retrieve in the paginated response. Must be a positive integer starting from 1. This parameter works in conjunction with the limit parameter to control which subset of payment methods is returned.

For example, page=1 with limit=10 returns records 1-10, while page=2 with limit=10 returns records 11-20.

limit.description:
Number of payment methods to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a maximum limit of 100 records per page to ensure reasonable response sizes and system performance. This prevents excessive data transfer and maintains optimal API response times.

Buyers with many saved payment methods benefit from pagination to browse their payment options efficiently. Typical values range from 10-50 depending on UI requirements.

payment_type.description:
Filter payment methods by type.

Allows filtering the results to show only payment methods of a specific type such as credit cards, debit cards, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, or bank transfer. This field corresponds to the payment_type column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema.

If null or omitted, all payment method types are included in the results. This filter is useful when buyers want to view only a specific category of their saved payment methods, such as showing only credit cards during checkout or only digital wallets for contactless payments.

card_brand.description:
Filter by card brand or issuer.

Allows filtering payment methods by card brand (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover) or digital wallet provider. Corresponds to the card_brand column in the Prisma schema which stores brand information for card-type payment methods.

If null or omitted, all card brands are included. For non-card payment methods like digital wallets, this field may contain the wallet provider name or be null.

last_four_digits.description:
Filter by partial match of last four digits.

Allows buyers to search for payment methods by the last four digits of their card number or account identifier. This corresponds to the last_four_digits column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema.

Useful when buyers remember part of their card number and want to locate a specific payment method. Performs partial matching, so searching for '1234' will match any payment method whose last_four_digits contains that sequence.

If null or omitted, no filtering by card number digits is applied.

is_active.description:
Filter by active status of the payment method.

When true, returns only active payment methods that can be used for transactions. Active status is typically determined by checking if the payment method is verified and not expired. When false, returns only inactive or expired payment methods.

This filter helps buyers identify which of their saved payment methods are currently usable versus those that need updating or removal. If null or omitted, both active and inactive payment methods are included in the results.

Note: Active status may be computed based on is_verified flag and expiration date validation, not directly stored in the Prisma schema.

is_default.description:
Filter by default payment method status.

When true, returns only the payment method marked as the buyer's default for checkout. Corresponds to the is_default column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema. Only one payment method can be default per buyer.

When false, returns all non-default payment methods. If null or omitted, both default and non-default payment methods are included.

Useful for quickly identifying or retrieving the buyer's preferred payment method for streamlined checkout experiences.

is_verified.description:
Filter by verification status.

When true, returns only payment methods that have been verified through the payment provider and are ready for use in transactions. Corresponds to the is_verified column in the Prisma schema.

When false, returns only unverified payment methods that cannot yet be used for purchases. Unverified methods typically require additional validation steps before becoming usable.

If null or omitted, both verified and unverified payment methods are included. This filter helps buyers distinguish between ready-to-use and pending payment methods.

created_at_from.description:
Start of creation date range filter.

Filters payment methods created on or after this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. Corresponds to the created_at column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema.

Use in combination with created_at_to to define a specific date range. For example, buyers can search for payment methods added during a particular month or year.

If null or omitted, no lower bound is applied to the creation date filter.

created_at_to.description:
End of creation date range filter.

Filters payment methods created on or before this timestamp. Must be in ISO 8601 date-time format. Works with the created_at column from the Prisma schema.

Combine with created_at_from to filter payment methods added within a specific time window. This is useful for auditing or reviewing recently added payment methods.

If null or omitted, no upper bound is applied to the creation date filter.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort the results by.

Specifies which field should be used for ordering the payment methods in the response. Available options correspond to columns in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema.

Options include created_at for chronological ordering (newest/oldest), payment_type for grouping by payment method category, is_default to show default payment method first, or billing_name for alphabetical sorting by cardholder name.

If omitted, a default sort order (typically by created_at descending) is applied.

order.description:
Sort order direction.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Ascending shows oldest/earliest first for dates or A-Z for text fields. Descending shows newest/latest first for dates or Z-A for text fields.

For example, sort_by=created_at with order=desc shows most recently added payment methods first, which is typically the most useful view for buyers.

If omitted, descending order is typically used as the default.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving buyer payment methods with pagination support.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for buyers to search through their saved payment methods stored in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. It supports filtering by payment type, card brand, verification status, default status, and creation date ranges, along with flexible pagination and sorting options.

All filter parameters are optional, allowing buyers to retrieve all their payment methods or narrow down results based on specific criteria. The pagination parameters ensure efficient data retrieval for buyers with many saved payment methods, preventing performance issues with large result sets.

This DTO is designed to work with the PATCH /shoppingMall/buyer/paymentMethods operation, which requires buyer authentication to ensure users can only access their own payment method records.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this payment method.

Corresponds to the id column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema. This UUID is generated automatically when the payment method is created and serves as the immutable identifier for all payment method operations.

Used in API paths for retrieving, updating, or deleting specific payment methods, and as a foreign key reference in transaction records.

payment_type.description:
Type of payment method.

Indicates the category of this payment instrument. Valid values include credit_card, debit_card, paypal, apple_pay, google_pay, and bank_transfer. Corresponds to the payment_type column in the Prisma schema.

This field determines how the payment provider processes transactions and which additional fields (like card_brand for cards) are relevant. Digital wallets and bank transfers may have different validation and processing requirements compared to traditional cards.

provider.description:
Payment provider name.

Identifies which payment processor handles this payment method, such as Stripe, PayPal, Square, or Braintree. Corresponds to the provider column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema.

This information helps buyers understand which payment platform is processing their transactions and may affect features like refund processing times, customer support channels, and available payment method types. Different providers may have different fee structures and international availability.

The provider name is set when the payment method is initially tokenized and remains constant throughout the payment method's lifecycle.

last_four_digits.description:
Last four digits of card number or account identifier.

Displays only the final four digits for security and buyer recognition purposes. Corresponds to the last_four_digits column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema, which is nullable.

This field is null for some payment method types (like certain digital wallets) that don't have traditional account numbers. For cards, it helps buyers identify which card they're using without exposing the full number.

Never used for payment processing - only for display and buyer convenience in selecting payment methods.

card_brand.description:
Card brand or issuer network.

Indicates the card network such as Visa, Mastercard, American Express, or Discover for card-type payment methods. Corresponds to the card_brand column in the Prisma schema, which is nullable.

This field is null for non-card payment methods like digital wallets, bank transfers, or PayPal. The brand information is provided by the payment provider during card tokenization and helps buyers recognize their cards through brand logos in the UI.

Card brand may affect transaction fees, acceptance at certain merchants, and available features like contactless payments.

billing_name.description:
Name on the payment method.

The cardholder name or account holder name as provided by the payment provider. Corresponds to the billing_name column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema, which is required.

Used for verification purposes during payment processing and displayed to help buyers identify their payment methods. This name should match the name on file with the payment provider to ensure successful transactions.

For cards, this is typically the embossed name on the physical card. For digital wallets, it's the account holder's registered name.

billing_postal_code.description:
Billing postal code for address verification.

The postal code associated with the billing address for this payment method. Corresponds to the billing_postal_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema, which is nullable.

Used for fraud prevention and payment authorization through Address Verification Service (AVS) checks. Some payment providers require postal code verification to reduce fraudulent transactions and chargebacks.

This field may be null for payment methods that don't require postal code verification or when the payment provider doesn't return postal code information during tokenization. Displaying this information helps buyers verify which billing address is associated with each saved payment method.

expiry_month.description:
Card expiration month if payment type is card.

Numeric month value (1-12) indicating when the card expires. Corresponds to the expiry_month column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema, which is nullable.

Null for non-card payment methods that don't have expiration dates. Used to validate that cards haven't expired before allowing transactions and to warn buyers when their cards are approaching expiration.

Combined with expiry_year to determine the full expiration date. Cards typically expire at the end of the specified month.

expiry_year.description:
Card expiration year if payment type is card.

Four-digit year value indicating when the card expires. Corresponds to the expiry_year column in the Prisma schema, which is nullable.

Null for non-card payment methods. Together with expiry_month, this determines if a card is still valid for transactions. The system should prevent using expired cards and notify buyers to update their payment information.

Typically ranges from the current year to 5-10 years in the future, as most cards have 3-5 year validity periods.

is_default.description:
Whether this is the buyer's default payment method.

Indicates if this payment method is automatically selected during checkout. Corresponds to the is_default column in the Prisma schema. Only one payment method can be marked as default per buyer.

Default payment methods streamline the checkout experience by pre-selecting the buyer's preferred payment option. Buyers can change their default through account settings, which updates this flag and clears it from the previously default method.

The system enforces the single-default-per-buyer constraint through business logic or database unique indexes.

is_verified.description:
Whether the payment method has been verified and is ready for transactions.

Indicates verification status through the payment provider. Corresponds to the is_verified column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema. Unverified payment methods cannot be used for actual purchases.

Verification typically involves the payment provider confirming the payment method is valid, active, and authorized for use. This may include small charge verification, address verification, or other provider-specific validation steps.

Only verified payment methods appear as selectable options during checkout, protecting both buyers and the platform from invalid payment attempts.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method was added to the buyer's account.

Records when the buyer saved this payment method. Corresponds to the created_at column in the Prisma schema, which is automatically set by the database.

Useful for displaying payment methods in chronological order and for auditing purposes. Buyers may want to see their most recently added payment methods first, making this field important for default sorting.

Timestamp is in ISO 8601 format and includes both date and time information with timezone.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method information was last modified.

Records the most recent update to this payment method's data. Corresponds to the updated_at column in the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema, which is automatically updated by the database on each modification.

This field is important for security auditing and fraud detection, helping identify when payment method details were changed. It's also useful for showing buyers when they last updated their payment information, particularly for compliance with data accuracy requirements.

Timestamp is in ISO 8601 format with timezone information. Updated whenever any field in the payment method record changes, including verification status updates or default flag changes.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ISummary.description:
Lightweight payment method summary for list views and references.

Contains essential identification and status fields needed to display payment methods in dropdown selectors, checkout payment option lists, and account management interfaces. This DTO is derived from the shopping_mall_payment_methods Prisma schema but excludes sensitive provider tokens and detailed billing information for security and performance.

Used when showing available payment methods during checkout or in buyer account settings. Provides sufficient information for buyers to recognize and select their preferred payment method through the last four digits, card brand, billing name, and expiration information.

Security note: Full card numbers, CVV codes, and payment provider tokens are never included in this summary. Only display-safe, masked information is exposed to ensure PCI compliance and buyer data protection.

id.description:
Primary key uniquely identifying this payment method.

Generated as a UUID v4 value upon payment method creation.
Used to reference this specific payment method across all platform operations including order checkout and payment processing.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Foreign key to the buyer who owns this payment method.

References shopping_mall_buyers.id.
Establishes ownership relationship - each payment method belongs to exactly one buyer.
Buyers can have multiple payment methods for checkout flexibility.

buyer.description:
Summary information about the buyer who owns this payment method.

Provides essential buyer context including name and account status.
Useful for administrative views showing payment method ownership.

payment_type.description:
Type of payment method indicating the payment instrument category.

Valid values include: credit_card, debit_card, paypal, apple_pay, google_pay, bank_transfer.
Determines which payment processing flow and validation rules apply.
Influences available transaction features and processing fees.

provider.description:
Name of the payment service provider that processes transactions for this payment method.

Examples include: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree.
Identifies which provider's API and token system manages this payment method.
Required for routing payment requests to the correct processor.

provider_token.description:
Secure tokenized identifier from the payment provider representing the payment method.

Replaces sensitive card data with a provider-specific token reference.
Used to authorize and capture payments without storing actual card numbers or account credentials.
Tokens are unique per payment method and cannot be reverse-engineered to reveal original payment details.

last_four_digits.description:
Last four digits of the card number or account identifier for buyer recognition.

Displayed to buyers to help identify which payment method they're using.
Provides sufficient information for selection without revealing full account details.
Null for payment methods that don't have a meaningful digit-based identifier.

card_brand.description:
Brand of the payment card if the payment type is a card-based method.

Valid values include: visa, mastercard, amex, discover.
Null for non-card payment methods like PayPal or bank transfers.
Used to display appropriate card brand logos and apply brand-specific validation rules.

expiry_month.description:
Card expiration month (1-12) if the payment type is a card.

Used in combination with expiry_year to validate card is not expired before processing payments.
Platform can warn buyers proactively when cards are approaching expiration.
Null for non-card payment methods.

expiry_year.description:
Card expiration year (four-digit format) if the payment type is a card.

Stored as full year value (e.g., 2025) for unambiguous expiration validation.
Used in combination with expiry_month to prevent processing with expired cards.
Null for non-card payment methods.

billing_name.description:
Name associated with the payment method as provided by the payment provider.

Typically matches the cardholder name or account holder name.
Used for verification during payment authorization and for display purposes.
Required for all payment method types to ensure proper payment attribution.

billing_postal_code.description:
Postal code associated with the billing address for this payment method.

Used for address verification system (AVS) checks during payment authorization.
Helps prevent fraud by validating the buyer has legitimate access to the payment method.
Null if the payment provider or payment type doesn't require postal code verification.

is_default.description:
Indicates whether this payment method is the buyer's default for checkout.

Only one payment method per buyer can be marked as default.
Default payment method is automatically pre-selected during checkout for buyer convenience.
Buyers can change their default payment method at any time through account settings.

is_verified.description:
Indicates whether the payment method has been verified through the payment provider.

Verification confirms the payment method is valid and can be used for transactions.
Unverified payment methods cannot be used to complete purchases.
Verification typically occurs immediately after adding the payment method via provider validation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method was added to the buyer's account.

Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Provides audit trail for when buyers registered new payment methods.
Immutable after initial creation.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method information was last modified.

Updated automatically whenever payment method details change (e.g., setting as default, updating billing information).
Recorded in ISO 8601 format with timezone information.
Useful for tracking payment method maintenance and audit purposes.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the payment method was soft-deleted by the buyer.

Null for active payment methods that are currently available for use.
Soft deletion preserves audit trail and historical transaction references.
Deleted payment methods are hidden from buyer's active payment method list but remain in database for compliance and reconciliation.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.description:
Complete payment method entity representing a buyer's saved payment instrument.

Stores tokenized payment information including credit cards, debit cards, and digital wallets that buyers save for streamlined checkout.
Each payment method is securely tokenized through the payment provider, ensuring the platform never stores sensitive card details directly.

Buyers can save multiple payment methods and designate one as their default for convenient checkout.
Payment methods support soft deletion to maintain audit trails while allowing buyers to remove unused methods from their active list.

The system stores only payment provider tokens and last four digits for identification - never full card numbers or CVV codes.
All payment methods must be verified through the payment provider before being marked as usable for transactions.

payment_type.description:
Type of payment method being registered.

Specifies the category of payment instrument, such as 'credit_card', 'debit_card', 'digital_wallet', or other supported payment types. This field determines which validation rules and processing logic the system applies. Different payment types may require different sets of additional fields and follow different security protocols.

provider.description:
Payment provider or payment gateway name.

Identifies the third-party payment processor handling this payment method, such as 'Stripe', 'PayPal', 'Square', 'Braintree', or other integrated payment providers. The provider must be one of the supported payment gateways configured in the platform. This field determines which provider API will be used for payment processing.

provider_token.description:
Tokenized payment method identifier obtained from the payment provider.

This secure token must be obtained from the payment gateway (Stripe, PayPal, etc.) before submitting this registration request. The token represents the actual payment instrument and is used instead of transmitting raw payment details for PCI DSS compliance. Clients typically obtain this token through the payment provider's client-side SDK or tokenization API.

card_brand.description:
Brand of the credit or debit card.

Indicates the card network or issuer brand such as 'Visa', 'Mastercard', 'American Express', 'Discover', 'JCB', etc. This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The card brand is used for display purposes and applying brand-specific validation rules.

Null for non-card payment methods like PayPal or bank transfers.

last_four_digits.description:
Last four digits of the card number or account identifier.

For security purposes, only the last four digits of the card number should be provided. This allows buyers to identify their cards without exposing the full card number. The full card number should never be transmitted to the backend - instead, use the payment provider's tokenization mechanism.

Null for payment methods that don't have a meaningful digit-based identifier.

expiry_month.description:
Card expiration month (1-12) if the payment type is a card.

The month component of the card's expiration date, represented as an integer from 1 to 12 (1 = January, 12 = December). This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The system validates that the card has not expired based on this value and expiry_year.

Used in combination with expiry_year to validate card is not expired before processing payments. Platform can warn buyers proactively when cards are approaching expiration. Null for non-card payment methods.

expiry_year.description:
Card expiration year (four-digit format) if the payment type is a card.

The year component of the card's expiration date, represented as a four-digit integer (e.g., 2025, 2026). This field is required when payment_type is 'credit_card' or 'debit_card'. The system validates that the combination of expiry_month and expiry_year represents a future date.

Stored as full year value for unambiguous expiration validation. Used in combination with expiry_month to prevent processing with expired cards. Null for non-card payment methods.

billing_name.description:
Cardholder name or billing name for the payment method.

The full name of the person or entity to whom the payment method is issued, exactly as it appears on the card or in the payment account. This name is used for verification purposes during payment processing and should match the payment provider's records.

Typically matches the cardholder name or account holder name. Required for all payment method types to ensure proper payment attribution.

billing_postal_code.description:
Postal code of the billing address.

The ZIP or postal code associated with the billing address for this payment method. This field is used for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during payment processing to reduce fraud risk. The postal code should match the billing address on file with the card issuer or payment provider.

Helps prevent fraud by validating the buyer has legitimate access to the payment method. Null if the payment provider or payment type doesn't require postal code verification.

is_default.description:
Flag indicating whether this should be set as the buyer's default payment method.

When set to true, this payment method will become the buyer's default payment option, automatically pre-selected during checkout. If another payment method is currently set as default, it will automatically be updated to is_default false. Defaults to false if not specified, meaning the payment method is saved but not set as the default option.

Only one payment method per buyer can be marked as default. Buyers can change their default payment method at any time through account settings.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.ICreate.description:
Request body for registering a new payment method to a buyer's account.

This type defines the data structure required to create a new payment method record in the shopping_mall_payment_methods table. It contains the essential information needed to securely save a payment instrument for future use in checkout transactions.

The buyer's identity (shopping_mall_buyer_id) is automatically extracted from the JWT authentication token and must NOT be included in this request body. This ensures secure association of payment methods with the correct buyer account and prevents unauthorized creation of payment methods for other users.

Security considerations are paramount in payment method registration. The provider_token must be obtained from a supported payment provider (Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree) before submission - clients should never transmit raw payment card details directly to the backend. Instead, use the payment provider's client-side SDK or tokenization API to securely obtain the provider_token, which serves as a secure reference to the actual payment instrument stored by the provider.

For credit and debit cards, only the last_four_digits should be transmitted (never the full card number), along with the card_brand, expiry_month, and expiry_year. The full card number is handled exclusively by the payment provider's tokenization process. The billing_name and billing_postal_code are used for Address Verification Service (AVS) checks during payment processing.

The is_default flag allows buyers to immediately designate this payment method as their preferred default option. If set to true, any previously default payment method for this buyer will automatically be updated to is_default false, maintaining the business rule of exclusive default status.

The is_verified field is set automatically by the system after validating the payment method through the payment provider and is not included in the client request. All required validation, tokenization verification, and security checks are performed by the backend before the payment method is saved. The system ensures PCI DSS compliance through tokenization and never stores raw payment card numbers in the database.

IShoppingMallPaymentMethod.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying existing payment method details.

This schema represents the request body for updating payment method information in a buyer's account. It enables buyers to modify payment method details such as billing address information and default status preferences without needing to delete and re-add the payment method.

All fields are optional to support partial updates, allowing buyers to modify specific fields without affecting other payment method details. Immutable fields like provider_token, card_brand, and card_last_four_digits cannot be updated for security and compliance reasons - buyers must delete and re-add payment methods to change these values.

When is_default is set to true, the system automatically updates other payment methods to is_default false, ensuring only one default payment method exists per buyer account.

billing_name.description:
Name on the billing account or card.

This field represents the cardholder name or account holder name associated with the payment method. It may be updated if the buyer's name changes or if there was an error in the original entry.

The billing name is used for payment verification and must match the name on the payment method as registered with the payment provider.

billing_postal_code.description:
Postal code of the billing address.

This field represents the ZIP code or postal code associated with the payment method's billing address. It is often used for payment verification through Address Verification Service (AVS) checks.

Buyers may update this field if their billing address changes or to correct entry errors.

is_default.description:
Whether this payment method should be the default payment method for the buyer.

When set to true, this payment method becomes the default choice during checkout. The system automatically sets is_default to false for all other payment methods belonging to the buyer, ensuring only one default payment method exists per account.

This field allows buyers to change their preferred payment method without deleting and re-adding payment methods.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for payment transaction queries.

This schema defines the request parameters for searching and filtering payment transaction records with pagination support. It enables complex queries based on transaction status, payment method details, buyer information, order references, transaction dates, and payment amounts.

The schema supports comprehensive filtering for various use cases including buyer payment history review, seller revenue tracking, administrator financial auditing, and dispute resolution. All filter criteria are optional, allowing flexible query construction from simple to highly specific searches.

Pagination parameters enable efficient navigation through potentially large transaction datasets, while sorting options allow ordering by transaction date, amount, status, or other relevant fields in ascending or descending order.

page.description:
Page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

This field specifies which page of results to retrieve. Combined with limit, it enables efficient navigation through large transaction datasets without loading all records at once.

Default value is typically 1 if not specified.

limit.description:
Number of transaction records to return per page.

This field controls the page size for pagination. The maximum value is typically enforced to prevent performance issues from excessively large page sizes.

Default value is typically 20-50 records if not specified.

sort_by.description:
Field name to sort results by.

This field specifies which transaction attribute to use for sorting. Common sort fields include 'created_at' (transaction timestamp), 'amount' (payment amount), 'transaction_status' (status), and 'updated_at' (last modification time).

When combined with sort_order, this enables flexible result ordering to meet various display and analysis requirements.

oneOf.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

sort_order.description:
Sort direction for ordered results.

This field specifies whether to sort in ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc') order. Combined with sort_by, it controls the order of returned transaction records.

Descending order is commonly used for timestamp fields to show recent transactions first.

transaction_status.description:
Filter by payment transaction status.

This field filters transactions based on their processing status such as 'pending', 'completed', 'failed', 'refunded', or 'cancelled'. It enables searching for transactions in specific states for monitoring, reporting, or troubleshooting purposes.

Multiple statuses may be supported through comma-separated values or array format depending on implementation.

payment_method_provider.description:
Filter by payment provider type.

This field filters transactions based on the payment method provider such as 'credit_card', 'paypal', 'bank_transfer', etc. It is useful for analyzing transaction patterns by payment method or generating provider-specific reports.

buyer_id.description:
Filter by buyer who made the payment.

This field filters transactions to show only those belonging to a specific buyer. It is typically used by administrators for buyer-specific financial queries or dispute resolution.

For buyer-scoped operations, this filter may be automatically set to the authenticated buyer's ID from the JWT token.

order_id.description:
Filter by associated order identifier.

This field filters transactions to show only those related to a specific order. It is commonly used when displaying payment history for a particular order or investigating order-specific payment issues.

amount_min.description:
Minimum transaction amount filter (inclusive).

This field sets the lower bound for transaction amount filtering. When specified, only transactions with amounts greater than or equal to this value are returned.

Useful for finding high-value transactions or filtering out small payments in financial analysis.

amount_max.description:
Maximum transaction amount filter (inclusive).

This field sets the upper bound for transaction amount filtering. When specified, only transactions with amounts less than or equal to this value are returned.

Useful for finding transactions within specific amount ranges or identifying suspicious large payments.

created_at_start.description:
Filter transactions created on or after this timestamp.

This field sets the start of the transaction date range filter. When specified, only transactions created on or after this timestamp are returned.

Commonly used for generating financial reports for specific time periods or analyzing transaction trends over time.

created_at_end.description:
Filter transactions created on or before this timestamp.

This field sets the end of the transaction date range filter. When specified, only transactions created on or before this timestamp are returned.

Combined with created_at_start, this enables precise date range filtering for reporting and analysis purposes.

search.description:
General search term for transaction records.

This field enables full-text search across relevant transaction fields such as transaction ID, gateway reference numbers, or buyer information. It provides a user-friendly way to find specific transactions without knowing exact field values.

The implementation may search across multiple fields and support partial matching for improved discoverability.

Current transaction status tracking payment lifecycle.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ISummary.description:
Lightweight payment transaction summary for references.

Provides essential payment transaction information for use in other entities.
Used when refund transactions reference the original payment being refunded.

Includes key identifiers, amounts, and status without detailed provider responses.

payment_method_id.description:
Identifier of the payment method to use for this transaction.

References a saved payment method from the shopping_mall_payment_methods table that belongs to the authenticated buyer. The payment method must be active and valid when provided. This could be a saved credit card token, bank account reference, or digital wallet identifier.

This field is optional (nullable) to support scenarios where buyers enter payment details directly at checkout without using a saved payment method. When null, the buyer provides payment information inline during the transaction creation process, and the payment gateway tokenizes it directly.

When provided, the system validates that the specified payment method belongs to the authenticated buyer and is verified for use. Corresponds to the shopping_mall_payment_method_id column in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description: Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Authorization holds funds on the payment method without completing the transfer.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Capture completes the payment transfer after a successful authorization.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Void cancels a previous authorization before capture.
Type of transaction indicating the operation being performed. Refund returns captured funds to the buyer.

transaction_type.description:
Type of payment transaction indicating the operation being performed.

Valid values: authorization, capture, void, refund. Authorization holds funds on the payment method, capture completes the payment transfer. Void cancels an authorization, refund returns captured funds to the buyer. Determines the financial effect and reversibility of the transaction.

For order payments, the typical flow is authorization followed by capture. The authorization verifies funds availability and holds the amount, while capture finalizes the transfer when the order is ready to ship.

amount.description:
Transaction amount to process.

The payment amount for this transaction, which must match the order total to prevent payment manipulation. This amount includes all order costs: item subtotals, taxes, shipping fees, and any applicable discounts. The system validates this amount against the associated order's total before initiating payment processing.

currency.description:
Currency code for the payment amount.

ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY) for the transaction. This must match the order's currency and must be a currency supported by the platform and the selected payment gateway. The currency determines how the payment gateway processes the transaction and affects settlement procedures.

provider.description:
Payment service provider that will process this transaction.

Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree. Identifies which payment processor's API will be used to process this transaction. The platform routes the payment request to the specified provider's API endpoint.

The provider selection is typically determined by the payment method type and platform configuration. Different providers may support different payment methods, currencies, and geographic regions. Required for routing the transaction to the correct payment gateway.

oneOf.description: Initial transaction status indicating processing in progress.
Transaction status indicating funds are successfully held.
Transaction status indicating payment completed successfully.
Transaction status indicating the payment provider rejected the transaction.
Transaction status indicating an authorization was cancelled.
Transaction status indicating captured funds were returned.

status.description:
Initial status of this payment transaction.

Valid values: pending, authorized, captured, failed, voided, refunded. Pending indicates processing in progress, authorized means funds are held, captured means payment completed. Failed indicates the payment provider rejected the transaction.

For new transaction creation, the typical initial status is 'pending' while the payment gateway processes the request. The status will be updated based on the provider's response to authorization or capture attempts.

provider_transaction_id.description:
Unique transaction identifier assigned by the payment provider.

Optional field that can be populated if the transaction ID is known at creation time or provided by the payment gateway during initial request. Typically null for new transaction creation and populated by the backend after receiving the provider's response.

Used for reconciliation with provider transaction records and dispute resolution. Required for successful transactions to enable refunds and chargebacks. When provided during creation, it helps link client-side payment initiation with server-side transaction recording.

Corresponds to the provider_transaction_id column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

provider_response.description:
Raw JSON response from the payment provider for this transaction.

Optional field that can store the complete provider response if available during transaction creation. Typically null for new transactions and populated by the backend after payment gateway communication.

Stored for debugging, reconciliation, and regulatory compliance purposes. Contains provider-specific transaction details including authorization codes, risk scores, and additional metadata. Useful for investigating payment failures and resolving customer disputes.

Corresponds to the provider_response column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

failure_reason.description:
Human-readable reason for transaction failure if status is failed.

Optional field typically null for new transaction creation and populated if the initial payment attempt fails. Examples include: insufficient_funds, card_declined, invalid_card, fraud_detected, network_error.

Helps customer support and buyers understand why payment didn't process. May be displayed to buyers or used for automated retry logic. The backend populates this based on the payment provider's error response.

Corresponds to the failure_reason column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

failure_code.description:
Provider-specific error code for failed transactions.

Optional machine-readable code enabling detailed error analysis and conditional retry logic. Typically null for new transaction creation and populated if the payment provider returns an error code.

Used by payment processing system to determine if transaction should be retried automatically. Different providers use different error code formats and meanings. The backend maps provider error codes to this field for consistent error handling.

Corresponds to the failure_code column in the shopping_mall_payment_transactions Prisma schema.

ip_address.description:
IP address from which the payment is being initiated.

Captured for fraud detection, security auditing, and geographic analysis. Used to identify suspicious payment patterns and potential account compromise. Helps payment providers assess transaction risk and apply appropriate fraud prevention measures.

This field is optional but highly recommended for security. If not provided by the client, the server may capture it from the request headers. Including accurate IP address information improves fraud detection accuracy and may reduce payment decline rates.

user_agent.description:
Browser user agent string for the payment request.

Captured for fraud analysis and device fingerprinting. Helps identify automated attacks and unusual device patterns. Payment providers use this information as part of their risk assessment algorithms.

This field is optional but recommended for fraud prevention. The user agent string provides information about the buyer's browser and operating system, which can help detect suspicious activity patterns such as automated bot attacks or device spoofing attempts.

IShoppingMallPaymentTransaction.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new payment transaction.

This DTO captures the essential information needed to initiate a payment transaction for an order during the checkout process. The buyer selects a saved payment method or enters payment details directly, and confirms the payment amount, which the system validates against the order total before creating the transaction record and submitting to the payment gateway.

The order context is provided through the URL path parameter (orderId) rather than in the request body, ensuring that payment transactions are always created within the context of a specific order. The authenticated buyer identity is derived from the JWT token, ensuring that buyers can only create payment transactions for their own orders.

Security validation includes verifying that the payment method belongs to the authenticated buyer (when provided), the amount matches the order total, and the currency is consistent throughout the order and payment flow. These validations prevent payment manipulation and ensure transaction integrity.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the refund transaction record.

shopping_mall_refund_request_id.description:
Refund request that authorized this refund transaction.

References the shopping_mall_refund_requests.id foreign key in the Prisma schema. This establishes the authorization trail from buyer refund request through admin approval to financial execution.

Every refund transaction must have a corresponding approved refund request that initiated the refund workflow. This relationship ensures proper authorization and audit trail for all refund payments processed through the system.

refundRequest.description:
Refund request that authorized this refund transaction.

References the original buyer refund request that underwent admin review and approval.
This link establishes the authorization trail from buyer request through admin decision to financial execution.
Every refund transaction must have a corresponding approved refund request.

shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id.description:
Original payment transaction being refunded.

References the shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id foreign key in the Prisma schema. This identifies the initial payment that is being reversed through this refund transaction.

Refunds can only be processed against completed payment transactions. This relationship ensures refund amounts never exceed original payment amounts and maintains proper financial reconciliation between payments and refunds.

originalPayment.description:
Original payment transaction being refunded.

References the initial payment that is being reversed through this refund.
Refunds can only be processed against completed payment transactions.
This relationship ensures refund amounts never exceed original payment amounts.

shopping_mall_order_id.description:
Order associated with this refund.

References the shopping_mall_orders.id foreign key in the Prisma schema. This provides context for which purchase is being refunded.

Refunds are always tied to specific orders even when processing partial refunds. This relationship supports order-level financial reconciliation, reporting, and enables tracking of all refund activity for a given order.

order.description:
Order associated with this refund.

Provides context for which purchase is being refunded.
Refunds are always tied to specific orders even when processing partial refunds.
This relationship supports order-level financial reconciliation and reporting.

shopping_mall_buyer_id.description:
Buyer receiving the refund.

References the shopping_mall_buyers.id foreign key in the Prisma schema. This identifies the customer account that will receive the refunded funds.

Must match the buyer who made the original purchase. Used for buyer communication, financial account reconciliation, and ensuring refunds are properly credited to the correct customer account.

buyer.description:
Buyer receiving the refund.

Identifies the customer account that will receive the refunded funds.
Must match the buyer who made the original purchase.
Used for buyer communication and financial account reconciliation.

refund_amount.description:
Amount being refunded to the buyer.

May be partial or full order amount depending on refund approval decision.
Amount cannot exceed the original payment transaction amount.
Stored as precise decimal value for accurate financial calculations.

currency.description:
Currency code for the refund amount.

Three-letter ISO 4217 code matching original payment currency.
Refunds must be processed in the same currency as the original payment.
Examples: USD, EUR, GBP, JPY.

oneOf.description:
Refund processing status.

Tracks refund lifecycle through payment provider from initiation to completion.
Processing indicates refund has been submitted to payment provider but not yet finalized.
Completed means funds have been successfully returned to buyer's account.
Failed indicates refund could not be processed and may require manual intervention.

Refund processing status.

Tracks refund lifecycle through payment provider from initiation to completion.
Processing indicates refund has been submitted to payment provider but not yet finalized.
Completed means funds have been successfully returned to buyer's account.
Failed indicates refund could not be processed and may require manual intervention.

Refund processing status.

Tracks refund lifecycle through payment provider from initiation to completion.
Processing indicates refund has been submitted to payment provider but not yet finalized.
Completed means funds have been successfully returned to buyer's account.
Failed indicates refund could not be processed and may require manual intervention.

status.description:
Refund processing status.

Tracks refund lifecycle through payment provider from initiation to completion.
Processing indicates refund has been submitted to payment provider but not yet finalized.
Completed means funds have been successfully returned to buyer's account.
Failed indicates refund could not be processed and may require manual intervention.

provider.description:
Payment provider processing the refund.

Must match the original payment provider to ensure proper fund routing.
Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Braintree.
Provider determines refund processing time and capabilities.

provider_refund_id.description:
Unique refund transaction identifier from payment provider.

Used for reconciliation and tracking refund status with the payment provider.
Provides the external reference needed to query provider APIs for refund status.
Null if refund has not yet been submitted to provider or provider does not assign IDs.

provider_response.description:
Raw JSON response from payment provider for refund processing.

Stored for debugging and audit purposes to maintain complete provider communication history.
Contains provider-specific details about refund processing including internal status codes.
Null if provider has not yet responded or communication failed.

failure_reason.description:
Reason for refund failure if status is failed.

Examples: insufficient_balance, account_closed, provider_error, card_expired.
Null for successful refunds or refunds still in processing state.
Provides actionable information for resolving failed refunds.

initiated_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund transaction was initiated with the payment provider.

Marks the moment refund processing began through the payment provider's API.
Used to calculate refund processing time and identify delayed refunds.
Immutable timestamp set once when refund submission occurs.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp when the refund was successfully completed and funds returned to buyer.

Null if refund is still processing or failed.
Marks the moment funds became available in buyer's account.
Used for buyer communication and financial reconciliation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this refund transaction record was created.

Immutable audit timestamp marking when refund record entered the system.
May differ from initiated_at if record is created before provider submission.
Used for audit trails and system performance monitoring.

IShoppingMallRefundTransaction.description:
Refund payment processing records for approved refund requests.

Records actual refund payment processing that occurs after refund requests are approved by admins or sellers.
This entity is distinct from refund requests which track buyer refund requests and approval workflow.

Each refund transaction represents a financial operation returning funds to the buyer through the payment provider.
Refund transactions reference both the original payment transaction being refunded and the refund request that authorized the refund.

Refunds can be full (entire order amount) or partial (percentage or specific amount based on refund reason).
The system tracks refund status through the payment provider lifecycle from initiation through completion or failure.

Refund transactions are immutable audit records that cannot be modified after creation.
All refund processing details including provider responses and timestamps are permanently logged for financial reconciliation and compliance.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the refund transaction record.
