IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.ISummar.description:
Summary representation of a review moderation action for list views and audit trails.

Provides lightweight information about administrative and automated actions taken on product reviews from the shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs table. Used in moderation history displays, audit logs, and administrative dashboards where complete action details are not required.

This summary variant focuses on essential moderation metadata including action type, status transitions, moderator identity, timestamps, and automated system flags, while excluding detailed justifications and internal notes to optimize performance in list contexts.

Maintains accountability and traceability through moderator references and complete status transition information, enabling administrators to track moderation patterns and identify records requiring detailed investigation.

page.description:
Page number for pagination, starting from 1.

Specifies which page of moderation log results to retrieve when working with large audit trails.

limit.description:
Number of moderation log entries to return per page.

Controls the page size for pagination, with a maximum limit of 100 entries to ensure reasonable response sizes and performance.

shopping_mall_admin_id.description:
Filter moderation logs by the administrator who performed the action.

When specified, returns only moderation actions performed by the specific administrator. Useful for reviewing an individual moderator's activity, performance evaluation, or investigating specific administrative decisions. Null or omitted returns logs from all moderators.

action_type.description:
Filter moderation logs by the type of action performed.

When specified, returns only logs matching the specified action type. Enables focused analysis of specific moderation activities. The valid action types are:
- auto_approved: Review automatically approved by system
- auto_flagged: Review automatically flagged by content filters
- manual_approved: Review manually approved by administrator
- manual_rejected: Review manually rejected by administrator
- edited_by_admin: Review content edited by administrator
- deleted_by_admin: Review deleted by administrator
- deleted_by_buyer: Review deleted by the buyer who created it
- restored: Previously deleted or rejected review restored to visibility

Null or omitted returns logs for all action types.

previous_status.description:
Filter moderation logs by the review status before the moderation action was applied.

When specified, returns only logs where the review had the specified status prior to the moderation action (pending_moderation, approved, rejected). Useful for analyzing status transitions, such as finding all reviews that were approved but later rejected, or tracking reviews that moved from pending to approved. Null or omitted returns logs for all previous statuses.

new_status.description:
Filter moderation logs by the resulting review status after the action.

When specified, returns only logs where the moderation action resulted in the specified status (pending_moderation, approved, rejected). Useful for analyzing outcomes of moderation decisions and status transitions. Null or omitted returns logs for all resulting statuses.

moderation_reason.description:
Filter moderation logs by searching within the moderation reasoning text.

When specified, performs a partial text match against the moderation_reason field to find logs containing specific justifications, policy violation details, or administrative notes. Useful for investigating patterns in specific types of rejections, tracking enforcement of particular policies, or searching for logs related to specific compliance issues.

Supports partial matching to enable flexible searches across the reasoning text (maximum 1000 characters as per Prisma schema). For example, searching for "profanity" would find all logs where profanity was cited as a reason. Null or omitted returns logs regardless of moderation reasoning content.

from.description:
Filter moderation logs to include only actions performed on or after this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the start of the time window. Useful for analyzing moderation activity within specific periods or investigating recent moderation decisions. Null or omitted includes logs from the beginning of time.

to.description:
Filter moderation logs to include only actions performed on or before this timestamp.

Enables date range filtering by specifying the end of the time window. Used in combination with 'from' parameter to define precise time ranges for moderation activity analysis. Null or omitted includes logs up to the current time.

sort_by.description:
Field to sort the moderation log results by.

Specifies the ordering criterion for the returned logs:
- created_at: Sort by timestamp of the moderation action (default)
- action_type: Sort alphabetically by action type

Null or omitted defaults to sorting by created_at in descending order (most recent first).

order.description:
Sort order direction for the results.

Specifies whether to sort in ascending (asc) or descending (desc) order based on the sort_by field. Null or omitted defaults to descending order to show most recent moderation actions first.

IShoppingMallReviewModerationLog.IReques.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering review moderation logs.

Provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for retrieving moderation audit trails with support for pagination, moderator filtering, action type filtering, previous and new status filtering, moderation reason text search, date range filtering, and flexible sorting options. All filter parameters are optional, enabling both broad searches across all moderation activity and highly targeted queries for specific investigations.

This request structure enables administrators to efficiently analyze moderation patterns, investigate specific incidents, audit individual moderator performance, track policy compliance, search for specific policy violations or rejection reasons, track status transitions, and generate reports on moderation activities within defined time periods or matching specific criteria.

scenario.draft: Test successful buyer account registration with complete valid information. This scenario validates that a new buyer can create an account by providing all required registration fields including email, password, full name, optional phone number, and session context (href, referrer). The test should verify that the system creates a new buyer record in the shopping_mall_buyers table, generates a session record in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions, issues both access and refresh tokens following JWT standards, and returns complete buyer profile information with email_verified set to false initially. Validate that the password is securely hashed before storage, email uniqueness is enforced, and the response includes all required fields such as buyer ID (UUID), email, full_name, phone_number, email_verified status, timestamps (created_at, updated_at), and authorization tokens (access token, refresh token, expired_at, refreshable_until). Confirm that deleted_at is null for newly created active accounts.

Test buyer registration when phone_number is not provided (null). This scenario verifies that the registration process succeeds even when the optional phone_number field is omitted or explicitly set to null, since the shopping_mall_buyers table allows nullable phone numbers. The test should confirm that all other required fields (email, password, full_name, href, referrer) are sufficient for successful account creation, and that the returned buyer profile correctly shows phone_number as null. Validate that the account is fully functional and authentication tokens are properly issued despite the missing phone number.

Test buyer registration with an email address that already exists in the system. This scenario validates the email uniqueness constraint enforcement at the database level. First, create a buyer account with a specific email address successfully. Then attempt to register another buyer account using the exact same email address. The test should verify that the system rejects the duplicate registration attempt, enforces the unique constraint on the email column in shopping_mall_buyers table, and returns an appropriate error response indicating that the email is already registered. Confirm that no duplicate buyer records are created and no authentication tokens are issued for the failed registration attempt.

Test buyer registration with password that meets the minimum length requirement of 8 characters. This scenario validates password strength enforcement during account creation. The test should verify that passwords with exactly 8 characters are accepted as valid, while passwords shorter than 8 characters are rejected. Validate that the system enforces the minLength constraint defined in the IShoppingMallBuyer.ICreate schema, and that valid passwords meeting the minimum length are successfully hashed and stored. Confirm that successful registration with a minimum-length password still issues proper authentication tokens and creates a fully functional buyer account.

Test that buyer registration properly captures and stores session context information including IP address, href (current page URL), and referrer URL. This scenario validates that the session metadata is correctly recorded in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table for audit trail and analytics purposes. The test should verify that when IP is provided, it is stored in the session record; when IP is null, the server extracts it from HTTP headers. Confirm that href and referrer URLs are mandatory fields and are properly validated as valid URIs. Validate that the session context enables security monitoring, fraud detection, and user journey analysis. The test should also verify that referrer can be an empty string for direct access scenarios while still being a required field.

Test successful buyer authentication with valid credentials. This scenario validates the complete login workflow for an existing buyer account. First, create a buyer account through registration with known email and password credentials. Then attempt to login using those exact credentials along with session context (href, referrer). The test should verify that the system validates the email and password against the shopping_mall_buyers table, creates a new session record in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions, issues fresh JWT access and refresh tokens, and returns complete buyer profile information. Validate that the response includes buyer ID, email, full_name, phone_number, email_verified status, timestamps, and authorization tokens with proper expiration times. Confirm that the authentication succeeds for active accounts (deleted_at is null) and that password verification occurs through secure one-way hashing comparison without exposing the plain text password.

scenario.draft: Test buyer login attempt with correct email but incorrect password. This scenario validates password verification and authentication failure handling. First, create a buyer account with a known email and password. Then attempt to login using the correct email but with an intentionally wrong password. The test should verify that the system rejects the authentication attempt, does not issue any tokens, and returns an appropriate error response indicating authentication failure. Confirm that failed login attempts do not create session records in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions and that the password comparison is performed securely through hashing without revealing information about the password or account status.

dependencies.purpose: Create a buyer account with known credentials to test password verification failure

scenario.draft: Test buyer login attempt with an email address that does not exist in the shopping_mall_buyers table. This scenario validates the system's handling of authentication attempts for non-registered accounts. Attempt to login using a well-formed email address (valid format per RFC 5322) that has never been registered in the system, along with any password. The test should verify that the system rejects the login attempt, does not reveal whether the email exists or not (to prevent account enumeration attacks), returns an appropriate authentication failure response, and does not create any session records or issue any tokens.

Test that buyer login properly captures and stores session context information including IP address, href (current page URL), and referrer URL in the shopping_mall_buyer_sessions table. This scenario validates session metadata tracking for security monitoring and user journey analysis. First, create a buyer account. Then login with that account while providing complete session context including optional IP address, mandatory href (the login page URL), and mandatory referrer (previous page URL or empty string for direct access). The test should verify that the session record in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions contains the captured context, that IP can be extracted from HTTP headers when not explicitly provided, that href and referrer are validated as proper URIs, and that this metadata enables audit trail tracking, fraud detection, and conversion funnel analysis.

scenario.draft: Test buyer login with email address using different casing than registration. This scenario validates that the system performs case-insensitive email matching during authentication. First, create a buyer account with an email address in lowercase (e.g., buyer@example.com). Then attempt to login using the same email but with different casing variations (e.g., Buyer@Example.COM, BUYER@EXAMPLE.COM). The test should verify that authentication succeeds regardless of the email casing used during login, that the system normalizes email addresses for case-insensitive comparison, and that proper tokens are issued for all case variations. Confirm that the returned buyer profile shows the email in its original registered form.

scenario.draft: Test that a buyer can login multiple times from different locations or devices, creating multiple concurrent sessions. The test should verify that each login attempt succeeds independently, creates separate session records in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions with different session IDs, issues distinct sets of access and refresh tokens for each session, and allows all sessions to remain active concurrently. Confirm that each session has its own expiration tracking and can be managed independently.

scenario.draft:
Test that authenticated buyers can search and retrieve a paginated list of refund transactions associated with their specific order. This scenario validates the complete refund transaction search workflow including authentication, order ownership verification, filtering capabilities, and pagination.

The test begins by creating a buyer account and establishing authentication context. The buyer creates necessary order prerequisites: registering a delivery address, adding a payment method to their account, and preparing products for purchase. An admin creates a product category, a seller creates a product sale under that category, and the seller creates SKU variants for the product. The buyer adds these SKU variants to their shopping cart.

The buyer then creates an order by processing their cart items through checkout with payment processing. After order creation and delivery, the buyer submits one or more refund requests for the order. These refund requests are reviewed and approved by administrators, triggering the creation of refund transaction records that process the approved refunds through the payment provider.

Finally, the buyer retrieves the paginated list of refund transactions for their specific order using the search endpoint. The test validates various search and filtering capabilities including filtering by transaction status (processing, completed, failed), filtering by refund amount ranges (min_amount, max_amount), filtering by payment provider, filtering by date ranges (initiated_from, initiated_to, completed_from, completed_to), sorting options (by created_at, initiated_at, completed_at, refund_amount, status), and pagination parameters (page, limit, sort_order).

The test ensures that buyers can only access refund transactions for their own orders, that the search results are properly filtered and sorted according to the provided criteria, that pagination works correctly with appropriate page metadata, and that the response includes essential refund transaction information such as transaction IDs, amounts, status, timestamps, and payment processing details.

Edge cases to validate include searching for orders with no refund transactions (empty result set), searching with various filter combinations, verifying that refund transactions from other buyers' orders are not accessible, and ensuring that multi-seller order refund transactions are properly attributed and filtered.

Execute token refresh operation and verify that the refreshed session maintains the same buyer identity (same buyer ID), preserves session tracking information, and that the session record in shopping_mall_buyer_sessions is properly updated with the refresh activity. Validate that multiple consecutive refresh operations work correctly, each providing valid new tokens while maintaining session integrity and audit trail.

dependencies.purpose: Create new buyer account to establish initial authenticated session for testing session continuation through multiple refresh cycles

scenario.draft: Test successful seller account registration workflow with complete business information. Submit a registration request with all required fields including valid email, strong password, full name, phone number with country code, business name, business description, store name, and session tracking information (href and referrer). Validate that the registration succeeds and returns complete seller profile information along with JWT authentication tokens (access and refresh tokens). Verify that the created seller account has proper initial status (pending approval), email_verified is false, and that a corresponding session record is created in shopping_mall_seller_sessions. Confirm that the returned tokens can be used immediately for authenticated requests to seller endpoints.

Test seller registration behavior when attempting to register with an email address that is already in use by another seller account. First, create a seller account with a specific email address. Then attempt to register a second seller account using the same email address but with different business information. Verify that the duplicate registration is rejected with appropriate error response indicating that the email is already registered. Validate that the system properly enforces email uniqueness constraint across all seller accounts and prevents duplicate seller registrations.

Test seller registration behavior when attempting to use a store name that is already taken by another seller. First, create a seller account with a specific store name. Then attempt to register a second seller account using the same store name but with different email and business details. Verify that the system rejects the registration with appropriate error response indicating that the store name must be unique. Validate that store name uniqueness is enforced to ensure distinct brand identities across all sellers on the platform.

Test seller registration password validation requirements and security constraints. Attempt to register seller accounts with various password scenarios including: passwords shorter than minimum 8 characters, passwords meeting minimum length requirements, and passwords with various character combinations. Verify that weak passwords (those not meeting minimum 8 character requirement) are rejected with appropriate validation error messages. Confirm that passwords meeting security requirements are accepted and properly hashed server-side before storage. Validate that the plain text password is never stored and that the system enforces consistent password security practices.

Test seller registration with comprehensive business information validation. Submit registration requests with various combinations of business details to validate field requirements: test minimum and maximum length constraints for business_name (2-200 characters), business_description (up to 2000 characters), store_name (2-100 characters), and full_name (1-255 characters). Verify that phone numbers are validated against E.164 international format pattern. Confirm that all required business fields must be provided and that registration fails appropriately when required information is missing or doesn't meet format requirements. Validate that complete, valid business information is properly stored and returned in the authentication response.

Test that seller registration properly captures and records session tracking information for analytics and security auditing. Register a new seller account with explicit href (current page URL) and referrer (previous page URL) values, and optionally provide IP address. Verify that the registration succeeds and that session information is properly recorded in the shopping_mall_seller_sessions table. Validate that the session tracking data includes the connection URL (href), referrer URL, and IP address (whether client-provided or server-extracted). Confirm that this session tracking enables proper user journey analysis, marketing attribution, and security monitoring throughout the seller's platform usage.

Test the complete workflow of retrieving seller segments within a multi-seller order from the buyer's perspective. This scenario validates that when a buyer places an order containing items from multiple sellers, they can successfully query and retrieve the seller-specific portions of their order with proper filtering and pagination.

Workflow:
1. Authenticate as a buyer using join to create a new buyer account
2. Create a delivery address for order shipping
3. Register a payment method for checkout
4. Authenticate as admin to create product categories
5. Authenticate as first seller to create products
6. Create a product sale listing in a category
7. Create SKU variants for the product
8. Authenticate as second seller to create different products
9. Create another product sale in the same category
10. Create SKU variants for the second seller's product
11. Switch back to buyer context and add items from both sellers to cart
12. Create an order from the cart items (this will split into seller segments)
13. Retrieve seller segments using the patch endpoint with various filters

Validation points:
- Verify that the order contains multiple seller segments
- Validate that each seller segment has correct subtotal and shipping cost
- Confirm that filtering by seller_id returns only that seller's segment
- Test pagination with limit and page parameters
- Verify that status filtering works correctly
- Validate that search functionality works across seller names and tracking numbers
- Confirm that sorting by different fields (created_at, subtotal) works correctly
- Ensure response includes proper pagination metadata

This test validates the multi-seller order architecture where a single buyer order is split into independent seller fulfillment segments, each with its own status tracking, shipping details, and financial breakdowns.

Test that administrators can retrieve the complete audit trail of status transitions for a buyer's order. This scenario validates the search and filtering capabilities for order status history records from an admin perspective.

1. Create an admin account via join to establish administrative authentication context
2. Create a category to enable product listing
3. Create a seller account via join to establish seller authentication for product and SKU creation
4. Create a product sale listing assigned to the category
5. Create a SKU variant for the product to make it purchasable
6. Create a buyer account via join to establish buyer authentication context
7. Create a buyer delivery address for order shipping
8. Register a payment method for order payment processing
9. Add the product SKU to the buyer's shopping cart
10. Create an order from the cart items, triggering initial status history records
11. Switch back to admin authentication context
12. Search order status histories using the PATCH endpoint with various filter criteria

Validation points include:
- Successful retrieval of paginated status history records
- Correct filtering by status type (pending, confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded)
- Proper date range filtering using from_date and to_date parameters
- Accurate sorting by created_at or status fields in ascending/descending order
- Proper pagination with page and limit parameters
- Verification that all status transitions are captured with timestamps, actor information, and change reasons
- Confirmation that admin can view complete audit trail for any order regardless of seller or buyer
- Validation of response structure including pagination metadata and status history summary records

scenario.draft: Test advanced pagination and filtering capabilities for product sale snapshot retrieval. This scenario validates that sellers can efficiently navigate through potentially large snapshot histories using various filtering and pagination parameters. Create a complete test environment with seller, admin, category, and product sale. Then test multiple snapshot retrieval scenarios: pagination with different page sizes (limit parameter from 1 to 100), navigation through multiple pages (page parameter), filtering by product status at snapshot time to find snapshots where the product was in specific lifecycle states (draft, published, suspended), date range filtering using created_at_from and created_at_to to retrieve snapshots within specific time windows, and sorting control using the sort parameter for both ascending (created_at) and descending (-created_at) chronological order. Verify that pagination metadata accurately reflects the filtered result set, page boundaries are correctly enforced (requesting page beyond total pages returns empty results), limit parameter constrains response size properly, filtering parameters correctly narrow the result set, and combined filters work together properly (date range + status + pagination). Validate edge cases including empty result sets when no snapshots match filters, single-page results when total records are less than limit, and last page with partial results.

Test successful token refresh workflow using a valid refresh token. Perform login to obtain initial tokens, then immediately use the refresh token to request new access tokens. Verify that the refresh operation returns new valid JWT tokens (both access and refresh) with updated expiration timestamps, along with current seller profile information. Validate that the new access token works for authenticated requests and that refresh token rotation occurs (new refresh token issued).

Test token refresh behavior with an invalid or malformed refresh token. Attempt to refresh tokens using a completely invalid refresh token string that doesn't correspond to any session. scenario.draft:
Test the complete order cancellation workflow where a buyer submits a cancellation request for their order. This scenario validates:

1. Buyer authentication and order creation workflow - The buyer must first register/login, add a delivery address, register a payment method, add items to cart, and successfully place an order before requesting cancellation.

2. Cancellation request creation - The buyer submits a cancellation request specifying the order ID, a valid cancellation reason (e.g., 'buyer_changed_mind'), and optionally a detailed explanation.

3. Request validation - The system validates that the order exists, belongs to the authenticated buyer, and is in a cancellable state.

4. Initial status setting - The cancellation request is created with approval_status 'pending' awaiting admin or seller review.

5. Response validation - The created cancellation request includes all required fields (id, shopping_mall_order_id, cancellation_reason, approval_status, requested_at timestamps) and the buyer identity is correctly populated from the JWT token.

6. Business rule enforcement - The system ensures buyers can only cancel their own orders and cannot create cancellation requests for orders belonging to other buyers.

This test validates the buyer's ability to initiate the order cancellation workflow and ensures proper request creation with audit trail establishment.

scenario.draft:
Test the partial order cancellation workflow where a buyer cancels only a specific seller's portion of a multi-seller order. This scenario validates:

1. Multi-seller order creation - The buyer places an order containing items from multiple sellers, creating a parent order with multiple seller sub-orders.

4. Granular cancellation control - The cancellation applies only to the specified seller's portion, while other sellers' portions continue normal fulfillment.

5. Request creation with seller context - The cancellation request is created with the seller segment reference, enabling targeted cancellation processing and partial refunds.

6. Business logic validation - The system ensures the partial cancellation amount calculation is based only on the items in the specified seller segment, not the entire order total.

This test validates the marketplace's ability to handle partial cancellations in multi-seller order scenarios, ensuring granular control over order lifecycle management.

scenario.draft:
Test the admin approval workflow for buyer-initiated order cancellation requests. This scenario validates:

1. Complete order and cancellation setup - A buyer creates an order and submits a cancellation request that enters 'pending' status awaiting admin review.

2. Admin authentication and authorization - An admin user authenticates and accesses the cancellation request for review.

3. Approval decision - The admin updates the cancellation request with approval_status set to 'admin_approved', indicating the cancellation is granted.

4. Refund amount specification - The admin optionally specifies the refund_amount that should be returned to the buyer, which may differ from the original order amount due to restocking fees or partial refunds.

5. Audit trail creation - The system records the approving admin's identity (from JWT token) in approved_by_admin_id field and sets the approved_at timestamp.

6. Status transition validation - The cancellation transitions from 'pending' to 'admin_approved', triggering downstream refund processing and inventory restoration workflows.

7. Authorization enforcement - The operation is restricted to admin actors only, ensuring buyers and sellers cannot directly approve cancellation requests.

This test validates the admin's ability to review and approve cancellation requests with proper audit trail and refund amount tracking.

scenario.draft:
Test the refund amount specification workflow during cancellation approval. This scenario validates:

1. Order creation with known totals - A buyer places an order with specific item costs, shipping, and taxes, establishing the baseline order total.

2. Cancellation request submission - The buyer submits a cancellation request for the order.

3. Admin review with refund calculation - The admin reviews the cancellation and calculates the appropriate refund amount, which may differ from the original order total due to:

   - Payment processing fees that cannot be refunded
   - Partial refunds for multi-item orders
   - Promotional discount adjustments

4. Refund amount specification - The admin approves the cancellation and explicitly sets the refund_amount field to the calculated refund value.

5. Financial transparency - The refund amount is recorded in the cancellation record, providing clear documentation of the actual amount returned to the buyer.

6. Audit and reconciliation - The refund_amount enables financial reporting, reconciliation, and buyer communication about exact refund values.

This test validates the platform's ability to track and document refund amounts accurately during the cancellation approval process, supporting financial transparency and dispute resolution.

This scenario validates that admins can successfully remove product listings and all associated data including sale snapshots, variant attributes, variant values, SKUs, images, questions, and answers through hard deletion.

Business logic validations:
- Admin authorization is required for deletion operations
- Sale code must match an existing sale record
- Deletion is permanent and irreversible (hard delete)
- All related subsidiary data is cascade deleted
- Operation maintains referential integrity

This test ensures the administrative capability to remove product listings works correctly and that the cascade deletion properly cleans up all associated data without leaving orphaned records in the system.

scenario.draft:
Test that deleting a product sale properly performs cascade deletion of all related subsidiary data. This scenario validates the comprehensive cleanup of variant attributes, variant values, SKUs, images, questions, and answers when a sale is deleted.

Workflow steps:
1. Admin authenticates and creates a category
2. Seller authenticates and creates a comprehensive product sale with multiple related entities
3. Seller adds variant attributes to the sale (e.g., Color, Size)
4. Seller adds variant values to the attributes (e.g., Red, Blue for Color)
5. Seller creates SKUs representing specific variant combinations
6. Seller uploads product images
7. Admin deletes the sale listing
8. Verify all cascade-deleted data is properly removed from the system

Business logic validations:
- Sale deletion triggers cascade to variant attributes
- Variant attribute deletion cascades to variant values
- Sale deletion removes all associated SKUs
- Product images are deleted with the sale
- Customer questions and seller answers are removed
- No orphaned records remain after deletion
- Database referential integrity is maintained

This test ensures the hard deletion mechanism properly cleans up the entire product data hierarchy without leaving inconsistent state or orphaned subsidiary records.

- Sort order (asc/desc) is properly applied
- Default sorting uses display_order when not specified

scenario.draft:
Test that buyers can retrieve detailed information about a specific order item within their own order. This scenario validates the complete order item retrieval workflow from order creation to detailed item access.

The test establishes the complete order context by: (1) authenticating as buyer, (2) creating delivery address, (3) registering payment method, (4) adding a product SKU to cart (which requires prior category, sale, and SKU creation), (5) creating an order from cart items.

The test validates that: the response contains complete order item details including product_name, sku_code, variant_attributes (JSON string), quantity, unit_price, line_total, discount_amount, timestamps (created_at, updated_at), the item includes SKU summary information with variant details, the buyer can only access items from their own orders, and all captured purchase-time data is preserved accurately.

The test also verifies that the item's pricing and product information reflect the state at the time of purchase, even if the current product catalog has changed.

scenario.draft:
Test that platform administrators can search and retrieve seller-specific order segments within a multi-seller order with comprehensive filtering capabilities. This scenario validates the complete workflow from order creation through seller segment querying.

The test begins by creating necessary prerequisite data: an admin account for authentication, a category for product organization, a seller account to list products, a product sale listing, a product SKU variant, a buyer account for purchasing, a delivery address, a payment method, and cart items. The buyer then creates an order from the cart items, which triggers the system to split the order into seller-specific segments.

Once the order exists with seller segments, the admin authenticates and searches for seller segments within that specific order using the PATCH endpoint. The search request can include various filters such as seller_id, status, min_subtotal, max_subtotal, shipping_method, tracking_number, carrier_name, shipped_after, shipped_before, delivered_after, delivered_before, along with pagination parameters (page, limit) and sorting options (sort_by, sort_order).

The test validates that:
- The response returns a paginated list of seller segment summaries matching the search criteria
- Pagination metadata correctly reflects the current page, limit, total records, and total pages
- Each seller segment summary includes essential information: id, sub_order_number, status, seller summary, subtotal, shipping_cost, shipping_method, tracking_number, carrier_name, shipped_at, delivered_at, created_at, updated_at
- Filtering by seller_id returns only segments belonging to that specific seller
- Status filtering correctly filters segments by their fulfillment status (pending, confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled)
- Financial filters (min_subtotal, max_subtotal) correctly filter by monetary amounts
- Shipping method filter returns only segments using the specified method
- Date range filters correctly filter by shipped_at and delivered_at timestamps
- Text search across seller names, store names, and tracking numbers works correctly
- Sorting by various fields (created_at, updated_at, subtotal, shipped_at, delivered_at) in both ascending and descending order works correctly
- Only authorized admins can access this endpoint
- The endpoint returns proper error responses for invalid order IDs or unauthorized access attempts

scenario.draft:
Test a complex multi-seller order scenario where a buyer's order contains items from multiple sellers, validating that each seller segment can be retrieved independently with correct item assignments and financial calculations.

This scenario creates a realistic multi-seller marketplace situation: multiple sellers each listing different products in various categories, a buyer adding items from different sellers to their cart, and placing a single order that gets split into multiple seller-specific segments. The test then retrieves each seller segment individually to verify correct order splitting and data isolation.

The test validates that:
- When an order contains items from multiple sellers, the system correctly creates separate seller segments (shopping_mall_order_sellers records)
- Each seller segment can be retrieved independently using the parent orderId and the specific sellerId
- Each seller segment contains only the items belonging to that specific seller
- Financial calculations are correctly partitioned: each seller's subtotal reflects only their items
- Shipping costs are calculated independently for each seller's portion
- Each seller segment has its own status tracking, allowing independent fulfillment workflows
- Each seller segment has its own shipping method, tracking number, and carrier information
- The sum of all seller segment subtotals equals the parent order's subtotal
- Item assignments are correct: no items appear in multiple seller segments
- Each seller segment's sub_order_number follows the correct format (ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN-S#)
- Buyers can track each seller's fulfillment progress independently
- The buyer can only access seller segments from their own orders, not from other buyers' orders

scenario.draft:
Test that authenticated sellers can retrieve a paginated list of reviews for their products with comprehensive filtering capabilities. This scenario validates the core review retrieval functionality including seller ownership validation, pagination, and various filter combinations.

Test workflow:
1. Register a new seller account via /auth/seller/join to establish seller authentication context
2. Create multiple product sales for the seller to have products with reviews
3. Create buyer accounts and place orders for the seller's products
4. Submit multiple product reviews with varying characteristics (different ratings, verified/unverified purchases, with/without images, anonymous/attributed)
5. Call the target endpoint PATCH /shoppingMall/seller/sellers/{sellerId}/reviews with the authenticated seller's token
6. Verify the response includes only reviews for products belonging to the authenticated seller
7. Test pagination by requesting different page numbers and page sizes
8. Test filtering by rating ranges using min_rating and max_rating parameters
9. Test filtering by verified_purchase_only flag to show only verified purchase reviews
10. Test filtering by date ranges using start_date and end_date parameters
11. Test sorting options (created_at, rating, helpfulness) with both ascending and descending order
12. Test filtering by has_seller_response to identify unanswered reviews
13. Test filtering by has_images to find reviews with customer photos
14. Validate that the response structure matches IPageIShoppingMallReview.ISummary with proper pagination metadata
15. Verify that review summary includes essential fields like star_rating, review_title, review_body, buyer information, sale information, verification status, and helpfulness metrics

Business validations:
- Sellers can only access reviews for their own products (security isolation)
- Pagination correctly handles large review datasets
- Filtering combinations work correctly together
- Response includes proper buyer and product context for each review
- Verified purchase badges are correctly indicated
- Review statistics (helpfulness votes, timestamps) are accurately populated

scenario.draft:
Test that seller review retrieval properly enforces cross-seller data isolation, ensuring sellers cannot access reviews for products belonging to other sellers.

Test workflow:
1. Register seller A via /auth/seller/join
2. Register seller B via /auth/seller/join

4. Create product sales for seller B
5. Create buyer accounts and submit reviews for both seller A's and seller B's products

11. Verify response does NOT contain any reviews for seller A's products
12. Attempt to access seller B's reviews using seller A's authentication token and seller B's sellerId in path parameter
13. Verify the system prevents unauthorized access (either by filtering results or returning authorization error)

Business validations:
- Each seller sees only reviews for their own products
- Cross-seller data leakage is prevented
- Path parameter sellerId is validated against authenticated seller's identity
- Security boundaries are properly enforced between competing merchants

scenario.draft:
Test the behavior when attempting to delete a seller account that has already been deleted, validating proper handling of idempotent deletion requests and soft delete state management. This scenario ensures the system handles repeated deletion attempts gracefully and maintains data integrity.

The test workflow begins with seller registration to create a new account and obtain authentication tokens. The seller then successfully deletes their account through the DELETE endpoint, setting the deleted_at timestamp. Subsequently, the test attempts to delete the same account again using the same authentication context to verify idempotent behavior.

Validation points include: (1) first deletion succeeds and sets deleted_at timestamp appropriately, (2) second deletion attempt either succeeds idempotently (returning the already-deleted account state) or returns an appropriate error indicating the account is already deleted, (3) deleted_at timestamp remains unchanged by the second deletion attempt, (4) no data corruption or unintended side effects from repeated deletion, (5) consistent response structure for both deletion attempts.

Business rules to verify: soft delete implementation preserves the deleted_at timestamp across multiple deletion attempts, the operation is idempotent or clearly indicates the account is already in deleted state, and historical data integrity is maintained regardless of repeated deletion requests.

Edge cases to consider: attempting deletion immediately after first deletion (minimal time gap), attempting deletion with expired authentication tokens after account deletion, and verifying that the deleted account cannot be used for login or other operations between the two deletion attempts.

scenario.draft:
Test that the seller session search endpoint properly enforces authorization boundaries, ensuring sellers can only access their own session data and cannot view sessions belonging to other sellers. This validates critical security isolation between seller accounts.

The test workflow creates two independent seller accounts (Seller A and Seller B) through separate registration flows, each obtaining their own authentication tokens. Each seller establishes one or more authentication sessions. Then, using Seller A's authentication token, the test attempts to query sessions by providing Seller B's seller ID in the path parameter.

Validation points include: (1) successful creation of two independent seller accounts with separate authentication contexts, (2) each seller can successfully query their own sessions when using matching JWT token and sellerId path parameter, (3) authorization failure when Seller A attempts to access Seller B's sessions by providing Seller B's ID in the path, (4) appropriate HTTP error response (403 Forbidden or 401 Unauthorized) indicating authorization violation, (5) error message clearly communicates the authorization boundary violation, (6) no data leakage about Seller B's sessions in error responses.

Business rules to verify: JWT token validation extracts the authenticated seller's ID and compares it against the sellerId path parameter, mismatches must be rejected before any session data is retrieved, and sellers are strictly isolated to their own authentication session data for privacy and security.

Security considerations: this test validates a critical security boundary preventing cross-account session data access, ensures proper JWT token validation and path parameter verification, confirms that session data is considered sensitive and protected from unauthorized viewing, and verifies that path parameter manipulation cannot bypass authentication controls to access other sellers' session histories.

scenario.draft:
Test the seller session search behavior when filters produce no matching results, validating proper handling of empty result sets with correct pagination metadata. This ensures the API gracefully handles queries that match no sessions.

The test workflow creates a new seller account and establishes an initial authentication session. The seller then queries their session history using filter criteria guaranteed to match no sessions, such as filtering by a non-existent IP address, filtering by date ranges before the account was created, or searching for text that doesn't appear in any session data.

Validation points include: (1) successful response with HTTP 200 status even when no results match, (2) empty data array in the response body, (3) correct pagination metadata with records count of 0, pages count of 0, and current page handling, (4) response structure still conforms to IPageIShoppingMallSellerSession.ISummary schema, (5) consistent behavior across different filter types that produce empty results.

Business rules to verify: empty result sets are a valid response condition rather than an error, pagination metadata accurately reflects zero results, and clients can distinguish between empty results due to filters versus authorization failures.

Empty result scenarios: filtering by IP address that never authenticated, filtering by date range entirely in the future or before account creation, searching for random text that doesn't appear in any session fields, filtering by referrer URLs that were never used, and combining multiple filters that have no intersection in the session data.

Edge cases: empty results on page 1 versus requesting page 2 when there are zero results total, handling of limit parameter when there are no results to limit, and verifying sort parameters don't cause errors even when there are no results to sort.

scenario.draft: Test the basic product sales search functionality with pagination parameters. Verify that the endpoint returns a properly paginated list of published products when called without authentication. Test with various page sizes (limit parameter) and page numbers to ensure pagination metadata is accurate. Validate that the response includes the correct pagination object with current page, limit, total records, and total pages. Verify that product summaries contain all required fields including id, code, title, status, condition, price, seller information, and category information. Test edge cases like requesting page beyond available pages, minimum and maximum limit values, and default pagination behavior when parameters are omitted.

Test comprehensive filtering capabilities of the product sales search endpoint. Validate search functionality by partial product name matching with various query strings including single words, multi-word queries, and minimum length constraints. Test category filtering by creating products in different categories and filtering by category_id to ensure only products from the specified category are returned. Test price range filtering using min_price and max_price parameters individually and in combination. Validate status filtering to ensure draft, pending_approval, and other non-published products are excluded from unauthenticated searches while published products are returned. Test condition filtering (new, refurbished, used) to verify products are correctly filtered by their condition. Test brand filtering with exact brand name matching. Verify that multiple filters combine with AND semantics. Test stock availability filtering using has_stock parameter to ensure only in-stock products are returned when enabled.

Test all sorting options for product sales search to verify correct result ordering. Test sorting by created_at (default) to ensure newest products appear first. Test price_asc sorting to verify products are ordered from lowest to highest price based on minimum SKU price. Test price_desc sorting to verify products are ordered from highest to lowest price. Test title_asc sorting for alphabetical ordering A-Z. Test title_desc sorting for reverse alphabetical ordering Z-A. Verify that sorting works correctly in combination with filters and pagination. Test that the sort_by parameter defaults to created_at when not specified. Validate that sorting respects pagination boundaries and returns correctly ordered results across multiple pages.

Test product sales search behavior when no products match the search criteria. Verify that the endpoint returns an empty data array when filters exclude all products. Test scenarios like searching for non-existent product names, filtering by categories with no products, price ranges with no matching products, and brands that don't exist. Validate that pagination metadata correctly reflects zero results with records=0 and pages=0. Ensure the response structure remains valid even with empty results. Test that combining restrictive filters that exclude all products returns a properly formatted empty response without errors.

Test seller-specific product filtering functionality. Create products from multiple different sellers and verify that filtering by seller_id returns only products belonging to the specified seller. Test that the seller_id filter works correctly with UUID format validation. Verify that combining seller_id filter with other filters like category, price range, and status correctly narrows results. Test filtering by non-existent seller_id to ensure empty results are returned. Validate that seller summary information in the response matches the filtered seller. Test seller filtering across pagination to ensure all pages contain only products from the specified seller.

Test complex scenarios combining multiple search criteria simultaneously. Verify that combining search text, category filter, price range, status, condition, brand, seller filter, stock availability, and sorting works correctly with AND semantics. Test realistic buyer scenarios like searching for 'laptop' in Electronics category with price range $500-$1500, condition 'new', with stock available, sorted by price ascending. Validate that each filter correctly narrows the result set and that pagination metadata accurately reflects the filtered count. Test various combinations to ensure filters don't conflict and that the most restrictive combination of filters is properly applied. Verify that response data matches all specified criteria.

Test price filtering with boundary conditions and edge cases. Verify that min_price=0 includes all products. Test that products with price exactly equal to min_price are included. Test that products with price exactly equal to max_price are included. Verify that max_price filter excludes products priced above the threshold. Test price range where min_price equals max_price to find products at exact price point. Test invalid scenarios like min_price greater than max_price. Test price filtering with decimal values to ensure proper precision handling. Verify that price comparisons use the minimum SKU price across all product variants correctly.

Test pagination edge cases and boundary conditions. Verify that page=1 returns the first set of results. Test requesting page number beyond total available pages to ensure graceful handling. Test limit parameter at minimum boundary (limit=1) and maximum boundary (limit=100). Verify that invalid limit values outside the 1-100 range are handled appropriately. Test that pagination metadata correctly calculates total pages with various record counts and page sizes. Verify that requesting the last page returns the correct number of remaining records (which may be less than limit). Test pagination consistency by verifying that iterating through all pages returns all matching products exactly once without duplicates or gaps.

Test search text query validation and behavior. Verify that search queries with minimum length of 2 characters work correctly. Test that queries shorter than 2 characters are handled appropriately. Test case-insensitive searching to ensure 'Laptop', 'laptop', and 'LAPTOP' return the same results. Verify partial matching works correctly by searching for substrings of product titles. Test multi-word search queries with implicit AND semantics to ensure all words must match. Test special characters and Unicode characters in search queries. Verify that search works correctly when combined with other filters. Test searching with leading/trailing whitespace to ensure proper trimming or handling.

Test category filtering behavior to verify it only returns products directly assigned to the specified category and does not include products from child categories (non-recursive filtering). Create a category hierarchy with parent and child categories. Assign products to both parent and child categories. Filter by parent category_id and verify that only products directly assigned to the parent are returned, excluding products in child categories. Filter by child category_id and verify only products in that specific child category are returned. Test filtering by non-existent category_id to ensure empty results. Verify that category summary information in responses matches the product's assigned category.

Test product status filtering and visibility rules for unauthenticated access. Verify that only products with status='published' are visible in unauthenticated searches by default. Create products with various statuses (draft, pending_approval, published, suspended, archived). Perform search without authentication and verify only published products appear in results. Test that explicit status filter for published works correctly. Verify that attempting to filter by other statuses like draft or suspended returns empty results or only published products when unauthenticated. Test that suspended and archived products are excluded from public searches even if they match other filter criteria.

Test that product summary data in search results contains all required fields with correct values. Verify that each product summary includes id (UUID format), code (unique business identifier), title (product name), status (published), condition (new/refurbished/used), brand (string or null), short_description (string or null), price (minimum SKU price as number), thumbnail_url (URI or null), return_policy_days (integer), warranty_info (string or null), created_at (ISO datetime), updated_at (ISO datetime), deleted_at (null for active products), seller summary object with all required seller fields, and category summary object with all required category fields. Test that computed fields like price and thumbnail_url are correctly derived from SKU and image relationships. Verify data type correctness for all fields.

Test the has_stock filtering parameter to verify stock-based product visibility. Create products with various stock scenarios: products with multiple SKUs all in stock, products with some SKUs in stock and some out of stock, and products with all SKUs out of stock. Test has_stock=true filter to verify it returns only products having at least one SKU with available inventory. Test has_stock=false or omitted to verify all products are returned regardless of stock status. Verify that the stock check correctly examines inventory levels across all SKU variants for each product. Test stock filtering in combination with other filters to ensure correct AND semantics.

import { HttpException } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Prisma } from "@prisma/sdk";
import jwt from "jsonwebtoken";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";
import { v4 } from "uuid";
import { MyGlobal } from "../MyGlobal";
import { PasswordUtil } from "../utils/PasswordUtil";
import { toISOStringSafe } from "../utils/toISOStringSafe";

import { IShoppingMallRefundRequest } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallRefundRequest";
import { IShoppingMallOrder } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallOrder";
import { IShoppingMallBuyer } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallBuyer";
import { IShoppingMallAdmin } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallAdmin";
import { AdminPayload } from "../decorators/payload/AdminPayload";

export async function getShoppingMallAdminRefundRequestsRefundRequestId(props: {
  admin: AdminPayload;
  refundRequestId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;
}): Promise<IShoppingMallRefundRequest> {
  const refundRequest =
    await MyGlobal.prisma.shopping_mall_refund_requests.findUnique({
      where: {
        id: props.refundRequestId,
      },
      include: {
        order: true,
        buyer: true,
        reviewedByAdmin: true,
      },
    });

  if (!refundRequest) {
    throw new HttpException("Refund request not found", 404);
  }

  return {
    id: refundRequest.id,
    shopping_mall_order_id: refundRequest.shopping_mall_order_id,
    shopping_mall_order_seller_id:
      refundRequest.shopping_mall_order_seller_id ?? undefined,
    shopping_mall_buyer_id: refundRequest.shopping_mall_buyer_id,
    refund_request_number: refundRequest.refund_request_number,
    refund_reason: refundRequest.refund_reason,
    refund_explanation: refundRequest.refund_explanation,
    requested_amount: refundRequest.requested_amount,
    status: refundRequest.status as
      | "requested"
      | "under_review"
      | "information_requested"
      | "approved"
      | "processing"
      | "completed"
      | "denied"
      | "cancelled",
    admin_decision: refundRequest.admin_decision
      ? (refundRequest.admin_decision as
          | "approve_full"
          | "approve_partial"
          | "deny"
          | "escalate"
          | "pending")
      : undefined,
    admin_decision_notes: refundRequest.admin_decision_notes ?? undefined,
    approved_refund_amount: refundRequest.approved_refund_amount ?? undefined,
    return_required: refundRequest.return_required,
    return_tracking_number: refundRequest.return_tracking_number ?? undefined,
    return_received_at: refundRequest.return_received_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.return_received_at)
      : null,
    requested_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.requested_at),
    reviewed_at: refundRequest.reviewed_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.reviewed_at)
      : null,
    approved_at: refundRequest.approved_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.approved_at)
      : null,
    denied_at: refundRequest.denied_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.denied_at)
      : null,
    completed_at: refundRequest.completed_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.completed_at)
      : null,
    reviewed_by_admin_id: refundRequest.reviewed_by_admin_id ?? undefined,
    created_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.created_at),
    updated_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.updated_at),
    deleted_at: refundRequest.deleted_at
      ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.deleted_at)
      : null,
    order: {
      id: refundRequest.order.id,
      order_number: refundRequest.order.order_number,
      status: refundRequest.order.status,
      subtotal: refundRequest.order.subtotal,
      shipping_total: refundRequest.order.shipping_total,
      tax_total: refundRequest.order.tax_total,
      discount_total: refundRequest.order.discount_total,
      total_amount: refundRequest.order.total_amount,
      estimated_delivery_start: refundRequest.order.estimated_delivery_start
        ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.estimated_delivery_start)
        : undefined,
      estimated_delivery_end: refundRequest.order.estimated_delivery_end
        ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.estimated_delivery_end)
        : undefined,
      actual_delivery_at: refundRequest.order.actual_delivery_at
        ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.actual_delivery_at)
        : undefined,
      cancelled_at: refundRequest.order.cancelled_at
        ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.cancelled_at)
        : undefined,
      completed_at: refundRequest.order.completed_at
        ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.completed_at)
        : undefined,
      created_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.created_at),
      updated_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.order.updated_at),
    },
    buyer: {
      id: refundRequest.buyer.id,
      email: refundRequest.buyer.email,
      full_name: refundRequest.buyer.full_name,
      phone_number: refundRequest.buyer.phone_number ?? undefined,
    },
    reviewed_by_admin: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin
      ? {
          id: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.id,
          email: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.email,
          full_name: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.full_name,
          phone_number: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.phone_number,
          admin_level: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.admin_level as
            | "super_admin"
            | "moderator"
            | "support",
          email_verified: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.email_verified,
          created_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.created_at),
          updated_at: toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.updated_at),
          deleted_at: refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.deleted_at
            ? toISOStringSafe(refundRequest.reviewedByAdmin.deleted_at)
            : null,
        }
      : undefined,
  };
}

import { HttpException } from "@nestjs/common";
import { Prisma } from "@prisma/sdk";
import jwt from "jsonwebtoken";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";
import { v4 } from "uuid";
import { MyGlobal } from "../MyGlobal";
import { PasswordUtil } from "../utils/PasswordUtil";
import { toISOStringSafe } from "../utils/toISOStringSafe";

import { IShoppingMallRefundRequest } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallRefundRequest";
import { IShoppingMallOrder } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallOrder";
import { IShoppingMallBuyer } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallBuyer";
import { IShoppingMallAdmin } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IShoppingMallAdmin";
import { AdminPayload } from "../decorators/payload/AdminPayload";

export async function putShoppingMallAdminRefundRequestsRefundRequestId(props: {
  admin: AdminPayload;
  refundRequestId: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;
  body: IShoppingMallRefundRequest.IUpdate;
}): Promise<IShoppingMallRefundRequest> {
  const existing =
    await MyGlobal.prisma.shopping_mall_refund_requests.findUnique({
      where: { id: props.refundRequestId },
    });

  if (!existing || existing.deleted_at !== null) {
    throw new HttpException("Refund request not found", 404);
  }

  const now = new Date();
  const isApproved = props.body.status === "approved";
  const isDenied = props.body.status === "denied";

  const updated = await MyGlobal.prisma.shopping_mall_refund_requests.update({
    where: { id: props.refundRequestId },
    data: {
      status: props.body.status,
      ...(props.body.admin_decision !== undefined && {
        admin_decision: props.body.admin_decision,
      }),
      ...(props.body.admin_decision_notes !== undefined && {
        admin_decision_notes: props.body.admin_decision_notes,
      }),
      ...(props.body.approved_refund_amount !== undefined && {
        approved_refund_amount: props.body.approved_refund_amount,
      }),
      ...(props.body.return_required !== undefined && {
        return_required: props.body.return_required,
      }),
      ...(props.body.return_tracking_number !== undefined && {
        return_tracking_number: props.body.return_tracking_number,
      }),
      reviewed_by_admin_id: props.admin.id,
      reviewed_at: now,
      ...(isApproved && { approved_at: now }),
      ...(isDenied && { denied_at: now }),
      updated_at: now,
    },
    include: {
      order: true,
      buyer: true,
      reviewedByAdmin: true,
    },
  });

  return {
    id: updated.id,
    shopping_mall_order_id: updated.shopping_mall_order_id,
    shopping_mall_order_seller_id:
      updated.shopping_mall_order_seller_id === null
        ? null
        : updated.shopping_mall_order_seller_id,
    shopping_mall_buyer_id: updated.shopping_mall_buyer_id,
    refund_request_number: updated.refund_request_number,
    refund_reason: updated.refund_reason,
    refund_explanation: updated.refund_explanation,
    requested_amount: updated.requested_amount,
    status: updated.status as
      | "requested"
      | "under_review"
      | "information_requested"
      | "approved"
      | "processing"
      | "completed"
      | "denied"
      | "cancelled",
    admin_decision:
      updated.admin_decision === null
        ? null
        : (updated.admin_decision as
            | "approve_full"
            | "approve_partial"
            | "deny"
            | "escalate"
            | "pending"),
    admin_decision_notes:
      updated.admin_decision_notes === null
        ? null
        : updated.admin_decision_notes,
    approved_refund_amount:
      updated.approved_refund_amount === null
        ? null
        : updated.approved_refund_amount,
    return_required: updated.return_required,
    return_tracking_number:
      updated.return_tracking_number === null
        ? null
        : updated.return_tracking_number,
    return_received_at:
      updated.return_received_at === null
        ? null
        : toISOStringSafe(updated.return_received_at),
    requested_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.requested_at),
    reviewed_at:
      updated.reviewed_at === null
        ? null
        : toISOStringSafe(updated.reviewed_at),
    approved_at:
      updated.approved_at === null
        ? null
        : toISOStringSafe(updated.approved_at),
    denied_at:
      updated.denied_at === null ? null : toISOStringSafe(updated.denied_at),
    completed_at:
      updated.completed_at === null
        ? null
        : toISOStringSafe(updated.completed_at),
    reviewed_by_admin_id:
      updated.reviewed_by_admin_id === null
        ? null
        : updated.reviewed_by_admin_id,
    created_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.created_at),
    updated_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.updated_at),
    deleted_at:
      updated.deleted_at === null ? null : toISOStringSafe(updated.deleted_at),
    order: {
      id: updated.order.id,
      order_number: updated.order.order_number,
      status: updated.order.status,
      subtotal: updated.order.subtotal,
      shipping_total: updated.order.shipping_total,
      tax_total: updated.order.tax_total,
      discount_total: updated.order.discount_total,
      total_amount: updated.order.total_amount,
      estimated_delivery_start:
        updated.order.estimated_delivery_start === null
          ? null
          : toISOStringSafe(updated.order.estimated_delivery_start),
      estimated_delivery_end:
        updated.order.estimated_delivery_end === null
          ? null
          : toISOStringSafe(updated.order.estimated_delivery_end),
      actual_delivery_at:
        updated.order.actual_delivery_at === null
          ? null
          : toISOStringSafe(updated.order.actual_delivery_at),
      cancelled_at:
        updated.order.cancelled_at === null
          ? null
          : toISOStringSafe(updated.order.cancelled_at),
      completed_at:
        updated.order.completed_at === null
          ? null
          : toISOStringSafe(updated.order.completed_at),
      created_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.order.created_at),
      updated_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.order.updated_at),
    },
    buyer: {
      id: updated.buyer.id,
      email: updated.buyer.email,
      full_name: updated.buyer.full_name,
      phone_number:
        updated.buyer.phone_number === null ? null : updated.buyer.phone_number,
    },
    reviewed_by_admin: updated.reviewedByAdmin
      ? {
          id: updated.reviewedByAdmin.id,
          email: updated.reviewedByAdmin.email,
          full_name: updated.reviewedByAdmin.full_name,
          phone_number: updated.reviewedByAdmin.phone_number,
          admin_level: updated.reviewedByAdmin.admin_level as
            | "super_admin"
            | "moderator"
            | "support",
          email_verified: updated.reviewedByAdmin.email_verified,
          created_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.reviewedByAdmin.created_at),
          updated_at: toISOStringSafe(updated.reviewedByAdmin.updated_at),
          deleted_at:
            updated.reviewedByAdmin.deleted_at === null
              ? null
              : toISOStringSafe(updated.reviewedByAdmin.deleted_at),
        }
      : null,
  };
}
